src/core/output.ts.what: Output envelope and emitters for the ui binary: JSON envelope type, CommandResult, the result builders (ok, errText, errJson, okJson, internalErr...) and forTerminal(), which turns an author-controlled string into one escaped, length-capped line.
src/core/output.ts.why: Commands return a CommandResult and never touch streams, so handlers stay pure and testable. forTerminal exists because stdout is a machine channel an agent parses: a value taken from an artifact (a class name, a stylesheet href) printed verbatim could forge an output line or repaint the terminal.
src/core/output.ts.gotcha: forTerminal escapes every C0/C1 control char and marks truncation with an ellipsis. It is not HTML-escaping or quoting, so it is not safe for any other output context.

src/core/cli-args.ts.what: Hand-rolled argv parser for ui. Returns command, subcommand, positionals, a flags map, help/version/json booleans and the repeatedFlags set.
src/core/cli-args.ts.why: Zero dependencies and deterministic. isValueToken decides whether `--key next` takes next as its value: negative numbers and bare `-` are values, while `--x`, `-h` and `-v` are flags.
src/core/cli-args.ts.gotcha: flags keeps only the last value of a repeated flag. A repeat is recorded in repeatedFlags, so a command that needs every value must check that set. An unknown short flag such as `-x` is stored as a flag named `x` and not rejected here; flag-guard.ts does the rejecting.

src/core/flag-guard.ts.what: Rejects unknown long flags for a (sub)command. help, version and json are always allowed. Suggests the nearest declared flag by Levenshtein distance when it is within max(2, len/2).
src/core/flag-guard.ts.why: The lenient parser silently swallowed misspelled flags: `--brand-color` was dropped and the command still exited 0. A host model forming commands from prose is the likeliest caller to make that mistake.
src/core/flag-guard.ts.gotcha: Reports only the first unknown flag, in key order. Each command must call findUnknownFlag with its own list of accepted flags, so a new flag that is not registered there is rejected.

src/core/token-model.ts.what: DTCG token-file types, parser and validator. The public shape is category to {tokenName: Token}. Nested groups are flattened into one name joined by "-". Checks each leaf for a known $type and a $value. Does not resolve aliases.
src/core/token-model.ts.why: Persona starting_tokens nest into sub-groups, such as font.family.body. Flattening keeps every consumer two-tier, and the joined names match the dot-to-dash rule token-emit uses for CSS custom properties.
src/core/token-model.ts.gotcha: Two source paths can flatten to the same name (family.body and family-body). The parser throws BAD_TOKEN on the collision instead of overwriting. Alias resolution lives in token-resolve.ts.

src/core/ds-manifest.ts.what: The ds.manifest.json schema: types, hand-rolled validation (additionalProperties:false at root, persona and changelog entries), canonical JSON and SHA-256 hashing, load and save, and newManifest/appendChangelog.
src/core/ds-manifest.ts.why: Hash verification of tokens and registry only works if every writer produces the same bytes. canonicalStringify is declared the single writer, so a reseal never produces a false DS_TAMPERED.
src/core/ds-manifest.ts.gotcha: Writers must call canonicalStringify, never JSON.stringify. sortedKeysReplacer uses defineProperty so a "__proto__" key survives. Validation rejects unknown keys at every level, so a new manifest field needs a schema change here first.

src/core/design-system.ts.what: In-memory design-system model. Discovers design/ds.manifest.json by walking up at most 5 levels (stopping at .git), loads tokens, registry and manifest, verifies hashes, parses and resolves tokens. Also picks the registry file path via registryFileForDir.
src/core/design-system.ts.why: The only module that reads all three artifacts together and checks that they agree. A hash mismatch is DS_TAMPERED, and the message points the user at the sanctioned commands instead of a manual edit.
src/core/design-system.ts.gotcha: When a foreign component-registry.json occupies the default name, the kernel uses figma-component-registry.json and sets foreignRegistryAtDefaultPath. It never touches the foreign file. allowUnsealed tolerates hash drift only, reported on unsealedDrift.

src/core/registry-store.ts.what: Component registry: record types, hand-rolled validation (names must be Category/Variant PascalCase unless source-authored), load and save, and pure register, lookup and list operations. saveRegistry writes shards, then the contract file, sorted by name.
src/core/registry-store.ts.why: The output is deterministic because records are sorted before writing. Shards land first, so a failed write aborts before the contract file changes. figmaNode pointers are checked against path traversal because the registry is committed, shared input.
src/core/registry-store.ts.gotcha: loadRegistry backfills scope "local" on read for records written before the field existed. Validation rejects unknown keys with BAD_REGISTRY, so adding a field means updating COMPONENT_ALLOWED_KEYS too.

src/core/memory-store.ts.what: Filesystem boundary for project memory: an append-only ledger (design/memory.events.jsonl), a disposable count cache, a compiled graph cache keyed by a hash of the ledger bytes, and user-scope project registry and taste profile under ~/.ease-design (or EASE_DESIGN_HOME).
src/core/memory-store.ts.why: The ledger is the source of truth; the graph and counter are disposable views that can be rebuilt. Appends serialise through a mkdir lock with a bounded 100 ms wait, so two writers cannot allocate the same event id.
src/core/memory-store.ts.gotcha: If a process dies between taking the lock and releasing it, design/memory.events.lock stays behind and later appends fail with MEMORY_LOCKED. The code never breaks a lock on its own. Graph cache validity is checked against raw bytes, not mtime.

src/core/taste-lint.ts.what: Deterministic taste linter: about two dozen pure regex and string check functions, a few of them grouped over HTML, each mapped to one rubric axis. Findings are sorted by axis, then line. Severity is error (fails the exit code) or warning (report only).
src/core/taste-lint.ts.why: It gives the model self-critique gate a binary floor the model cannot argue its way past. Subjective axes are left to the model.
src/core/taste-lint.ts.gotcha: Comments are blanked before any check, so commented-out markup cannot trigger a finding. Only errorCount sets the exit code. knownHexes is optional: without a design-system context the raw-hex check is skipped silently.

src/core/url-slug.ts.what: Derives a kebab-case folder slug from a URL: the hostname with www. stripped, and dots and slashes turned into dashes. Also validates a kebab-case override of up to 64 characters.
src/core/url-slug.ts.why: The docstring names the /ui:from-url output folder as its consumer. Only tests/url-slug.test.ts calls it: no production module in src/ or scripts/ imports deriveSlug.
src/core/url-slug.ts.gotcha: DEAD CANDIDATE: zero production callers. BUG (latent): dots and dashes map to the same character, so a-b.com and a.b.com both derive a-b-com (verified). Two different sites would silently share one output folder once this is wired in.

src/core/component-kit/responsive-lint.t.what: Responsive-story lint for kit components. A component passes if its markup has an @media (min-width: ...) rule, or a <!-- responsive-exempt: reason --> with a non-empty reason. Anything else is an error. Exports lintResponsive over a list of components.
src/core/component-kit/responsive-lint.t.why: The other floor linters look for hazards, and a component with no media query has none, so a missing responsive story passed every check. The file header says it is exercised at the seam in tests/component-kit.test.ts, not through a ui subcommand.
src/core/component-kit/responsive-lint.t.gotcha: DEAD CANDIDATE, UNWIRED: the only caller is tests/component-kit.test.ts. knowledge/mode-constraints.md presents this rule as enforced, but no production gate runs it. Confirm whether a gate should call it before treating this as dead code.

src/types/css-tree-subpaths.d.ts.what: Ambient type declarations for three css-tree subpath modules (parser, walker, generator), which have no types upstream. They reuse node types from the root css-tree package.
src/types/css-tree-subpaths.d.ts.why: The root css-tree entry loads a lexer that reads syntax data at runtime. That cannot be bundled, and it broke the relocatable binary, so the engine imports the subpaths directly.
src/types/css-tree-subpaths.d.ts.gotcha: Flagged as an orphan, which is a false positive: the consumer src/core/extractors/html/css-cascade.ts imports by module name, and an ambient declaration produces no import edge. Not dead. Keep it when reviewing orphans.

src/core/knowledge-lint.ts.what: Knowledge-core linter. An FS-free orchestrator that takes pre-read content and runs about 13 check families: index rows, persona drift, broken cross-links, stale benchmarks, provenance grammar, catalog drift, front matter, routing, capability and pilot receipts. Output is sorted errors first.
src/core/knowledge-lint.ts.why: Keeps the knowledge core consistent with its own conventions without any model call. The command layer owns all I/O, so the checks stay pure and testable.
src/core/knowledge-lint.ts.gotcha: capabilityCatalogJson: undefined skips that check family, while null reports the file as missing. The canvas and gradient catalogs treat absent as null. The skip and the missing-file report look similar in the output but mean different things.

src/core/ds-guidelines-model.ts.what: Pure types and helpers for the DS guidelines pack: rule entries with their source paths, text and block parts, file and pack shapes, plus hashedSlug, uniqueId, slug and the ordering helpers compareText and compareNumeric.
src/core/ds-guidelines-model.ts.why: A pack is generated markdown whose generated blocks are sealed by hash, so edits are detectable. Each rule keeps the paths of its sources, so every line can be traced back.
src/core/ds-guidelines-model.ts.gotcha: Ordering is deliberately code-unit (compareText) or a pinned-locale numeric compare, never a bare localeCompare, so the pack is byte-identical on every machine. A hashedSlug id depends only on its own evidence, so ids stay stable when other rules are added.

src/core/taste-checks-shared.ts.what: Shared string helpers for the taste checks: stripCommentsPreservingOffsets, blankDeadMarkup (scripts and comments blanked, offsets kept), cssRegions, a heuristic cssRules flattener, and selectorSubjectIsRoot.
src/core/taste-checks-shared.ts.why: One definition for every linter family, so a fix to comment handling reaches all of them.
src/core/taste-checks-shared.ts.gotcha: cssRules is a heuristic, not a CSS parser: it yields the inner rules of @media blocks and keyframe stops. selectorSubjectIsRoot does not recognise :is(body) or :where(html); the file states this limit.

src/core/tell-lint.ts.what: Runs the generated-UI tell family over one artifact's facts. Partitions rules by what the extractor can supply, derives roles, runs each rule, then dedupes and collapses repeated findings. Also adds the contrast and content families.
src/core/tell-lint.ts.why: Tells judge a habit, not a rubric breach. Because the rules read facts, the same set works for HTML, JSX, Swift and Dart. collapseRepeated turns 54 identical lines into one finding with a count and an example node.
src/core/tell-lint.ts.gotcha: Collapsing keys on checkId plus message, so separate nodes with an identical message merge into one line (the example nodeRef keeps one locator). Rules the extractor cannot supply are reported NOT-EVALUATED, never as passed.

src/commands/figma-reconcile-run.ts.what: The IO runner for `ui figma reconcile`. Handles --dry-run (default), --apply, --skip, --mirror-file and --file-slug. Reads the change log from a cursor, computes the delta against the registry, and on apply writes sidecars, then the registry, then the sync-state cursor.
src/commands/figma-reconcile-run.ts.why: The kernel stays pure: every file read and write and the cursor policy live here, and the live Figma scan never runs here. The write order means a pointer never outlives the file it names. The cursor only advances to the earliest target that is still blocked.
src/commands/figma-reconcile-run.ts.gotcha: One 742-line function holding several interacting cursors (global, byFile, byte hint). The subtle rules are documented inline: rebase on rotation, strict versus lenient matching of pending entries, and a rewind persisting byte 0. Read those comments before editing.

src/core/finding-schema.ts.what: FloorFinding schema v1, the single finding shape every gate family emits. Defines the three severity tiers (error, warning, advisory), the repair-scope and repair-target types, and the shared countBySeverity and failing helpers.
src/core/finding-schema.ts.why: The retry ladder, stuck detector and telemetry all key off this one shape, so it was ratified before any of them were built. Advisory exists so a sign can print without failing a build.
src/core/finding-schema.ts.gotcha: Never derive warningCount by subtracting errors from findings.length, because that silently counts advisory findings as warnings. The file records that thirteen call sites once did this. Use countBySeverity.

src/core/component-kit/index.ts.what: COMPONENT_KIT, the 27 stable component records (Button, Input, Card, Dialog, Table and others) that `ds init` registers into every fresh design system unless --bare is passed. Each record is set to scope "local" and sorted by name.
src/core/component-kit/index.ts.why: A fresh DS starts with a registry that the specimen check can pass with zero gaps. The header lists the four waves that built it. The scope default is injected here so the 27 source files stay scope-free.
src/core/component-kit/index.ts.gotcha: Adding a component means editing this array and the matching file. Registration runs validateComponentRecord, so a malformed kit record fails loudly at init, not later.

src/core/component-kit/kit-types.ts.what: KitComponent: a ComponentRecord with variants, description and status "stable" made required, so a half-authored kit component fails tsc.
src/core/component-kit/kit-types.ts.why: Every kit record must declare its full State matrix in variants. The narrow states enum cannot express Loading or Invalid, so State=... entries in variants are the source of truth for that matrix.
src/core/component-kit/kit-types.ts.gotcha: The type narrows only at compile time. Each record is still a plain ComponentRecord, so validateComponentRecord accepts it unchanged at runtime.

src/core/memory-events.ts.what: Typed vocabulary for the append-only design-memory ledger: 22 closed event types, the required data keys for each, provenance rules, and deterministic serialise and parse.
src/core/memory-events.ts.why: The ledger (design/memory.events.jsonl) is the single source of truth, and graphs and profiles are rebuildable views. A fixed key order means the same event always produces the same bytes.
src/core/memory-events.ts.gotcha: taste_vote and taste_veto differ by one character. A typo records a loudly wrong event, but `memory query --type` can silently return the other stream. Insights and outcome_recorded events must carry refs, or validation refuses them.

src/commands/tell-lint.ts.what: The `ui tell-lint` command. Resolves targets, runs the fact pass per file, optionally runs the rendered pass in a browser already on the machine, merges rendered findings back onto the right page, and prints what the engine saw and what it could not read.
src/commands/tell-lint.ts.why: A zero from a half-read project is not a clean result. Each file therefore reports its census (what was seen), its skips and unresolved sheets, and its NOT-EVALUATED rules, so a silent blind spot cannot pass as clean.
src/commands/tell-lint.ts.gotcha: Without --render the seven rendered rules are NOT-EVALUATED, never counted as passing. The browser comes from --browser, CHROME_PATH, or a platform default. Exit code 1 only on an error-severity finding; advisories never fail.

src/core/ds-guidelines-pack.ts.what: buildPack: assembles the DS guidelines pack (markdown files plus a manifest) from the sealed store, rulings, terminology, grammar, soul and seeded scenarios. Rebuilds keep every answer: answers merge by slot id, and any without a slot are parked in an orphans file.
src/core/ds-guidelines-pack.ts.why: It is deterministic (same inputs, same bytes) so the pack can be verified and diffed, and the clock is injected. Answers are never dropped, because a person wrote them.
src/core/ds-guidelines-pack.ts.gotcha: Rule ids must be unique across the pack, and a duplicate throws an internal error. Markdown the build did not produce is reported as stale and never deleted.

src/core/ds-kit-seal.ts.what: Integrity boundary for adopted kits. Validates the shape and hashes of kit.lock.json, verifies every bound file and both store projections (tokens and registry), and refuses ds init or import from replacing a bound kit (KIT_DOWNGRADE).
src/core/ds-kit-seal.ts.why: An adopted kit is a sealed contract. Its tokens, registry and evidence must still match what was verified, or the store has been tampered with.
src/core/ds-kit-seal.ts.gotcha: readBoundKit rebuilds the theme from the current tokens and compares it byte for byte, so any hand edit to the theme fails. A verified kit also needs its receipt content hash to match the lock revision.

src/core/layout-lint.ts.what: The static HTML layout linter. Runs 20 string and regex checks (3 error checks, then 17 warning checks) and returns the shared FloorFinding shape. Redirect stubs are skipped entirely.
src/core/layout-lint.ts.why: It catches structurally broken or layout-smelly HTML without a DOM or a browser. Comments are blanked first, so commented-out markup cannot trigger a check.
src/core/layout-lint.ts.gotcha: Heuristic by design: the header states that there is no DOM. Error checks run first, so errors always print before warnings. A redirect stub (no html or body) short-circuits to zero findings.

src/commands/ds-init-impl.ts.what: The `ui ds init` command. Validates name, persona, intent and brand hex, refuses to overwrite an existing DS without --force, expands the persona into a token skeleton, registers the component kit unless --bare, writes tokens, registry and manifest, and wires the soul and heartbeat fuel line.
src/commands/ds-init-impl.ts.why: One command produces a sealed, hashed design system plus the learning-loop files it needs.
src/commands/ds-init-impl.ts.gotcha: Without --force the manifest is written with exclusive create (flag wx), so a concurrent init fails rather than overwriting. With --force the prior changelog is kept. Kit registration happens here, not in expandPersona, which always returns an empty registry.

src/core/ds-kit-validate.ts.what: Validates an authored kit against its spec. prepareKit builds a list of findings covering undeclared content, the token inventory, the theme projection, case obligations, mappings, variant coverage, implementation exports and the minimum component count. validateKit throws unless the findings are empty, then validates the evidence and produces the verified lock.
src/core/ds-kit-validate.ts.why: A kit is sealed only after every source item maps to a component or to a reasoned disposition, and every captured variant has a bound case.
src/core/ds-kit-validate.ts.gotcha: Most checks append a finding and continue. Only the structural ones throw KitError, so callers must read the findings list rather than assume that no throw means success. A component that still carries a legacy figmaNode pointer fails with KIT_FIGMA_SIDECAR.

src/core/design-facts/extractor-registry.what: The roster of extractors (html-cascade, css-only, jsx-tailwind, sfc, swiftui, flutter, figma-nodes, rendered-cdp). Each declares the fact kinds it can supply and at what confidence, plus its file extensions and whether its output is an undercount.
src/core/design-facts/extractor-registry.why: A rule whose inputs an extractor cannot supply is reported NOT-EVALUATED, never silently passed. A polyglot linter needs this to avoid turning "I could not see it" into "it is clean".
src/core/design-facts/extractor-registry.gotcha: css-only supplies no structure or text, so layout-level rules never run on a bare stylesheet. That is by design. Extractors not yet built are declared but unreachable at runtime.

src/core/gate.ts.what: runGate: the single composed judge for an HTML artifact. Runs six families (layout, a11y, taste, tell, content, and an autofix dry-run) and returns one verdict. pass is true only when no family has an error. Skipped and partial families are reported separately.
src/core/gate.ts.why: Every consumer judges with one instrument, so a linter added here reaches all of them at once. The autofix family turns any pending repair into a failure without changing the file.
src/core/gate.ts.gotcha: The tell, content and contrast checks share one fact extraction, so they cannot disagree. A family that ran but could not read the whole page is listed under partial, so a clean verdict over half a page stays visible. The file sits in "Other core" but belongs with the quality gates.

src/commands/designmd-audit-impl.ts.what: `ui designmd audit`: reads a folder holding DESIGN.md and an optional tokens.json, runs five audit families (format, source-fidelity, ref-integrity, accessibility, discipline), and writes audit.md and audit.json into that folder. Exit 0 PASS, 1 FAIL, 2 WARN.
src/commands/designmd-audit-impl.ts.why: It gives a repeatable, file-level check of a design doc against its own tokens and references, with a machine-readable report next to it.
src/commands/designmd-audit-impl.ts.gotcha: Not read-only: it writes audit.md and audit.json into the folder it audits. Discipline reads every regular file under 5 MB as UTF-8, so a binary file is decoded as garbage text rather than skipped.

src/core/build-evidence-rules-shared.ts.what: Shared types and primitives for `ui evidence lint`: the RuleResult shape, the pass, fail and skip constructors, a recursive walkFiles that skips symlinks, and runEvidenceLint, which runs rules R1 to R8 over one evidence folder.
src/core/build-evidence-rules-shared.ts.why: Rule modules need one definition of a result and one file walk. The orchestrator reads the folder once, so every rule sees the same snapshot.
src/core/build-evidence-rules-shared.ts.gotcha: CIRCULAR IMPORT: this file imports the rule modules (shots, probe, gates, deviations, persuade), and each of those imports pass, fail and skip back from here. It works only because the helpers are called at run time, not at load time. Moving the primitives into their own file would remove the cycle.

src/core/init-stub.ts.what: Builds the ui init manifest (status stub or ready, runtime, adapters, template hashes, model adapter) and resolves the package roots (templates and knowledge) by walking up until it finds templates/workflows/generate.md.
src/core/init-stub.ts.why: Doctor, init, agents, delivery and knowledge-activate all need to locate the bundled templates and knowledge at runtime, so path resolution lives in one place.
src/core/init-stub.ts.gotcha: The name is misleading. "stub" is only the status of an early manifest. The file is live code used by at least six commands, not a placeholder, so removing it as a stub would break ui init and doctor.

src/core/token-resolve.ts.what: DTCG alias resolver. Flattens a token tree to literal values by following alias chains, detects cycles, dangling aliases and type mismatches, and checks composite members (typography, shadow) against the type each slot requires.
src/core/token-resolve.ts.why: Downstream consumers (emitters, the registry, checks) need literal values only. Resolving once here means they never see an alias.
src/core/token-resolve.ts.gotcha: A nested alias such as {color.text.primary} falls back to the flattened name color.text-primary that token-model produces. Cycle detection uses the resolved path, so a nested and a flattened spelling of the same target count as one node.

src/commands/ds-guidelines-check-collect.what: Reads a built guidelines pack and collects every finding for `ds guidelines check` and export. Lints each markdown file the manifest lists, checks slots and the answers store, flags orphaned answers and unlisted stale files, and reports a seal that no longer matches.
src/commands/ds-guidelines-check-collect.why: The check command gets one list of findings. Markdown the manifest does not list is reported as stale and is never linted or exported.
src/commands/ds-guidelines-check-collect.gotcha: If the manifest cannot be read, the linter falls back to every markdown file in the folder, and the completeness check reports the failure separately. A manifest that is readable but lists a file restricts linting to that list.

src/commands/ds-import-impl.ts.what: `ui ds import`: converts an existing flat token file into the DTCG store, annotates roles with recognizeRoles, seals a minimal manifest with an empty registry, and wires the soul and heartbeat fuel line.
src/commands/ds-import-impl.ts.why: Teams with an existing tokens.json can use the other ds commands (a11y, status, diff) without rebuilding the design system from a persona.
src/commands/ds-import-impl.ts.gotcha: --force alone refuses while the registry holds components (REGISTRY_NOT_EMPTY). --reset-registry is the explicit opt-in. The imported manifest uses the placeholder persona slug "imported".

src/core/delivery/delivery-shared-valida.what: Shared validation helpers for delivery artifacts: type guards (objectValue, nonEmptyString, stringArray, numberArray), a finding builder, requireBase (checks kind and version), and namedObjects.
src/core/delivery/delivery-shared-valida.why: Every delivery validator checks the same shapes, so the guards live in one place instead of being copied into each artifact.
src/core/delivery/delivery-shared-valida.gotcha: finding() defaults severity to error. requireBase throws a DeliveryError rather than returning a finding, so callers must catch it.

src/core/design-facts/fact-collector.ts.what: The append-only builder every extractor writes into. add() rejects a fact whose kind the extractor did not declare, whose provenance names another extractor, or whose confidence is stronger than declared. It also tallies unresolved reads and sorts facts for deterministic output.
src/core/design-facts/fact-collector.ts.why: Makes the extractor contract enforceable at collect time. A wrong fact is worse than a missing one, so the collector throws rather than recording it quietly.
src/core/design-facts/fact-collector.ts.gotcha: Any contract violation throws FactContractError, so an extractor bug fails the run instead of producing a quiet wrong finding. Unresolved reads are counted but not stored with a location, so they cannot be traced to a line.

src/core/design-facts/fact-model.ts.what: The one normalized fact model. Defines four confidence levels (rendered, resolved, literal, heuristic), the ten fact kinds, and the Provenance record every fact carries (file, line, extractor, confidence, nodeRef).
src/core/design-facts/fact-model.ts.why: Lets a rule written once judge HTML, JSX, Swift and Dart. Provenance is required on every fact, so any finding can be traced to a source line.
src/core/design-facts/fact-model.ts.gotcha: atLeast() compares confidence by array index, so the order of CONFIDENCE_ORDER is load-bearing. Reordering it silently changes which facts an extractor may claim.

src/commands/agents.ts.what: The `ui agents` command. init writes Claude Code subagent files under .claude/agents/ from three role templates, list shows the stamped agents and whether each is fresh, and check flags stale agents and unknown roles. Opt-in: init never runs automatically.
src/commands/agents.ts.why: Each agent name is fixed at generation time from the studio and project names, but the agent reads its identity at runtime, so editing the soul needs no regeneration.
src/commands/agents.ts.gotcha: init is all-or-nothing: it checks for existing files before writing, and it removes the files it wrote if a later write fails. Only files carrying a design-os stamp are checked, so hand-written agents are never flagged.

src/commands/ds-kit-impl.ts.what: The `ui ds kit` dispatcher with six operations: plan, theme, prepare, validate, adopt and verify. Each parses its own flags, then calls the matching core function. Failures return a structured findings payload.
src/commands/ds-kit-impl.ts.why: Puts the kit lifecycle behind one command. Read-only operations are kept apart from adopt, the one that writes.
src/commands/ds-kit-impl.ts.gotcha: Each operation accepts a different flag set (plan: source, kind, tokens, out, name; adopt: out, now; verify: dir). Any other flag is rejected with UNKNOWN_FLAG, and a repeated flag is refused.

src/core/ds-guidelines-slots.ts.what: Scenario slots (QUESTION lines) in a guidelines pack, and answer preservation. parseSlots marks each slot open, partial or filled (filled means Do, Don't and Why are all present). injectAnswers and renderOrphans carry answers across a rebuild.
src/core/ds-guidelines-slots.ts.why: The host writes the answers, never the binary. A rebuild must keep every answer, so one whose slot has disappeared is parked in the orphans file instead of being dropped.
src/core/ds-guidelines-slots.ts.gotcha: An answer runs until a blank line that is not followed by a Do, Don't or Why line. Prose written later in the file is not picked up as part of the answer, on purpose.

src/core/memory-autorecord.ts.what: The single write path for auto-recorded outcomes: a command that acts appends a memory event as a side effect of running. withOutcome wraps a command result. recordOutcome resolves the project that owns the artifact and appends. lintOutcomeData builds the shared payload for lint runs.
src/core/memory-autorecord.ts.why: One write path keeps the event ledger consistent. It only writes into projects that already have a design/ folder, so it never creates state in an arbitrary directory.
src/core/memory-autorecord.ts.gotcha: BUG (low): the header says it never throws, but recordOutcome re-throws any error from validateEvent that is not a MemoryEventError (line 125). A malformed input can therefore change a command's exit code.

src/core/tell-rules.ts.what: The rule engine for tell rules. indexFacts drops facts that are identical in every field and buckets the rest by kind. Also defines TellRule, the finding builder, and the owner helpers (sameOwner, nearestOwner) that decide whether two facts describe one element.
src/core/tell-rules.ts.why: Rules receive facts and never source text, which is what lets one rule cover several languages. Identical facts collapse first, so a rule that counts facts counts the page, not a repeated read.
src/core/tell-rules.ts.gotcha: Same-element matching uses an exact nodeRef when both facts have one, and otherwise a 4-line window (OWNER_LINE_WINDOW). The window is deliberately tight: widening it trades missed findings for false ones.

src/commands/knowledge.ts.what: The `ui knowledge` dispatcher with 11 subcommands (activate, check, index, lint, render, fresh, promote, draft-ruling, ledger, effect-matrix, gradient-matrix). It holds the help text, which is the public list of check and error codes. Each subcommand lives in its own module.
src/commands/knowledge.ts.why: Groups the knowledge-core governance tools under one command, so their codes and flags are documented in one place.
src/commands/knowledge.ts.gotcha: Only `index` is implemented in this file. The other subcommands are delegated to their own modules. index writes knowledge/index.json only when --emit is passed.

src/core/ds-kit-parse.ts.what: Strict parser for a kit spec and kit.json. Helpers (object, string, array, strings, choice) reject unknown keys, control characters and malformed values. parseKitSpec checks every top-level field, each source, case and mapping before anything else reads the file.
src/core/ds-kit-parse.ts.why: The kit spec is authored input from outside the repo, so the parser refuses anything outside the expected shape rather than guessing. readKitJson decodes with fatal UTF-8.
src/core/ds-kit-parse.ts.gotcha: parseKitSpec casts the object to KitSpec after checking only the listed fields. Reference integrity (for example, a mapping that names an unknown case) is checked later in ds-kit-validate.ts, not here.

src/core/extractors/html/html-extractor..what: The reference-fidelity extractor. Parses HTML, builds the cascade, and emits facts for each element: structure, text, colour, gradient, typography, spacing, radius, border, shadow and motion. It is the only extractor that reaches resolved confidence, and it sets degraded when the document will not parse.
src/core/extractors/html/html-extractor..why: Every other extractor is measured against this one. A page with utility classes and no stylesheet is not read as clean: each class is counted as an unresolved read.
src/core/extractors/html/html-extractor..gotcha: DEAD BRANCH: line 178 is a no-op ternary (`own === textOf(el) ? own : own`); both arms return own. The behaviour is correct, but the code implies the two cases were meant to differ. Remove the ternary or restore the intended second arm.

src/core/extractors/web/sfc-extractor.ts.what: Reader for Vue, Svelte and Astro single-file components, and for bare .css files. A component's <style> block is read as declarations, and its template goes through the JSX scanner. A bare stylesheet gives declarations only, with no structure or text.
src/core/extractors/web/sfc-extractor.ts.why: Splitting the file lets each half be read at the fidelity it can support: CSS declarations here, template markup through the JSX scanner.
src/core/extractors/web/sfc-extractor.ts.gotcha: BUG: the header says the <style> block goes "through the real cascade at resolved confidence". The code builds a cascade and throws it away (`void cascade`, line 71). Declarations come from a regex, yet they are still emitted at resolved confidence, so overridden or shadowed rules in the same block are reported as if they applied.

src/core/lint-file-by-extractor.ts.what: The single dispatch from an extractor id to its reader. Returns findings, NOT-EVALUATED rules, a census of what the reader saw, and any stylesheets it could not open. Shared by the tell-lint command and the field corpus, so both judge the same pipeline.
src/core/lint-file-by-extractor.ts.why: A copy of this dispatch would drift, and the corpus would then certify a pipeline that users never run. An id with no reader reports every rule NOT-EVALUATED, never a clean pass.
src/core/lint-file-by-extractor.ts.gotcha: BUG (silent gap): for every non-cascade reader (swiftui, flutter, jsx-tailwind, sfc, css-only), contrast is never checked, and notComputable is hard-coded to 0. Nothing in the output reports the skipped check, though the file's own rule is that gaps must be named.

src/core/product-context-value.ts.what: Validation helpers for the product-context atlas JSON: exact-key checks, scalar and identifier rules, digests, RFC 3339 timestamps, sorted string lists, counters, and a finding list that is deduplicated and sorted before output.
src/core/product-context-value.ts.why: The atlas is untrusted input, so every field is checked against a fixed shape. Fixed identifier and digest patterns keep the canonical output the same for the same input.
src/core/product-context-value.ts.gotcha: ascii() compares UTF-16 code units: deterministic, but not locale order. requireSortedStrings enforces that order, so an unsorted list is rejected rather than re-sorted.

src/commands/ds-guidelines-export-impl.t.what: `ui ds guidelines export --target figma`. Refuses unless the pack passes check with no open slot. Then builds the Figma bundle (optionally trimmed to a byte budget), refuses unexpected files in the bundle folder, and writes the bundle and UPLOAD.md together.
src/commands/ds-guidelines-export-impl.t.why: Figma enforces a hard size cap and the bundle is uploaded by hand, so the export refuses rather than send something oversized, unfinished or stale.
src/commands/ds-guidelines-export-impl.t.gotcha: A file in the bundle folder that this export does not produce stops the export (BUNDLE_DIR_NOT_CLEAN). It is never deleted, because it would be uploaded by mistake.

src/core/a11y-lint.ts.what: Static-HTML accessibility linter for the WCAG criteria that markup alone can decide: alt text, page language, title, positive tabindex, viewport zoom, unnamed icon controls, heading order, paste, unlabeled inputs and removed focus outlines. Findings are error, warning or advisory, and sorted.
src/core/a11y-lint.ts.why: Passing this is not the same as accessible, and the command says so. Criteria that need a rendered DOM or human judgement are left out on purpose.
src/core/a11y-lint.ts.gotcha: Precision over recall: each check flags only when it is sure. Advisories never fail a build. The file notes a runtime import cycle between this module and the a11y-checks barrel, and it imports two checks directly to avoid it.

src/core/ds-kit-types.ts.what: Shared types for the kit system: KitError, the spec (KitSpec, KitSource, KitCase, KitMapping), KitPreparation and KitLock. It also re-exports Registry.
src/core/ds-kit-types.ts.why: The kit parser, validator, seal and adoption modules share these shapes. Keeping them in one file avoids circular type imports.
src/core/ds-kit-types.ts.gotcha: KitError carries a structured details list. A caller that prints only the message drops the findings, so format the details too.

src/core/ds-reseal.ts.what: The single write path for sealed artifacts. reseal rewrites design.tokens.json and/or component-registry.json plus the manifest atomically, bumps the generation, rehashes what changed, and appends a changelog entry. It writes staging files first, then renames them, with the manifest last.
src/core/ds-reseal.ts.why: Every writer must go through here, so the hashes in the manifest always match the files. The manifest is written last, so a mid-commit failure leaves a hash mismatch that the next load detects.
src/core/ds-reseal.ts.gotcha: The commit is a sequence of renames, not one transaction. A failure partway through leaves the store partly committed, and the thrown error names the recovery step. For a bound kit, the lock is also rewritten, after the kit is re-read.

src/core/prompt-plan/validate-prompt-pla.what: The top-level validator for a prompt-plan artifact. Checks the identity block, then delegates to specialised validators for facets, product truth, directions, visual system, regions, proportions, delivery plan, preflight and the builder packet. Returns ready only when there are no errors.
src/core/prompt-plan/validate-prompt-pla.why: A prompt plan goes to a builder only once it is complete, so the readiness decision is made in one place.
src/core/prompt-plan/validate-prompt-pla.gotcha: warningCount is computed as findings.length - errorCount. That is safe today because PromptPlanSeverity has only error and warning. Adding a third severity would silently count it as a warning, the same arithmetic trap the finding-schema file warns about.

src/commands/product-context-flow.ts.what: The `ui product-context project-flow` command. Reads a size-capped product atlas file, parses and checks it, then prints the projected flow as canonical JSON, or prints the blocking findings on stderr.
src/commands/product-context-flow.ts.why: The flow projection is what a downstream builder reads, so the command emits it only when the atlas replays cleanly.
src/commands/product-context-flow.ts.gotcha: Malformed input (bad JSON, bad UTF-8, or a failed replay) returns BAD_PRODUCT_ATLAS before any projection runs. Non-replay exceptions are rethrown, not converted.

src/core/ds-kit-files.ts.what: Byte-level file boundary for kits. kitPath validates portable paths (no backslashes, absolute paths, or Windows reserved names). readKitFile refuses symlinks and wrong-case paths and reads with O_NOFOLLOW. verifyKitFiles checks byte hashes, and indexKitContent walks the candidate root and fails on any undeclared file.
src/core/ds-kit-files.ts.why: A kit is a portable candidate folder, so its paths must mean the same thing on every operating system. A file the spec does not declare must never enter the sealed content.
src/core/ds-kit-files.ts.gotcha: readKitFile checks each path segment by listing its directory, which is case-sensitive, so a wrong-case name fails even on a case-insensitive disk. Reserved trees (evidence, design, dist, node_modules) are skipped by the walk and cannot be declared as content.

src/core/ds-kit-theme.ts.what: Turns a kit's tokens into an owner theme CSS file: a :root block and one [data-ds-mode] block per mode, plus alias lines that map Tailwind-style names (--color-*, --radius-*) onto token variables. Every value is checked for safe CSS before the file is produced.
src/core/ds-kit-theme.ts.why: The host writes this CSS to the candidate's declared theme path, so unsafe or ambiguous values must be refused, not escaped. The theme is a deterministic function of the tokens, which the seal re-checks.
src/core/ds-kit-theme.ts.gotcha: safeCssText refuses braces, semicolons, comments and unbalanced delimiters. Font-stack families are refused outright if they contain quotes or backslashes. The emitter inserts alias lines by replacing the first "}\n", so it relies on emitCss producing one block at that point.

src/core/extractors/web/jsx-extractor.ts.what: Reads JSX and TSX at literal confidence: className strings through the Tailwind resolver, style={{}} object literals, styled-components template CSS, element tags as a heuristic structure signal, and text between tags. A className given as an expression is counted as unresolved and never guessed at.
src/core/extractors/web/jsx-extractor.ts.why: Reading an unresolvable className as if it were literal would report styles the component never renders. Counting it instead keeps the verdict honest about how much the scanner could not see.
src/core/extractors/web/jsx-extractor.ts.gotcha: The header names three things read and one refused, but the code also reads styled-components and text content, which the header omits. BUG (low, performance): line 49 calls scan() inside the loop condition, so the whole file is rescanned on every iteration (quadratic in the number of className expressions).

src/commands/ds-change-token-impl.ts.what: `ui ds change-token`: changes one two-level token's value (literal or alias), validates it against the token's type, re-resolves the whole tree, reseals the design system through ds-reseal, and records a token_change event.
src/commands/ds-change-token-impl.ts.why: This is the sanctioned way to edit a sealed token. The header says it was the only writer that resealed correctly before the reseal extraction, so its behaviour is the reference for the shared helper.
src/commands/ds-change-token-impl.ts.gotcha: Composite tokens (typography, shadow) are refused, so their members must be edited by hand and resealed. A new value equal to the old one returns changed:false and writes nothing.

src/commands/ds-context-impl.ts.what: `ui ds context`: emits the design system as a read-only block for a host model, as markdown or JSON, with the project and studio soul, the guidelines pack, and an optional Tailwind @theme block. The text is capped by --max-bytes, and the theme is appended after the cap so it is never truncated.
src/commands/ds-context-impl.ts.why: The host reads this instead of the raw files, so one command produces the context that a generated page is built from.
src/commands/ds-context-impl.ts.gotcha: An unreadable soul or guidelines file silently degrades to absent, so a broken file does not show up as an error. Only --include, --max-bytes and --format are validated.

src/commands/ds-guidelines-impl.ts.what: Dispatcher for `ui ds guidelines` (build, check, export). Each action has its own allowed flag set, and any stray flag is refused. build calls buildPack and writes the result in stages. check and export delegate to their own modules.
src/commands/ds-guidelines-impl.ts.why: The three actions take different flags, so a flag that does not apply to an action is refused rather than silently ignored.
src/commands/ds-guidelines-impl.ts.gotcha: An unexpected error from the pack builder comes back as BUILD_FAILED with its cause, so a builder defect is a structured error, not a crash.

src/commands/init.ts.what: `ui init --runtime <r>` (or --all) writes a manifest and the runtime's adapter tree: commands and skills for Claude or Antigravity, or an AGENTS.md block for Codex. With --with-agents it also generates the agent roster after the adapter tree is written. Every collision is checked before the first write.
src/commands/init.ts.why: Installs ease-design into a project for one runtime, or all three. Writes are all-or-nothing, so a failed install leaves no partial state.
src/commands/init.ts.gotcha: The model adapter's verifiedAt date is a literal string (2026-07-18), so it must be changed by hand when the probe is repeated. As the header says, a failure after the adapter tree is written (during --with-agents) leaves that tree in place.

src/commands/knowledge-promote.ts.what: `ui knowledge promote`: selects live rulings that recur in the ledger, or that cite enough distinct source documents. It scrubs project names, people and hosts from the output, then writes candidates.json and candidates.md.
src/commands/knowledge-promote.ts.why: Moves a ruling that has shown it holds across events into a candidate list that can be shared, without leaking the project it came from.
src/commands/knowledge-promote.ts.gotcha: Names shorter than 4 characters are never scrubbed automatically, so they must be listed with --redact. Role words such as owner and source are excluded from name collection, so rulings about owners keep their wording.

src/commands/product-context.ts.what: The `ui product-context` dispatcher and its compile and lint actions. compile merges receipt files into a canonical atlas with a digest. lint replays an atlas and byte-compares the result. project-flow is delegated to its own module.
src/commands/product-context.ts.why: Lets a product atlas be built from receipts and checked later, with the canonical bytes as the proof.
src/commands/product-context.ts.gotcha: The input cap (MAX_COMPILE_INPUT_BYTES) applies to the whole batch of receipts, not to each file. An atlas above the output cap is refused, not truncated.

src/core/color-convert.ts.what: OKLCH colour conversion: sRGB to Oklab to OKLCH and back. Gamut clamping binary-searches chroma at fixed lightness and hue. Pure arithmetic with no dependencies.
src/core/color-convert.ts.why: Lets colour ramps and comparisons happen in a perceptual space, and keeps converted colours inside sRGB before they are written.
src/core/color-convert.ts.gotcha: isInSRGBGamut allows a 0.001 tolerance outside [0, 1], so a colour just outside the gamut counts as in-gamut and is returned unchanged. oklchToHex then clips the channels when it writes the hex value.

src/core/delivery/delivery-types.ts.what: Types for the delivery artifacts: four kinds (design-brief, generation-contract, qualification-record, learning-record), the findings and result shapes, the validation context (contract, activation, capability catalog), the six required gates (validate-layout, a11y-lint, taste-lint, content-lint, ds-usage-lint, ds-a11y), and the three marketing viewports (1440, 768, 390).
src/core/delivery/delivery-types.ts.why: The shared vocabulary for the delivery validators, so every validator uses the same kinds, gates and viewports.
src/core/delivery/delivery-types.ts.gotcha: DeliveryError has a single code, BAD_DELIVERY, so a caller cannot tell a bad kind from a bad version by code alone. The message carries that distinction.

src/core/delivery/validate-delivery.ts.what: Entry point for validating one delivery artifact. It checks kind and version, rejects learning-record above version 1, then routes to the v1 or v2 validator for that kind.
src/core/delivery/validate-delivery.ts.why: One place decides which validator applies, so each kind's rules stay in their own module.
src/core/delivery/validate-delivery.ts.gotcha: Only versions 1 and 2 are accepted, and learning-record is version 1 only. Both checks run here, before any validator is called.

src/core/design-facts/fact-kinds.ts.what: Per-kind payload types for the facts model: colour (with its role), gradient, typography, spacing, radius, border, shadow, motion, text (with its role, including metadata) and structure (with depth, ref and parentRef). Each docblock names the rule that needs the field.
src/core/design-facts/fact-kinds.ts.why: Ties each fact's shape to the rule that uses it, so fields are not added speculatively.
src/core/design-facts/fact-kinds.ts.gotcha: The metadata text role exists because a 9,334-character <title> once produced a line-length finding. Rules that judge prose must exclude it, while the census still counts it.

src/core/design-facts/index.ts.what: The public surface of the facts model. It re-exports fact-model, fact-kinds, fact-collector, extractor-registry and rule-requirements, and extractors and rules import from here only.
src/core/design-facts/index.ts.why: Lets the internal split change without touching the consumers.
src/core/design-facts/index.ts.gotcha: This is a barrel file. Any new export added to a re-exported module becomes public API automatically.

src/core/ds-guidelines-answers.ts.what: The answers store, guidelines.answers.json: a durable {version:1, answers:{slotId:{lines,file}}} file. Parsing validates every entry. mergeAnswers picks the winning answer for each slot id (the one in the slot's file, then the stored one, then any other file) and parks the losers.
src/core/ds-guidelines-answers.ts.why: Answers used to live only in generated files that the build overwrote. The store keeps them safe across rebuilds.
src/core/ds-guidelines-answers.ts.gotcha: An answer deleted from a markdown file comes back on the next build, because the store still holds it. To discard it for good, remove it from both the store and the file. The header and the CLI help both say this.

src/core/ds-guidelines-render.ts.what: Markdown rendering for the guidelines pack and its generated-block seal. Each generated block is wrapped in id and sha markers, where sha is the first 12 hex characters of the body's SHA-256. parseGeneratedBlocks reads the blocks back and reports structural damage.
src/core/ds-guidelines-render.ts.why: An edit to a generated block breaks its sha, so the checker can tell a hand edit from an untouched block. The fix is always a rebuild.
src/core/ds-guidelines-render.ts.gotcha: The seal covers only the body of each block. Edits outside the blocks are not detected by the seal, and are judged by other checks.

src/core/knowledge-promotion-ruling.ts.what: Helpers over one ruling record for the promotion commands: type guards, effectiveStatus (a ruling with no status is live unless it names a successor), usableRulings, distinctSourceDocuments, and a category-then-id sort.
src/core/knowledge-promotion-ruling.ts.why: Real project rulings predate the status field, so an unmarked ruling is treated as live rather than rejected.
src/core/knowledge-promotion-ruling.ts.gotcha: distinctSourceDocuments strips the #anchor from each source, so two sections of one file count as a single document and corroborate nothing.

src/commands/ds.ts.what: The `ui ds` dispatcher. It routes 14 subcommands (kit, init, import, context, change-token, set-role, status, diff, docs, a11y, specimen, preview, soul, guidelines) and holds the help text for all of them, including every error code.
src/commands/ds.ts.why: A single entry point for the design-system commands. The help text is the public contract for their flags and error codes.
src/commands/ds.ts.gotcha: The help text repeats detail that lives in each subcommand's own module, so the two can drift apart. Update both when a flag or an error code changes.

src/commands/figma-comments-run.ts.what: `ui figma comments`: reads a comments payload captured outside the kernel, folds it into threads, resolves each pin to its frame and chain, applies --under, --since, --pending, --authored-by and --include-resolved, and prints a digest. Read-only: no network and no model.
src/commands/figma-comments-run.ts.why: Design feedback is triaged from captured data, so the kernel never calls the API. --delivery-target is required, because a batch without one is not actionable.
src/commands/figma-comments-run.ts.gotcha: --since and --authored-by both include resolved threads, because the owner resolves a thread as soon as he replies, and filtering would hide the verdicts. --under is refused when its subtree is missing from the nodes payload, so an empty result cannot be mistaken for an empty section.

src/commands/ingest-figma-ds.ts.what: `ui ingest-figma-ds`: compiles a figma-agent scan (Variables, Styles, Components) into an unsealed, portable bundle: tokens.json, component-registry.json, DESIGN.md and, optionally, a seeded memory ledger.
src/commands/ingest-figma-ds.ts.why: Onboards an existing Figma design system into a form any runtime can read, with no network call and no model.
src/commands/ingest-figma-ds.ts.gotcha: The bundle is unsealed, and the command refuses an --out folder named design because that path is the sealed one. Run `ds import` to seal the output into a project.

src/core/color-scale.ts.what: Generates an 11-stop OKLCH palette (50 to 950) from one hex colour. It anchors the stop nearest the base lightness, sets lightness per stop, tapers chroma with a Gaussian, clamps to sRGB, and reports WCAG contrast against white.
src/core/color-scale.ts.why: Gives a brand colour a full ramp whose lightness steps are perceptually even. The header says the output matches the EaseUI original byte for byte, which rests on golden-value tests I did not open.
src/core/color-scale.ts.gotcha: DUPLICATE: srgbToLinear and the hex expansion are copied from color-convert.ts, on purpose, to keep this file self-contained. Change both copies together.

src/core/ds-context.ts.what: Formats a DesignSystem as the markdown or JSON context block a host reads. It emits semantic tokens only, plus the roles summary, the soul chain (project, studio, factory), the guidelines summary and the anti-patterns. maxBytes bounds only the variable tables.
src/core/ds-context.ts.why: The default context must stay small, while the stance and the roles always arrive intact. A byte budget that starved the tokens would defeat the purpose of the command.
src/core/ds-context.ts.gotcha: The soul chain, roles and guidelines are exempt from maxBytes, so output can exceed --max-bytes when they are large. The final fallback cuts text by bytes, which can split a multi-byte UTF-8 character and leave a replacement character.

src/core/memory-lessons.ts.what: Lesson replay for the memory ledger. compileLessons walks the ledger in order and builds lesson entries from proposed and reviewed events. It enforces that a review cites exactly its own lesson, and that status moves in order: accept or reject from pending, revoke from accepted. Also holds the shared guards.
src/core/memory-lessons.ts.why: A projection never confers approval. Status is derived from the ledger alone, so a lesson can become accepted only through a review event that cites it.
src/core/memory-lessons.ts.gotcha: compileLessons throws on the first invalid event, so a single bad event blocks the whole lesson replay. approvalRef and approvalFingerprint are checked for format only; the referenced file is never read.

src/adapters/index.ts.what: Dispatches to the per-runtime adapter generators (claude, antigravity, codex) and returns the list of files to write. Adds the model-adapter wrapper script to every runtime's list.
src/adapters/index.ts.why: Keeps the per-runtime generators pure, and keeps the wrapper out of the manifest's adapters[], so adapter-wrapper-lint sees only the shapes it expects.
src/adapters/index.ts.gotcha: generateAdapter reads and writes nothing, so a caller that needs to detect existing files must check them itself. init.ts does this.

src/commands/ds-preview-impl.ts.what: `ui ds preview`: loads and verifies the design system, then writes one self-contained specimen.html, or with --split one page per component plus an index.json.
src/commands/ds-preview-impl.ts.why: Gives a visual check of the tokens and registry with no build step, and the same design system always produces the same bytes.
src/commands/ds-preview-impl.ts.gotcha: With --split the pages are written one at a time, so a failure partway through leaves some pages from the new run and the rest from the old one. The error does not say which.

src/commands/gate.ts.what: `ui gate <file>` runs six families (layout, a11y, taste, tell, content, and an autofix dry-run), adds the token-coverage check, applies a family's gate_policy when --family is given, and reports PASS or FAIL. `ui gate coverage` lists the checks that can run for the project.
src/commands/gate.ts.why: One composed verdict per file, so every workflow gates the same way. --skip requires a reason, so a partial gate is always a declared decision.
src/commands/gate.ts.gotcha: BUG (silent weakening): without --tokens, token-coverage falls back to autoScoreTokenCoverage, which returns undefined on any error. A corrupt brand token file therefore silently removes a check the help text calls REQUIRED, and the gate can pass. Also, "coverage" is reserved: a file of that name cannot be gated. [found by reading the code; not reproduced]

src/core/ds-guidelines-gap-knowledge.ts.what: Finds the gaps measured in this design system (a component with no disabled or empty state, a canonical role no token plays, a declared token pair below AA) and turns each one into a rule that cites its knowledge file and carries its gap id. Sorted by id.
src/core/ds-guidelines-gap-knowledge.ts.why: General design knowledge enters the pack only as the answer to a gap found in this system, so no citation appears without evidence behind it.
src/core/ds-guidelines-gap-knowledge.ts.gotcha: Gap ids come from the evidence (component and state, role name, or token pair plus a hash), never from a counter. A gap is identified by its id, so one measurement recorded twice is kept once.

src/core/ds-kit-inventory.ts.what: Reads each kit source (a registry or a Figma capture) into inventory items. It checks the source hash and scope, validates each record, and re-projects Figma variables into the token tree to confirm nothing was lost.
src/core/ds-kit-inventory.ts.why: A kit is only as faithful as its inventory, so each captured component is checked against its source, and its tokens are rebuilt from the raw Figma variables.
src/core/ds-kit-inventory.ts.gotcha: Duplicate detection normalises names (NFKC, trimmed, lower-cased), so "Button" and "button " count as one component and fail the check.

src/core/ds-soul.ts.what: The soul kernel (design/soul.md): the scaffold written by ds init and soul init, the context formatter that caps the soul at 150 lines, and a structure linter. The linter checks the three required sections (Never, Always, Voice), real content in each, a ratified status and placeholder copy. It never judges taste.
src/core/ds-soul.ts.why: A soul is a declared stance, so only its structure is checked mechanically. Taste is left to the model.
src/core/ds-soul.ts.gotcha: checkSoul computes warningCount as findings.length - errorCount. That is safe today because only error and warning exist, but a third severity would be counted as a warning. This is the trap finding-schema.ts warns about.

src/core/prompt-plan/prompt-plan-shared-.what: Shared helpers for the prompt-plan validators: type guards, a finding builder that defaults severity to error, hasDecision (a decision needs an id, a value, a source type and a confidence), and sameMembers for order-free list comparison.
src/core/prompt-plan/prompt-plan-shared-.why: Every prompt-plan validator checks the same shapes, so the guards are kept in one file.
src/core/prompt-plan/prompt-plan-shared-.gotcha: BUG (low): sameMembers compares only length and membership, so it returns true for [a, a, b] against [a, b, b]. Callers that rely on it must check for duplicates separately. [found by reading the code; not reproduced]

src/core/tell-thresholds.ts.what: The registry of every tuning constant the tell family uses, each with its owner rule, unit and provenance. Colour windows, type, surface, labels, motion, alpha and voice thresholds all live here.
src/core/tell-thresholds.ts.why: A number that is written down is not pinned by being written down. The file says each constant is pinned by a boundary pair in tell-boundary-pairs.ts, where a value at the threshold must pass and one just past it must fail.
src/core/tell-thresholds.ts.gotcha: The header records 13 of 63 probes that came back green, and says a meta-test fails for any constant without a pair. I did not open tell-boundary-pairs.ts, so the meta-test is unconfirmed. Presence checks are kept out of this table on purpose.

src/core/token-coverage-io.ts.what: Filesystem glue for the token-coverage check. It finds the project's token file (the design-dir contract first, then brand/design/design.tokens.json), gathers the HTML and its linked stylesheets, and scores them.
src/core/token-coverage-io.ts.why: The gate needs to grade a page against the project's own tokens without the caller knowing where those tokens live.
src/core/token-coverage-io.ts.gotcha: autoScoreTokenCoverage swallows every error and returns undefined, so an unreadable auto-detected file looks the same as no file. The gate then skips a check it calls required (see gate.ts). The explicit path, scoreTokenCoverage, is the loud one.

src/adapters/templates.ts.what: Registries and resolver for the adapter generator. WORKFLOW_VERBS, SKILL_NAMES and JOURNEY_NAMES list the templates, resolveTemplatePath finds each one, and AGENT_TEMPLATE_COMMAND_ALLOWLIST pins the ui commands each agent template may cite.
src/adapters/templates.ts.why: The lists must match the template files. The allowlist catches a template that teaches a superseded command, which an existence check cannot do.
src/adapters/templates.ts.gotcha: The allowlist is checked template-to-list only. An entry left behind after a template edit stays as dead config until review removes it.

src/commands/ds-diff-impl.ts.what: `ui ds diff <base> <head>`: loads two design-system states (tokens and an optional registry), diffs them, and reports the semver and the visual-breaking changes as markdown, json or pr-comment. Exits 1 on a dangling reference.
src/commands/ds-diff-impl.ts.why: Lets a pull request show whether a token change is safe, without modifying either state.
src/commands/ds-diff-impl.ts.gotcha: A missing registry is read as an empty component list, with no error. A head directory that has no registry therefore reads as every component removed. Only the tokens file is required.

src/commands/ds-docs-impl.ts.what: `ui ds docs`: regenerates component reference docs from the registry, with resolved token values where the tokens file is readable. Writes to --out or stdout, as markdown or JSON.
src/commands/ds-docs-impl.ts.why: Docs generated from the registry cannot fall behind it, which is what keeps them trustworthy.
src/commands/ds-docs-impl.ts.gotcha: Unreadable tokens are swallowed. The docs still render, without any resolved values, and nothing in the output says so.

src/commands/ds-guidelines-load.ts.what: Shared project loading for the guidelines build, check and export actions. It resolves the project, loads and verifies the sealed store (hash drift is tolerated only with --allow-unsealed), and reads the optional inputs.
src/commands/ds-guidelines-load.ts.why: Every guidelines action starts from the same verified load, so none of them can run against a store that failed verification.
src/commands/ds-guidelines-load.ts.gotcha: The flag that names the pack directory differs by action: --out for build and check, but --pack for export, where --out names the bundle destination. The packFlag parameter selects which one.

src/commands/ds-kit-plan-impl.ts.what: `ui ds kit plan` (planKit): takes an owner's component capture, its tokens and a display name, and reserves a new candidate folder holding a source copy, the tokens, a theme file and a kit.json whose mappings are all unresolved.
src/commands/ds-kit-plan-impl.ts.why: Starts an owner kit as a reviewable, partial candidate. Each item stays unresolved until someone authors its implementation.
src/commands/ds-kit-plan-impl.ts.gotcha: The folder is reserved with mkdir, and a failed write leaves a partial reservation (KIT_PLAN_INCOMPLETE) that must not be reused. minimumComponents is a literal 25 in the spec, not derived from the capture.

src/commands/ds-set-role-impl.ts.what: `ui ds set-role <token> <role>`: sets the design-os.role annotation on one token and reseals through reseal, the same ceremony as change-token. Rejects an unknown token (BAD_TOKEN) and a non-canonical role (BAD_ROLE).
src/commands/ds-set-role-impl.ts.why: This is the owner's correction path for role recognition, recorded as a changelogged mutation rather than a hand edit.
src/commands/ds-set-role-impl.ts.gotcha: The no-op check compares only the stored role string, so setting the same role twice returns changed:false and writes nothing. There is no command to remove a role annotation; a different canonical role can only replace it.

src/commands/knowledge-draft-ruling.ts.what: `ui knowledge draft-ruling`: turns an approver's correction into a draft rulings file (status draft, approved_by empty), and optionally appends a ruling-candidate event to the ledger.
src/commands/knowledge-draft-ruling.ts.why: Captures a correction as a draft ruling, so it can be reviewed and promoted later instead of being lost in chat.
src/commands/knowledge-draft-ruling.ts.gotcha: BUG (ordering): the ledger event is appended before the draft file is written. If the file write then fails, the ledger holds an event for a draft that does not exist. A retry heals this, because DUPLICATE_ID is accepted and the file is then written. [found by reading the code; not reproduced]

src/commands/ds-a11y-impl.ts.what: `ui ds a11y`: audits the contrast of declared token pairs in design/design.tokens.json (explicit --pairs, or inferred), and exits 1 on any AA failure. Read-only, and it never claims accessibility.
src/commands/ds-a11y-impl.ts.why: A cheap, deterministic check on the colour pairs a system declares, run before any page is built.
src/commands/ds-a11y-impl.ts.gotcha: It checks only declared pairs. A pair the system never declares is never measured, so a clean run says nothing about pairs it did not see. The header says this.

src/core/ds-a11y.ts.what: Token-pair contrast audit. For each text token and surface token, it measures WCAG contrast and flags pairs below AA (4.5:1). It prefers {role}/{role}-foreground pairs, and also checks each foreground on its hover and active surfaces. Only explicit --pairs or the naming fallback are used when no pairs are declared.
src/core/ds-a11y.ts.why: Catches the recurring low-contrast secondary-text trap at the design-system level, before any screen is built. The output says it verifies declared pairs only and is not a conformance claim.
src/core/ds-a11y.ts.gotcha: The legacy fallback pairs every text-named token with every surface-named token by name alone, so its results are guesses; the report labels them as inferred. A result with measured=false is not a pass, and renderA11yReport prints a warning for it.

src/core/ds-guidelines-lint.ts.what: Linter for one rendered guidelines file. It checks each explicit token:, component: and term: span against the sealed design system, flags generated blocks whose body no longer matches its sha, flags host text that cites a superseded ruling, and flags slot answers that use a glossary-avoided word.
src/core/ds-guidelines-lint.ts.why: Only explicit spans are checked, so the linter never judges prose it cannot resolve. term: spans are counted, not judged, when no glossary exists, so the report never claims a verdict it did not reach.
src/core/ds-guidelines-lint.ts.gotcha: The superseded-citation regex matches ruling ids inside host-written text only. Generated blocks are exempt, so a superseded id inside a block is caught only by the block sha check.

src/core/ds-guidelines-store-sections.ts.what: Builds the store-derived guideline files: vocabulary.md (colour roles mapped to the project's own tokens, the forbidden colour pairs below AA, and the non-colour scales) and the components file. Missing inputs are recorded as skipped sources, never as errors.
src/core/ds-guidelines-store-sections.ts.why: Lets the pack describe the project in its own token names and never rename them. A skipped source is named in the manifest, so an absent input is visible.
src/core/ds-guidelines-store-sections.ts.gotcha: Forbidden-pair rules are omitted entirely when pairs can only be guessed from names, and the skipped-source note says so. A pack built from such a store has no forbidden-pair section at all.

src/core/ds-kit-adopt.ts.what: Exclusive adoption of a validated kit. It freezes the validated bytes, reserves a fresh target folder with mkdir, writes every file with exclusive create, re-reads the destination bytes, and writes the manifest last as the single seal. On failure it withdraws the seal and reports what was committed.
src/core/ds-kit-adopt.ts.why: A reservation never overwrites an existing folder, and the seal is published only after the destination has been checked, so a half-adopted kit cannot look valid.
src/core/ds-kit-adopt.ts.gotcha: A failed adoption leaves a reserved, incomplete folder behind, and the error says to retry only into a different absent destination. The non-null assertion on kit.json relies on validateKit having already indexed it.

src/core/figma-node-reader.ts.what: Sidecar storage for captured Figma node specs: one components/<slug>.figma.json file per component, with a pointer on the registry record. It derives the pointer path (with a case-preserving file-slug segment), validates the payload shape, and reads and writes sidecars with a byte-equality content guard.
src/core/figma-node-reader.ts.why: Keeps the shared registry small and lets each component's Figma spec diff on its own. The design-to-code markup stays one-way and is not touched here.
src/core/figma-node-reader.ts.gotcha: Validation is shallow by design: it checks the discriminant and passes the tree through. The file imports toSafeFilename from html-export.ts, a coupling that looks out of place for Figma storage. On a case-insensitive filesystem, two different slugs that differ only by case still land in one directory; the file says so.

src/core/memory-error.ts.what: The shared error types for the memory ledger: MemoryEventError (a typed error with a code) and MemoryAppendCommittedError, which means the append succeeded and a later failure must not trigger another append.
src/core/memory-error.ts.why: Lives in its own file so event validation and lesson replay can share the error type without an import cycle.
src/core/memory-error.ts.gotcha: MemoryAppendCommittedError computes partial by comparing the ids it has against expectedCount. Callers that do not pass expectedCount get partial=false even when the batch was cut short.

src/core/method-json-schema.ts.what: A small, deterministic Draft-07 subset validator for the method and brief contracts. It supports type, const, enum, length and pattern checks, required and additionalProperties, items, allOf, if/then, oneOf and anyOf, and local $ref. It returns a list of path-keyed issues.
src/core/method-json-schema.ts.why: Lets the method contracts be checked with no dependency, and deterministically, so the same value always yields the same issues.
src/core/method-json-schema.ts.gotcha: Keywords outside the subset (format, not, additionalItems, dependencies, and others) are silently ignored, so a schema that depends on them accepts values it should reject. Nesting is capped at 64 levels.

src/core/product-context-compile.ts.what: Compiles one or more product-context receipts into a canonical product atlas. It normalises and orders the receipts, checks that they share one product id and that no receipt id repeats, totals the omitted counts with an overflow guard, collects coverage and findings, resolves fields and supersession, and emits canonical bytes with a digest.
src/core/product-context-compile.ts.why: Gives the same receipts the same atlas bytes every time, so the atlas can be verified later by replay.
src/core/product-context-compile.ts.gotcha: Accepts 1 to 1024 receipts. A product-id mismatch throws a ProductIdMismatch error, and a count overflow throws OmittedOverflow. Both are caught by the command layer, not here.

src/adapters/claude.ts.what: Claude Code adapter: builds the artifact list for the claude runtime. It writes one slash-command file per workflow verb (including init), one skill file per craft skill and per journey, and one routing rule.
src/adapters/claude.ts.why: Turns the template registries into the files a Claude Code project loads. Every file is a write, so the init collision check can treat them all the same way.
src/adapters/claude.ts.gotcha: DRIFT: the header says 22 slash-command files and 45 artifacts. The registries give 23 verbs (init included), 19 craft skills and 3 journeys, plus 1 routing rule, which is 46 artifacts. Fix the header.

src/adapters/wrapper-shapes-shared.ts.what: Shared, pure helpers for the runtime wrapper builders: YAML quoting, path slashing, the knowledge-root anchor, the skill reference lines, the routing glue shown to the host model, and the routing rule file builder.
src/adapters/wrapper-shapes-shared.ts.why: The same routing guidance goes to Claude, Antigravity and Codex. Keeping it in one place stops the runtimes from drifting apart.
src/adapters/wrapper-shapes-shared.ts.gotcha: The routing text is hard-coded in this file and not read from the templates, so changing how a workflow is routed means changing code. The text also names a sibling skill (es:designer) and the design:os Figma plugin by name, so a runtime without them relies on the fallback sentence.

src/commands/delivery.ts.what: `ui delivery validate <file.json>`: reads a delivery artifact (design brief, generation contract, qualification record or learning record), supplies sibling references (contract, activation) and the installed capability catalog for v2 briefs, then validates it and prints the findings.
src/commands/delivery.ts.why: Checks the shape and the false-green invariants of a delivery artifact. The host model does the qualitative judgment; this command is deterministic.
src/commands/delivery.ts.gotcha: Sibling references are read only when they resolve inside the record's own directory (symlinks are checked with realpath), so a reference cannot reach outside it. A missing or unreadable sibling is silently treated as absent, so the validator then reports it as a missing reference rather than as a read error.

src/commands/design-lint.ts.what: `ui design lint <project-root>`: loads the project's design directory view and lints it against the installed design-dir schema. It prints each finding with its path and a fix hint, and exits 1 on any error.
src/commands/design-lint.ts.why: Gives a single pass over a design directory's shape, so a project can be checked before its design files are used.
src/commands/design-lint.ts.gotcha: warningCount is computed as findings.length - errorCount, the same subtraction that finding-schema.ts warns about. It is safe only while lintDesignDir produces two severities. Check the finding type before adding a third.

src/commands/ds-soul-impl.ts.what: `ui ds soul init|check|factory`: writes the soul scaffold (project or studio), structure-lints it, or prints the factory baseline. Works on design/soul.md, or on the studio soul in EASE_DESIGN_HOME with --studio.
src/commands/ds-soul-impl.ts.why: Connects the soul kernel to the command line. A missing file is reported as a finding on check, because calling check means a soul is expected.
src/commands/ds-soul-impl.ts.gotcha: --studio and --dir cannot be combined, and factory accepts only the global flags. The studio path is user-scoped, so a studio soul is shared across every project on the machine.

src/commands/memory-context-impl.ts.what: `ui memory context --for generate|critique|why`: emits the project's memory as a compact prior for the host model. It includes the project preference prior, recalled context from a rank file, lessons, and, for generate and why only, the cross-project taste profile.
src/commands/memory-context-impl.ts.why: Memory may bias generation but never scores critique, so critique receives only token rationales and design fingerprints, and never the taste profile or any preference.
src/commands/memory-context-impl.ts.gotcha: When --rank-file is given, the events are read twice, once in selectLessonContext and again for the recall corpus. In critique mode the rank file is still validated, but its items are never added to the output.

src/commands/registry.ts.what: `ui registry register|lookup|list`: the component registry command. Register validates the record (strict Category/Variant names, or source-authored names for an owner kit), checks that its tokens exist in a sealed design system, and writes through reseal when a manifest is present, or plainly otherwise.
src/commands/registry.ts.why: The single entry point for adding components. Sealed systems are updated through reseal, so hashes stay correct.
src/commands/registry.ts.gotcha: When a manifest sits beside the registry, the store is loaded from the --file path too, and its seal is checked. Pointing --file at a registry that the manifest did not seal therefore fails with DS_TAMPERED, not with a plain write. Owner-kit names skip the strict pattern, and a name that normalises to an existing one is rejected by a separate collision check.

src/commands/templates-catalogue.ts.what: `ui templates catalogue|lint`: maintainer tools. catalogue emits schemas/template-descriptions.json from the template frontmatter, and with --check verifies the committed file against it. lint validates a catalogue file against its schema.
src/commands/templates-catalogue.ts.why: Keeps the template description catalogue in step with the template files, so discovery text never drifts from the templates it describes.
src/commands/templates-catalogue.ts.gotcha: Drift is checked only when the catalogue already passes its schema, so a malformed catalogue reports the schema error and not drift. The emitted file must match the on-disk bytes exactly.

src/core/a11y-checks-contrast.ts.what: Computed WCAG contrast from resolved facts. For each text colour it finds the nearest opaque background up the structure chain, falls back to the document background from html or body, and checks the ratio against 4.5:1 (or 3:1 for large text). Gradients, media-covered backgrounds and unresolvable backgrounds are reported as not computable.
