src/core/a11y-checks-contrast.ts.why: Lets the gate check contrast on a rendered surface without a browser. It refuses to judge where the background cannot be known, so a missing answer never reads as a pass.
src/core/a11y-checks-contrast.ts.gotcha: The lookup for a text node's typography uses a line-based fallback that can pick a different element's size on the same line. Inside the loop, typography.find is a linear scan, so the pass is quadratic in the number of facts. Both are minor.

src/core/css-token-ingest.ts.what: Builds a DTCG token tree from the custom properties extracted from a stylesheet. Literal values become primitives, and var() references become semantic aliases. Selectors become modes through classifySelector. Each leaf keeps the source name verbatim, and two source names that sanitise to one path fail with LEAF_COLLISION.
src/core/css-token-ingest.ts.why: Lets a design system be learned from the CSS a project already has. The verbatim leaf naming keeps two properties that differ only by a prefix as two separate tokens, instead of merging them.
src/core/css-token-ingest.ts.gotcha: A property whose every value is a var() reference and whose name has no recognised hint is typed as color by default (typeFromNameHint). A non-colour alias with an unusual name is therefore mistyped. Anything without a base selector is listed as unverified, not promoted.

src/core/ds-preview.ts.what: Specimen-page generator. buildSpecimenPage renders one self-contained HTML page from the design system: tokens, colour pairs with their own foreground, type, shape, motion and one block per component with markup. buildComponentPages renders one page per component with markup, for --split.
src/core/ds-preview.ts.why: A pure string transform, so the same design system always gives the same bytes, and the page passes the same linters as the rest of the output.
src/core/ds-preview.ts.gotcha: BUG (plausible, not reproduced): componentSlug is lossy. Every run of non-alphanumeric characters becomes one dash, so an owner-kit label "Owner Item 40" and "Owner-Item-40" both become owner-item-40. --split then overwrites one page with the other and lists two index entries for one file. Registry names are unaffected, because the standard pattern allows only letters.

src/core/extractors/native/swiftui-extra.what: Reads SwiftUI source at literal confidence: fonts, colours and gradients written as literals, corner radii, padding and stack spacing, edge overlays read as side tabs, shadows, animations, and Text strings. Structure is not supplied, so nesting rules are reported NOT-EVALUATED.
src/core/extractors/native/swiftui-extra.why: SwiftUI states its design in modifiers with literal arguments, which a scanner can read exactly. Theme lookups and conditionals are counted as unresolved, not guessed.
src/core/extractors/native/swiftui-extra.gotcha: Lines 183 and 184 run scan() inside loop conditions, so the file is rescanned on every iteration (quadratic, as in jsx-extractor.ts). The conditional pattern (a question mark followed later by a colon) is crude and can count Swift optional chaining as a ternary.

src/core/figma-apply.ts.what: Pure apply core for the Figma live sync. It takes the preview delta, the current registry and an optional mirror index of captured node specs, then returns the next registry, the sidecar writes, a report and the paths to clean up. A deletion soft-deprecates a record; an update refreshes its scope and clears deprecation; an addition is materialised only when a capture exists.
src/core/figma-apply.ts.why: Keeps the kernel free of filesystem and network work, so the same log and captures always produce the same registry. Without a capture, a new component stays pending rather than getting a stub, so no content is invented.
src/core/figma-apply.ts.gotcha: Replaying the whole log over a base registry reproduces the final lifecycle state, so re-applying is idempotent. A pointer that moves to a new path schedules the old file for deletion, which the command layer must confirm points at a different physical file first.

src/core/figma-ds-ingest.ts.what: Pure orchestrator for the Figma design-system ingest. It checks that a ds.json has the three top-level arrays (components, tokens, styles), builds the DTCG token tree, classifies the registry, and assembles the DESIGN.md text and the counts.
src/core/figma-ds-ingest.ts.why: Turns one scan into the three portable stores (tokens, registry, DESIGN.md) with no network and no model, so the same scan always gives the same bytes.
src/core/figma-ds-ingest.ts.gotcha: parseDsFile checks that each key is an array, not what its elements contain, and the casts to DsComponent[] and DsVariable[] are unchecked. A malformed element reaches the builders as it is; only the token builder's own checks catch some of them.

src/core/figma-ds-tokens.ts.what: Converts Figma variables into a two-tier DTCG token tree. A variable with a literal value becomes a primitive, and one with a VARIABLE_ALIAS becomes a semantic alias. Tier prefixes are stripped from paths, mode values other than the base become extensions, and dangling or self-referential aliases are dropped.
src/core/figma-ds-tokens.ts.why: Makes a Figma library usable by the rest of the toolchain, and keeps the light/dark split the designer chose rather than flattening it.
src/core/figma-ds-tokens.ts.gotcha: A variable whose path collides with an earlier one is counted as skipped, and the name of the collision is not reported. Paths are sanitised to a-z, 0-9 and dashes, so two distinct Figma names can collide without a warning.

src/core/memory-graph.ts.what: Compiles the design-memory event ledger into a graph view: persona picks, axis failures, vibe words, token changes, design fingerprints and insights, plus the lesson replay. Weights decay by half-life (30 days), and the output is key-sorted, so the same events and clock give identical bytes.
src/core/memory-graph.ts.why: The ledger is the source of truth and this graph is rebuildable, so the graph can always be recompiled from the events.
src/core/memory-graph.ts.gotcha: A user pick only counts toward a persona when the chosen design id was recorded by an earlier variant_generated event. Several event types (component_registered, harvested, duel_result, manual_edit) are stored but contribute nothing to the graph.

src/core/persona-expand.ts.what: Expands a persona record into a complete token skeleton: primitive palettes, space, radius, type, shadows and duration, then the semantic colour, space, radius, text, elevation and motion layers. Foregrounds are chosen so they clear AA on their surface.
src/core/persona-expand.ts.why: Gives a new design system a full, accessible starting set that already follows the paired-foreground standard, so the first audit usually passes.
src/core/persona-expand.ts.gotcha: pickNeutralFg returns the best stop even when none reaches AA, and pickStateStop falls back to 600 without checking. Nothing here warns about that; only the later ds a11y run catches it. The golden counts in the tests must be updated with any reordering.

src/core/product-context-flow-projection.what: Projects a replayed product atlas into a flow (screens, transitions, entry points). It reads only resolved fields with a selected or coalesced candidate whose claim is present, lints the flow, and reports the result as available or blocked.
src/core/product-context-flow-projection.why: Lets a downstream builder read a flow only when the atlas evidence supports it, and never a flow that contains an error.
src/core/product-context-flow-projection.gotcha: The flow is returned only when there are no errors, and the truth status is always reported as not-evaluated. A blocked projection carries the reason as findings, so a caller must read the findings rather than assume a blank flow means none exists.

src/adapters/antigravity.ts.what: Antigravity adapter: builds the artifact list for the antigravity runtime. It writes one workflow file per verb (including init), one skill file per craft skill and per journey, and one routing rule.
src/adapters/antigravity.ts.why: Produces the workflow and skill files that an Antigravity project loads, with the same template registries as the Claude adapter.
src/adapters/antigravity.ts.gotcha: DRIFT: the header says 22 workflow files and 45 artifacts. The registries give 23 verbs (init included), 22 skills and 1 routing rule, which is 46. The claude.ts header has the same drift.

src/commands/brief-lint.ts.what: `ui brief lint <brief.json>`: validates a design brief's schema, then reads its blocking fields and computes the D4 receipt (CONTINUE or blocked). Optionally writes the questions the brief still needs to --questions.
src/commands/brief-lint.ts.why: Stops a brief that is malformed or incomplete before it drives a build, and lists the questions that unblock it.
src/commands/brief-lint.ts.gotcha: Exit codes are distinct: 1 for a schema error, 2 for a blocked brief and 0 for CONTINUE. The text output and the JSON output report the same findings, so a caller can branch on the exit code alone.

src/commands/ds-guidelines-check-impl.ts.what: `ui ds guidelines check`: runs collectCheck over a built pack and reports the findings, or with --profile figma --bundle validates an exported Figma bundle against its size, count and extension limits.
src/commands/ds-guidelines-check-impl.ts.why: Keeps the check and export commands on one set of findings, so a pack that checks clean is the pack that exports.
src/commands/ds-guidelines-check-impl.ts.gotcha: The Figma profile check reads every file under the bundle into memory before validating, so a very large bundle is read whole. Warnings are computed as findings.length - errorCount, which is safe while there are two severities.

src/commands/judge-report.ts.what: `ui judge report <judgments.jsonl>`: summarises how often shadow judgments match the human decision, per decision point, and checks the optional families file. Shadow mode only: it records and reports, and never enforces.
src/commands/judge-report.ts.why: Lets the team see whether a judge agrees with people before the judge is trusted to decide anything.
src/commands/judge-report.ts.gotcha: Each decision point reports 'not enough data' until a minimum sample of resolved judgments exists, so a small sample is never reported as a rate. The families path is checked only when given.

src/commands/knowledge-activate.ts.what: `ui knowledge activate <request.json>`: checks every profile in the capability catalog against its pilot receipts, then resolves an activation request against the catalog and prints the route, or a structured refusal.
src/commands/knowledge-activate.ts.why: A capability route must be backed by retained evidence, so activation fails closed when a pilot receipt is missing or does not verify.
src/commands/knowledge-activate.ts.gotcha: Receipts are verified for every profile that is not provisional, or that is registered as a v2 pilot, and a receipt id cannot be reused across profiles. A missing or unreadable catalog stops the command before any route is resolved.

src/commands/ksync-drift.ts.what: `ui ksync drift --pins <pins.json> --frames <frames.json>`: checks whether any pinned Figma frame has moved since it was pinned. Reports OK, DRIFT, MISSING or UNCHECKABLE for each pin, and flags an ingest that is too old.
src/commands/ksync-drift.ts.why: Tells the team when built routes no longer match the design they were pinned to. The kernel never calls Figma: the caller captures the frames and passes the file in.
src/commands/ksync-drift.ts.gotcha: The verdict is STALE-INGEST when the capture is older than --max-age-days (default 14) or undated, and it fails regardless of the pins. --warn-only turns any failure into exit 0, so a CI job can report drift without blocking.

src/commands/synthesize-conventions.ts.what: `ui synthesize-conventions <usage-dna.json>`: learns a product's applied conventions from a scan of real screens and writes CONVENTIONS.md, with measured DO and DON'T lines and optional cross-reference to a DS token scale. --seed-memory writes prefers and avoids insights to the ledger.
src/commands/synthesize-conventions.ts.why: Records how the design is actually used, which the vocabulary scan cannot show. Deterministic, so the same scan always gives the same document.
src/commands/synthesize-conventions.ts.gotcha: The DS cross-reference runs only when --ds is supplied, and the output says so. A truncated section is reported in the stats, so the reader knows the numbers may be partial.

src/core/ds-guidelines-figma-profile.ts.what: The Figma guidelines profile: one constant holds the limits (3 to 8 files, 200 KB hard cap, 100 KB soft cap, .md/.txt/.json only). Also parses the --budget flag and validates a bundle against those limits, including any open slots or open scenarios.
src/core/ds-guidelines-figma-profile.ts.why: Keeps Figma's limits in one place, so a change in the beta is a one-line edit. The checked-on date records when the limits were last verified.
src/core/ds-guidelines-figma-profile.ts.gotcha: Limits come from Figma's help article, not from an API, so they can drift without notice. The checkedOn date is the only evidence that they were confirmed, and it is not re-checked by any test.

src/core/extractors/native/flutter-extra.what: Reads Dart and Flutter source at literal confidence: TextStyle fonts, sizes, spacing and alignment, Color literals and Colors.* names, gradients, BorderRadius, EdgeInsets, Border and BoxShadow, and motion. Treats Roboto as the platform default when a file styles text without naming a family.
src/core/extractors/native/flutter-extra.why: Flutter's default face is Roboto, so an app that declares no family is judged as shipping Roboto. SwiftUI's system face is not treated that way, and the asymmetry is kept here, in the extractor that knows the platform.
src/core/extractors/native/flutter-extra.gotcha: BUG (plausible, from the regex alone): the height pattern matches any `height: N,` in the file, not only TextStyle height. `SizedBox(height: 16)` yields a line-height fact of 16, which the filter accepts only between 0.5 and 4. Small SizedBox heights such as 2 or 3 would become false line heights. Not run.

src/core/figma-reconcile-types.ts.what: Shared types for the Figma reconcile pipeline: the change-frame line read from figma.changes.jsonl, the coalesced component state, the registry view, the preview delta and the typed ReconcileError. Also fixes the expected change-log version at 1.
src/core/figma-reconcile-types.ts.why: The change-log format is the boundary shared with the figma-agent producer. Keeping these types in one file means the reader and the producer agree on the same shape.
src/core/figma-reconcile-types.ts.gotcha: The change-log version is a single constant. A reconcile run refuses a mismatch, so a producer that moves to a new version must bump it here in the same change.

src/core/judge-validate.ts.what: Validates the shadow judge's records: a judgment (checked against its JSON schema, then pick-in-candidates and human-decision rules) and the persona families file (unique slugs, nearest family on the same platform, no unreliable attribute, gate_policy only for known checks).
src/core/judge-validate.ts.why: The judge's records feed the agreement report and the gate's family policies. Invalid records are refused here, so a bad judgment cannot skew the report.
src/core/judge-validate.ts.gotcha: An attribute is treated as unreliable only when its agreement is below 0.6, and listing a reliable one is itself an error. The gate_policy rule uses the same check catalog as the gate, so a renamed check breaks any family that names it.

src/core/product-context-receipt-model.t.what: Normalises a product-context receipt and its claims into the canonical shape. It checks exact keys, the capture disposition, and the reason codes, and enforces that a captured receipt has a digest, claims and no omissions, while a capped one has omissions and reason codes.
src/core/product-context-receipt-model.t.why: Receipts are untrusted input, and a canonical shape is what makes the compiled atlas byte-stable.
src/core/product-context-receipt-model.t.gotcha: Each receipt may hold at most 256 claims, and each claim's supersedes list is checked for the id#id form. A malformed claim fails the whole receipt, not only that claim.

src/core/token-emit.ts.what: Pure emitters that turn a resolved token map into CSS custom properties, a Tailwind v4 @theme block, or Figma Tokens Studio JSON. Composite tokens expand to one variable per member, and a shadow also gets a single box-shadow value. A shadow with zero geometry is omitted.
src/core/token-emit.ts.why: Gives every target the same resolved values. Dropping zero shadows keeps a raw hex out of the compiled CSS, where the raw-hex check would reject it.
src/core/token-emit.ts.gotcha: DEAD BRANCH: in emitFigma, the ternary `typeof token.value === "object" ... ? token.value : token.value` returns the same value on both arms, so it does nothing. Remove it or restore the intended arm. Also, a malformed path with no dot is skipped silently.

src/commands/color.ts.what: `ui color`: OKLCH colour math as a command. It has four subcommands: convert (hex to OKLCH, or OKLCH to hex), scale (the 11-stop palette), contrast (WCAG ratio between two colours) and semantic (a palette from named colours).
src/commands/color.ts.why: Lets an agent or a person check a colour's contrast or build a palette without writing any code.
src/commands/color.ts.gotcha: normaliseHex only adds the # and uppercases; it does not validate the input. Each subcommand validates through the core functions, so a bad value fails with BAD_HEX there, not here.

src/commands/ds-guidelines-inputs.ts.what: Reads the optional inputs `ui ds guidelines` may use (rulings, CONTEXT.md, the glossary, CONVENTIONS.md, soul.md) and the existing pack folder into plain text. These are the only filesystem reads in that command besides the pack write.
src/commands/ds-guidelines-inputs.ts.why: A missing optional input is kept as a path with no text, so the pack can list it under skipped sources instead of failing. A file that exists but cannot be read is a hard READ_ERROR, not a silent skip.
src/commands/ds-guidelines-inputs.ts.gotcha: The existing pack is read in full: every .md under the pack folder, not only the files the last manifest lists. A malformed answers store is never silently replaced, because the file's own comment says it may hold the only copy of an answer.

src/commands/knowledge-check.ts.what: `ui knowledge check [--dir] [--as-of YYYYMM]`: walks knowledge/, runs lintKnowledge over the markdown, catalogs, source ledgers and web-technique files, prints the findings and exits 1 when any has error severity.
src/commands/knowledge-check.ts.why: Runs every knowledge rule in one pass, so a stale or broken knowledge file fails before the design uses it. The capability pilot receipts are checked here because reading them is file IO, which the kernel does not do.
src/commands/knowledge-check.ts.gotcha: Without --as-of the month is the current local month (currentMonth), so the same tree can pass in one month and fail the next. Every finding that is not an error is counted as a warning, and the exit code depends only on the error count.

src/commands/knowledge-ledger-lint.ts.what: `ui knowledge ledger lint <events.jsonl>`: reads a learning-ledger file, parses it as JSON Lines or a single JSON document, lints its events and prints the counts by type with each finding.
src/commands/knowledge-ledger-lint.ts.why: Checks every ledger event before its rulings are trusted, and exits non-zero on any finding so a CI job can gate on it.
src/commands/knowledge-ledger-lint.ts.gotcha: Lines that are not valid JSON do not stop the lint: they are counted and added as one extra finding on '(file)'. The exit code counts every finding as an error, whatever severity lintLedgerEvents gave it, so a warning-level check still fails the command.

src/commands/method-lint.ts.what: `ui method lint <run.json>`: validates one method run against the installed method-run schema, reads the design brief it cites (path relative to the run file) and prints a one-line status with the findings.
src/commands/method-lint.ts.why: The run file is the record of a method run. Linting it against the schema and against the brief it cites checks the record's consistency; it does not judge the design itself.
src/commands/method-lint.ts.gotcha: readBrief returns null for a missing or unparseable brief, and what the linter does with null is decided in core/method-lint.ts (not read here). A broken install surfaces as SCHEMA_UNAVAILABLE, not as a validation finding. warningCount is always 0.

src/commands/pattern-lint.ts.what: `ui pattern lint <card.json|dir>`: validates pattern cards against the installed pattern-card schema. Given a directory it collects every .json card beneath it, in name order, and lints each one.
src/commands/pattern-lint.ts.why: A pattern card is a reusable design-pattern record. The linter also receives the card's file name and parent folder as its location, so it can check the card against where it sits.
src/commands/pattern-lint.ts.gotcha: The first file that is not valid JSON ends the run with BAD_JSON, and the cards after it are not linted. A read failure on any file ends the run with FILE_NOT_FOUND. warningCount is always 0.

src/core/capability-catalog.ts.what: Parses and validates the capability catalog (version 1 or 2) into typed profiles, and fingerprints a v2 profile's policy fields with a SHA-256 digest.
src/core/capability-catalog.ts.why: The catalog decides which capabilities are available and what evidence each needs. Parsing fails closed on any malformed profile. For a registered capability the digest lets activation detect that its policy changed (CAPABILITY_PROFILE_POLICY).
src/core/capability-catalog.ts.gotcha: The policy-digest check runs only for ids that have a registered pilot identity carrying a profilePolicyDigest; other v2 profiles are not compared against any digest. A duplicate profile id fails the whole catalog, and in v1 a status of qualified maps to available while anything else maps to unavailable.

src/core/delivery/delivery-v1-validation.what: Validates the v1 delivery records (design brief, generation contract, qualification record): required fields, fixed value sets and the rules a QUALIFIED record must meet.
src/core/delivery/delivery-v1-validation.why: The delivery pipeline trusts these records. The QUALIFIED rules refuse a record that claims success while a required gate failed, a claim is unsupported, a Must criterion is uncovered, or a required viewport was never rendered.
src/core/delivery/delivery-v1-validation.gotcha: The qualification checks look at the record's own fields and booleans, not at the page. The QUALIFIED rules run only when status is QUALIFIED. The attempt counter is capped at 3.

src/core/ds-guidelines-components.ts.what: Builds components.md for the DS guidelines pack from the sealed registry: each category's components with their variants and states, then a 'Confusable names' section for look-alike names.
src/core/ds-guidelines-components.ts.why: A designer or a model can mix up near-identical or same-leaf names. Each look-alike cluster gets a QUESTION slot that asks which one to use when, so the answer is recorded rather than guessed.
src/core/ds-guidelines-components.ts.gotcha: Clusters are connected groups (union-find), so a chain of pairs becomes one cluster even when its outer names are not similar. The slot id hashes the whole sorted member set: adding one member changes the id, and the old answer is parked, not reused. Two names are confusable at edit distance 2 or less on the normalised form, or when they share a leaf under a different parent.

src/core/ds-guidelines-figma-export.ts.what: Assembles the Figma bundle from a checked canonical pack: components.md keeps only the look-alike answers and the component rulings, app rulings merge into apps.md, and the overview's file index is rewritten to match the files that remain.
src/core/ds-guidelines-figma-export.ts.why: Figma reads the component inventory from the library itself, so the bundle carries only what the library cannot show. Keeping it lean also lets it fit a size budget.
src/core/ds-guidelines-figma-export.ts.gotcha: When a budget is set, trimToBudget runs over the whole bundle. A file emptied by trimming is dropped, and the overview index is rewritten afterwards, so the index always matches the files written. Rulings sections that are not trimmable are kept whole.

src/core/figma-mirror-capture.ts.what: The file contract for a Figma mirror capture: parses and validates the JSON the broker writes after scanning live Figma nodes, and indexes the result by node id for `ui figma reconcile --apply`.
src/core/figma-mirror-capture.ts.why: The kernel must stay pure, with no network, so the live scan happens outside it. This file is the only way scanned specs enter, and a malformed capture fails hard as a bug instead of being guessed at.
src/core/figma-mirror-capture.ts.gotcha: A failed scan and a MAX_SCANS drop sit in separate lists because they mean different things: tried and lost, versus never tried. A successful re-scan of a node supersedes both a failure and a drop for that node. Version 1 captures, which have no dropped list, are still accepted.

src/core/html-css-loader.ts.what: The one loader every HTML/CSS-judging command uses to read a page's local linked stylesheets, expanding one level of @import. It returns the sheets it read and an error finding for each local file it could not read.
src/core/html-css-loader.ts.why: Before this module, linters read only the HTML's own text, so a page whose violations sat in a linked stylesheet gated green. Fixing the blind spot here fixes every linter that calls it.
src/core/html-css-loader.ts.gotcha: Remote hrefs (http, protocol-relative, data:) are skipped silently by design. A local <link> or @import that cannot be read becomes an error finding; it is never dropped. @import is followed one level only, so an import inside an imported file is not read.

src/core/memory-lesson-evidence.ts.what: The filesystem side of lesson evidence: realpath-contained reads of project files, byte fingerprints, the design-system revision a lesson is bound to, approval-receipt checks, and the preconditions the locked append runs before it records a lesson event.
src/core/memory-lesson-evidence.ts.why: A lesson can be accepted only with fingerprinted source evidence and a matching approval receipt, and only against the verified design system it was learned from. Rejection and revocation skip the environment checks, so a bad lesson can always be withdrawn.
src/core/memory-lesson-evidence.ts.gotcha: readLessonFile resolves symlinks with realpath before the containment check, so a symlink that escapes the project is refused. A stale kit (KIT_STALE) blocks acceptance but not rejection. The checks happen when the event is appended, not when the memory log is later replayed.

src/core/product-atlas-model.ts.what: Normalises and validates a product-atlas value: its embedded receipts and their digests, the input-set digest over the receipt list, each field's resolution and candidates, and the coverage counters.
src/core/product-atlas-model.ts.why: The atlas is a deterministic record, so the same inputs must always produce the same bytes. Any value outside that exact shape is rejected as BAD_PRODUCT_CONTEXT rather than repaired.
src/core/product-atlas-model.ts.gotcha: Receipts must be in ascending id order and candidates ordered by receipt then claim id, or the atlas is refused. A field whose resolution is 'resolved' must carry value null; every other resolution must carry a non-null value. Read the rule before assuming the names mean what they say.

src/core/product-context-lint.ts.what: Lints a product-atlas file by normalising it, rebuilding it from its own receipts, and comparing the supplied bytes with the rebuilt bytes.
src/core/product-context-lint.ts.why: Two different defects need different repairs: a file that is not canonical (formatting or a hand edit) and a file whose receipts do not replay to the same atlas. Checking the bytes first stops whitespace from being blamed on the receipts.
src/core/product-context-lint.ts.gotcha: Both defects throw from here. The thrown messages are ATLAS_NOT_CANONICAL and BAD_PRODUCT_ATLAS, and the file's own comment says both surface as BAD_PRODUCT_ATLAS, so a caller that matches on the message must handle both.

src/core/prompt-plan/prompt-plan-types.t.what: The types for a prompt-plan lint result: a severity, a finding with its checkId and stage, the result shape with its ready flag and error and warning counts, and the BAD_PROMPT_PLAN error class.
src/core/prompt-plan/prompt-plan-types.t.why: Keeps the prompt-plan result shape in one place, so every producer and the JSON output agree on it.
src/core/prompt-plan/prompt-plan-types.t.gotcha: This file only declares the shapes. PromptPlanResult.ready is a stored boolean, not derived here, so a producer that sets ready inconsistently with errorCount would not be caught in this file.

src/core/report-style.ts.what: Pure string builders for the house report style: the brand banner, the rule-line header, the checklist row and the key/value line, plus the status glyphs. No colour, no ANSI.
src/core/report-style.ts.why: Gives every command the same plain output that reads the same in a terminal, a log or a pasted message.
src/core/report-style.ts.gotcha: renderBanner never throws: a missing or unreadable wordmark falls back to DESIGN:OS. ruleHeader drops its fill when the title and verdict leave no room, so that line can be shorter than the requested width.

src/core/taste-store.ts.what: The taste corpus store: the item, pair-vote and study record types, root resolution, and the append-only JSONL reads and writes for the three ledgers.
src/core/taste-store.ts.why: Every line is validated on load and on append, so a corrupt ledger fails with its file and line number instead of silently skewing the Elo replay that depends on it.
src/core/taste-store.ts.gotcha: Blank lines are skipped, but any other unparseable line stops the load with a TasteLedgerError. Root resolution is --root, then DESIGN_OS_TASTE_ROOT, then taste/ under the working directory. Append validates the shape and writes the line without reading the ledger, so a duplicate id is not rejected here.

src/core/token-coverage.ts.what: Aggregates classified CSS declarations into coverage per category and overall, where coverage = token / (token + raw). Derived values count toward the total but never toward the ratio.
src/core/token-coverage.ts.why: It is the single scoring entry point that both `ui token-coverage` and the gate's token-coverage check call, so the two cannot report different numbers.
src/core/token-coverage.ts.gotcha: A category with no token or raw declarations scores 1, so an empty category never fails the ratio. Derived declarations (calc, percentages, relative units) appear in the total only.

src/adapters/codex.ts.what: The Codex runtime adapter. It builds one upsert-section artifact for AGENTS.md, holding a block of hashes for the workflow, skill and journey templates plus the knowledge root.
src/adapters/codex.ts.why: The sentinel-delimited block can be replaced on every install without touching the user's own AGENTS.md text. The generator is pure and writes nothing.
src/adapters/codex.ts.gotcha: The file's comment says the hashes come from the audited template catalogue, not from disk, so a template edit that skips the catalogue leaves the block's hashes stale. The init verb is skipped because it has no template file.

src/commands/ds-specimen-impl.ts.what: `ui ds specimen [--dir] [--strict] [--json]`: reads the component registry, runs the applicable-state check on each component, and reports the gaps in its variant-by-state matrix.
src/commands/ds-specimen-impl.ts.why: Surfaces a component that claims states it does not show. A stable component with a missing disabled or empty state is breaking its own contract.
src/commands/ds-specimen-impl.ts.gotcha: Only disabled-on-interactive and empty-on-data-family are checked; focus is deliberately not required. A gap on a stable component always fails the command, while warnings fail it only with --strict. A missing registry is DS_NOT_FOUND.

src/commands/judge-record.ts.what: `ui judge record --out <judgments.jsonl> --event <json>`: validates one judgment, refuses it if its id conflicts with the ledger, and appends it. Prints the id and its state, pending or human decision.
src/commands/judge-record.ts.why: The judgment ledger is append-only, so every record is validated and checked for id conflicts before it is written.
src/commands/judge-record.ts.gotcha: A ledger with any invalid line refuses the append (LEDGER_INVALID) until it is repaired. A failed write is reported as WRITE_ERROR without the underlying cause.

src/commands/knowledge-fresh.ts.what: `ui knowledge fresh <rulings.json>`: checks each live ruling's age against --days (default 90) and whether its anchored path still exists under --root, then reports fresh, stale and unanchored rulings.
src/commands/knowledge-fresh.ts.why: Rulings go stale and their anchors move; this shows which ones to revisit. Only --strict makes stale rulings fail the command.
src/commands/knowledge-fresh.ts.gotcha: The default as-of date is today's UTC date (toISOString), not the local date. Rulings that are not live or are unusable are counted but not assessed. The anchor check is existsSync only, so an anchor that still exists but no longer says the right thing passes.

src/commands/ksync-census.ts.what: `ui ksync census <manifest> --pins <pins>`: counts manifest entries by status (built, placeholder, orphan, parked, unlabeled), per app, and how much of the built set carries a pin. Labels and a component registry are optional inputs.
src/commands/ksync-census.ts.why: Shows how much of what was built is tied to the Figma frame it came from. --assume-unlisted gives unlisted entries a status instead of leaving them unlabeled.
src/commands/ksync-census.ts.gotcha: The pinned percentage reads 'n/a' when no built entry is labelled, rather than 0% or 100%. Pins that match no manifest frame are counted as unmatched, not dropped.

src/commands/memory-consolidate-impl.ts.what: `ui memory consolidate`: rebuilds the cross-project taste profile from the project registry, keeps every earlier insight, optionally appends one new insight with its provenance refs, and saves the profile.
src/commands/memory-consolidate-impl.ts.why: The profile is derived data, so rebuilding it from the registry keeps it current. Insights are the only part carried over from the prior profile.
src/commands/memory-consolidate-impl.ts.gotcha: With no registered projects the command exits OK and writes nothing. If the persona index cannot be read, the family resolver falls back to the slug itself, so persona family counts are wrong without any error. The new insight's refs are checked for shape only, not for whether those events exist.

src/commands/memory-export-corpus-impl.t.what: `ui memory export-corpus [--since <eventId>]`: reads the memory ledger and prints the embeddable corpus as NDJSON, or as the JSON envelope with --json, for the optional recall indexer.
src/commands/memory-export-corpus-impl.t.why: Keeps the deterministic half of the recall loop in the binary: the same ledger always yields the same bytes, with no network and no model call.
src/commands/memory-export-corpus-impl.t.gotcha: A missing ledger is an empty corpus, not an error. A ledger read failure returns the MemoryEventError code, or BAD_LEDGER for anything else. --since is passed straight to exportCorpus, which decides what an unknown id means.

src/commands/seam-lint.ts.what: `ui seam lint [--allowlist <path>]`: scans the JS and TS sources under src/ for prose reads, checks them against the seam allowlist (schemas/seam-allowlist.json by default), and exits 1 on any read that is not allowed.
src/commands/seam-lint.ts.why: Keeps the places where code reads prose under control. Each allowed read is listed, so a new one is a deliberate decision rather than an accident.
src/commands/seam-lint.ts.gotcha: A symlink anywhere under src/ aborts the scan rather than being followed. Declaration files (.d.ts) are skipped. A malformed allowlist stops the command with BAD_ALLOWLIST before any source is read.

src/core/content-checks-metadata.ts.what: The scaffolding check: flags a document <title> longer than the METADATA_MAX_CHARS threshold, which is usually a generation prompt left in the title. It reports an error, not a tell.
src/core/content-checks-metadata.ts.why: A prompt in the title lands in the browser tab, the search result and the social card. The file's comment says the threshold came from a measured, bimodal length distribution, so it is not a taste call.
src/core/content-checks-metadata.ts.gotcha: The check is deliberately length-only: prompt-shaped markers would overfit one generator's phrasing. The file says a leak under 200 characters should trigger adding markers. The quoted title is cut to 60 characters and passed through forTerminal before it reaches the message.

src/core/content-checks.ts.what: Per-rule static checks on UI microcopy: lorem ipsum, placeholder copy and names, vague link text, bare error codes, shouted caps, bare OK, Yes and No buttons, and similar. Each returns findings with a line number. allContentChecks is the one list every consumer composes from.
src/core/content-checks.ts.why: The rules are limited to ones with low false-positive rates on short imperative UI text. Prose linters are left out on purpose, because they misfire on microcopy.
src/core/content-checks.ts.gotcha: Some checks read raw HTML (placeholder-copy, placeholder-name, which also matches inside attributes) and others read visible text with tags stripped. plural-s-hack always reports line 1, because it searches visible text, which has no line positions.

src/core/designmd-parser.ts.what: A hand-rolled parser for DESIGN.md. It splits a file into its front-matter, body, ## headings and a nested YAML tree, without a YAML dependency.
src/core/designmd-parser.ts.why: The front-matter shape is narrow (groups, names, string values), so a small scanner is enough. Every audit family reads through it.
src/core/designmd-parser.ts.gotcha: It never throws: problems go into parseErrors, and callers must check that list before they walk the tree. Lines that do not match the key pattern, including list items and continuation lines, are skipped silently. An inline # starts a comment only when it follows whitespace, so a colour such as #fff is kept.

src/core/ds-guidelines-terminology-secti.what: Builds terminology.md for the DS guidelines pack from CONTEXT.md and the ontology glossary, and derives the map of avoided words that other checks use to reject synonyms.
src/core/ds-guidelines-terminology-secti.why: The pack tells a model which term to use and which words are rejected. The file header says CONTEXT.md wins when a term appears in both sources.
src/core/ds-guidelines-terminology-secti.gotcha: A glossary whose shape the flat reader cannot parse is skipped with a reason, never half-read. avoidedWords never lists a word that is itself a canonical term. Disagreements are returned as conflicts, which the file header says go into the manifest.

src/core/ds-kit-evidence.ts.what: Validates a kit's evidence receipt against its spec: the receipt's content hash must match the candidate, every required case must have passed with non-empty evidence files, and it returns the evidence files with their hashes.
src/core/ds-kit-evidence.ts.why: A kit is accepted only with a receipt that proves its own content. The stale check (KIT_EVIDENCE_STALE) stops a receipt for older content from certifying newer content.
src/core/ds-kit-evidence.ts.gotcha: The receipt's contentHash must be exactly the sha256-base64url form, or the check fails with KIT_FORMAT. Each evidence path must start with evidence/ and must not be the receipt itself. The returned list is sorted and hashed.

src/core/ds-soul-studio.ts.what: The studio soul, the layer above each project soul: the scaffold written to $EASE_DESIGN_HOME/studio-soul.md, a parser for the frontmatter name, a linter that adds a missing-name error to the project soul checks, and the context section cap.
src/core/ds-soul-studio.ts.why: A studio soul's name is baked into the agents generated for its products, so a studio soul without one is an error. The scaffold uses the same placeholder style the project linter already catches.
src/core/ds-soul-studio.ts.gotcha: An untouched scaffold name of <studio> counts as missing. writeStudioSoulScaffold never overwrites an existing file unless forced. soulName trims the value but does not normalise case or spaces.

src/core/figma-apply-mirror.ts.what: The mirror half of `ui figma reconcile --apply`: picks the captured node spec for a delta entry, or returns a named reason it has none, and builds a registry record for a newly captured component.
src/core/figma-apply-mirror.ts.why: Each captured component either lands in the registry with its real node definition or is reported as skipped with a reason. None disappears silently.
src/core/figma-apply-mirror.ts.gotcha: materialize writes an empty markup and an empty tokensUsed list on purpose: that is the shape Figma scans produce, and the node sidecar holds the real definition. The category is the text before the first slash, and a name with no slash is rejected by the validator.

src/core/knowledge-ledger-event.ts.what: The learning-ledger event contract: allowed types, sources and fields, a validator for one event, a linter for a whole ledger (duplicate ids, unclean events, counts by type), and the ruling-candidate event built from a draft ruling.
src/core/knowledge-ledger-event.ts.why: The validator is hand-written to mirror learning-event.schema.json, and a test pins its enums to the schema file, so the two cannot drift apart silently.
src/core/knowledge-ledger-event.ts.gotcha: correction and approval events must name an r-* ruling id in refs, or they fail ruling-ref-missing. Telemetry event kinds are rejected as out of scope. The ruling-candidate id is derived from the ruling id, so drafting the same ruling twice yields the same event id.

src/core/knowledge-ledger-write.ts.what: Appends one learning event to a JSON Lines ledger. It validates the event, refuses a whole-document ledger or a duplicate id, creates the file if needed, and never rewrites existing bytes.
src/core/knowledge-ledger-write.ts.why: The ledger is an audit trail, so the writer is append-only by design. A document-shaped file is refused rather than converted into lines.
src/core/knowledge-ledger-write.ts.gotcha: The duplicate-id check reads the whole file first and nothing locks it, so two concurrent writers can both pass the check. If the existing file lacks a final newline, one is added before the new line.

src/core/line-index.ts.what: Maps a UTF-16 offset to a 1-based line number through a newline index and binary search. The one-off lineOf helper keeps a two-entry cache keyed by the source text.
src/core/line-index.ts.why: Lint passes look up a line for every finding, and rescanning the source each time is quadratic. The results match the slice-and-split form exactly, including for negative and non-finite offsets.
src/core/line-index.ts.gotcha: The cache is module-global and keyed by full string equality. Sources over 256 KB are dropped from it on the next microtask, so memory is not held. clearLineIndexCache exists for tests and deterministic resets.

src/core/memory-context-render.ts.what: Renders the memory context within a UTF-8 byte budget. In JSON mode it drops optional fields in a fixed order (profile, prior, recalled) until the envelope fits. In text mode it keeps the required lessons and drops optional blocks from the end.
src/core/memory-context-render.ts.why: Accepted project lessons are required context and are never sliced. If they do not fit the budget, the command fails with CONTEXT_OVERFLOW and lists their ids.
src/core/memory-context-render.ts.gotcha: In JSON mode, complete stays true even when optional fields were dropped; omittedOptional is the field that shows the drop. In text mode the omission notice can itself push the output over budget, in which case only the required payload is returned.

src/core/token-coverage-extract.ts.what: Pulls colour, font-family, font-size, spacing, radius and shadow declarations out of a page's CSS by regex, skipping token-definition blocks (:root, @theme, data-theme, .dark), and records the line of each.
src/core/token-coverage-extract.ts.why: Coverage measures usage, not token literals. Excluding the definition blocks means defining a token does not count as a raw value in use.
src/core/token-coverage-extract.ts.gotcha: This is a regex scan, not a CSS parser, so anything the patterns do not match is silently not counted. The category patterns also run over inline style attributes that end in a semicolon. Results are sorted by line.

src/adapters/wrapper-shapes.ts.what: A facade that re-exports the deterministic string builders for each runtime's wrapper: the knowledge anchor, the init verb description, and the Claude, Antigravity and Codex blocks.
src/adapters/wrapper-shapes.ts.why: Adapters import from one module, so the builders can be split across files for size without changing any caller.
src/adapters/wrapper-shapes.ts.gotcha: It contains no logic. Each builder's behaviour lives in its own wrapper-shapes-* file.

src/commands/ds-status-impl.ts.what: `ui ds status`: prints a read-only summary of the design system's manifest: name, generation, persona, token and component counts, the status breakdown, the kit status, and a warning when the name is the import default.
src/commands/ds-status-impl.ts.why: The default name imported-ds becomes the identity of every agent generated from the store, so status warns about it. The warning is not an error, so existing stores keep working.
src/commands/ds-status-impl.ts.gotcha: The file says the warning literal must match the default in ds-import-impl.ts, but the two are separate literals kept in sync by hand. The JSON form carries the warning as a field; the text form prints it first.

src/commands/edit-strategy.ts.what: `ui edit-strategy` with three subcommands: select classifies a change request, number-lines prefixes each HTML line with its number, and apply patches an HTML file with an ln-diff (written in place only with --write).
src/commands/edit-strategy.ts.why: Lets a model make a targeted edit by quoting line ranges, not by regenerating the whole page. A failed match returns the nearest window for each unmatched chunk, so the model can repair the diff once before a full regeneration.
src/commands/edit-strategy.ts.gotcha: Stdin can be read only once, so the HTML and the diff cannot both be '-'. Without --write the patched HTML goes to stdout and the summary to stderr. A diff with zero parsed chunks is BAD_DIFF, not an empty success.

src/commands/knowledge-ledger-append.ts.what: `ui knowledge ledger append <events.jsonl> --event <json>`: parses the --event JSON and hands it to the append-only ledger writer, then prints whether the file was created or appended to.
src/commands/knowledge-ledger-append.ts.why: A thin shell over appendLedgerEvent. It owns the flag parsing and the output shape, and the validation lives in the writer.
src/commands/knowledge-ledger-append.ts.gotcha: Invalid --event JSON is refused as BAD_JSON before any schema check. The writer's own codes (BAD_EVENT, DUPLICATE_ID, LEDGER_NOT_JSONL) pass through unchanged.

src/commands/knowledge-rulings-render.ts.what: `ui knowledge render <rulings.json> --out <dir> [--lang en,vi]`: writes one rulings.<lang>.md per requested language into the output directory.
src/commands/knowledge-rulings-render.ts.why: Produces the human-readable rulings in each language. The blocker check runs before anything is written, so an invalid rulings file never produces output.
src/commands/knowledge-rulings-render.ts.gotcha: Languages are validated before the file is read, and the default is en. Files are written one language at a time, so a write failure part-way leaves the earlier language files on disk.

src/commands/memory-record-impl.ts.what: `ui memory record <type> --data <json>`: validates the event, builds it, appends it to the memory ledger, then recompiles the projection and updates the project registry. The same file also holds `compile` and `fingerprint`.
src/commands/memory-record-impl.ts.why: The ledger is the source of truth; compile rebuilds the view from it. The event is built with an empty id, and the id that appendEvent returns is the one reported.
src/commands/memory-record-impl.ts.gotcha: A failure after the append is reported as committed (committed:true, MEMORY_COMMITTED), and the message tells the caller not to repeat the record but to run compile. --no-registry skips only the registry update.

src/commands/tokens.ts.what: `ui tokens compile <file.json> [--target css|tailwind|figma]`: parses a DTCG token file, resolves its aliases, and prints the chosen target to stdout. With --json it returns all three targets in one envelope.
src/commands/tokens.ts.why: The single entry point that turns a token file into CSS, a Tailwind @theme block or Figma JSON. Cycles, dangling aliases and type mismatches come back as typed error codes.
src/commands/tokens.ts.gotcha: An unknown --target is refused only in text mode; with --json the flag is ignored, not checked. The Figma JSON is re-parsed for the envelope and falls back to the raw string if it does not parse.

src/commands/vr.ts.what: `ui vr diff | gate | accept`: visual regression over PNGs the host has already rendered. diff compares two images, gate compares every baseline with the same-named current render, and accept copies renders over the baselines.
src/commands/vr.ts.why: The binary never renders, so the comparison depends only on the files. Masks let known dynamic regions be ignored.
src/commands/vr.ts.gotcha: --max-ratio defaults to 0, so any changed pixel is a regression unless the caller sets a ratio. The help text says a size or missing mismatch is a regression, while a render with no baseline is 'new' and not a failure. accept overwrites baselines by file name without asking.

src/core/a11y-checks.ts.what: Per-rule static HTML accessibility checks: image alt text, html lang, document title, positive tabindex, zoom blocking, viewport meta, unnamed icon controls, blocked paste, and heading hierarchy. Two focus and label checks are re-exported from a sibling module.
src/core/a11y-checks.ts.why: Regex-based and precision-first: a rule fires only when the markup alone shows the violation. Some rules are shared with the layout validator, so each lives here once.
src/core/a11y-checks.ts.gotcha: html lang and document title skip redirect stubs. A paste blocker is an error when an onpaste attribute cancels the event, but only a warning for a scripted listener, because a regex cannot prove runtime behaviour. A handler that touches clipboard data is treated as a re-insert and exempt.

src/core/delivery/delivery-learning-vali.what: Validates a v1 learning record: the benchmark identifiers, the trials (each must be blinded and controlled, with the four workflow variants), per-variant scores, and the art-direction and convergence checks it delegates to other modules.
src/core/delivery/delivery-learning-vali.why: A learning record claims a workflow improved the output. The validator refuses trials that were not blinded or that lack a comparison variant, so an uncontrolled comparison cannot count as evidence.
src/core/delivery/delivery-learning-vali.gotcha: Ceiling scores must be integers from 0 to 10 on all seven axes. An art-directed variant needs section-level board evidence. The validator checks the record's shape and completeness; it does not judge the scores themselves.

src/core/delivery/delivery-v2-brief-vali.what: Validates a v2 design brief: the v1 base checks, plus an activation reference that must resolve to a successful knowledge-activate envelope. The envelope is then replayed against the installed capability catalog.
src/core/delivery/delivery-v2-brief-vali.why: A marketing brief proceeds only on a capability that is qualified and routed as web-marketing, generate, html. The replay stops a receipt that was edited after the fact from passing.
src/core/delivery/delivery-v2-brief-vali.gotcha: If the catalog or its digest is missing, the function returns early with activation-catalog-unavailable and the replay never runs. Both v1 receipts (disposition QUALIFIED) and v2 receipts (ROUTED, QUALIFIED, QUALIFIED_DELIVERY_ALLOWED) are accepted as qualified.

src/core/delivery/delivery-v2-contract-v.what: Validates a v2 generation contract: the v1 base checks, plus asset provenance, responsive viewports and adaptations, motion tier and fallbacks, custom controls with their states and keyboard operations, composition, and section architecture (delegated).
src/core/delivery/delivery-v2-contract-v.why: The contract is what the generator must follow. These checks make a missing accessibility or fallback behaviour a validation failure before generation starts.
src/core/delivery/delivery-v2-contract-v.gotcha: An icon set other than Phosphor needs an exception with a reason and an evidenceRef. An image that contains essential text is refused. Reduced motion must be static-complete, and the content must be visible without JavaScript. The v1 base checks still run first.

src/core/delivery/delivery-v2-qualificat.what: Validates a v2 qualification record: the v1 base checks, then the asset, responsive, motion, control, composition and section-review evidence. The evidence is cross-checked against the generation contract the record references.
src/core/delivery/delivery-v2-qualificat.why: A QUALIFIED v2 record must show evidence for every asset, viewport and custom control its contract requires. A record with no referenced contract is an error whatever its status.
src/core/delivery/delivery-v2-qualificat.gotcha: The contract cross-checks for assets, viewports and controls run only when status is QUALIFIED. A referenced contract that is not version 2 fails contract-version-mismatch and stops the contract checks.

src/core/ds-context-roles.ts.what: Builds the Roles and Missing roles sections of `ds context` from the role annotation already stored on each token.
src/core/ds-context-roles.ts.why: It reads the stored design-os.role annotation rather than recomputing recognition, so a manual `ds set-role` correction is kept. The file header says a recomputation would silently discard it.
src/core/ds-context-roles.ts.gotcha: It returns null when no token carries a role, and both sections are then omitted, not guessed. An annotation whose value is not a canonical role is skipped without a message.

src/core/extractors/html/css-cascade.ts.what: Resolves a document's CSS cascade into the winning declaration for each element. Selectors are matched against the parsed DOM and ordered by !important, specificity and source order; inline style attributes come last.
src/core/extractors/html/css-cascade.ts.why: Regex linters cannot tell which rule wins for which element. Matching against the DOM gives the value that will actually render, which is what the tell and layout rules need.
src/core/extractors/html/css-cascade.ts.gotcha: @media blocks are collected but not applied unless a caller asks for that condition. Selectors that css-select cannot handle are reported in unsupportedSelectors, not guessed. Remote stylesheets are never fetched. The header says shorthands are not expanded, but declarationsOf expands them into longhands, so that header is stale.

src/core/figma-ds-designdoc.ts.what: Builds the DESIGN.md text for an ingested Figma design system: tokens split into primitives and semantic aliases, the component table, icons rolled up into one note, screen frames listed apart, and the local styles.
src/core/figma-ds-designdoc.ts.why: Gives a portable, human- and AI-readable spec of the design system, separate from the machine registry. The builder has no clock and no filesystem, so the same input gives the same document.
src/core/figma-ds-designdoc.ts.gotcha: A token counts as semantic only when its whole value is a {alias}. Dark-mode overrides from $extensions are appended to the value cell. Screen frames are kept out of the component list on purpose.

src/core/figma-reconcile.ts.what: The public surface of the Figma reconcile core: it re-exports the on-disk contract types, the change-log parser, the change coalescer and the preview delta.
src/core/figma-reconcile.ts.why: Consumers keep one import path while the logic is split across focused modules.
src/core/figma-reconcile.ts.gotcha: It has no behaviour of its own. TypeScript rejects a name that two of the four re-exported modules both export, so the facade would fail to compile rather than pick one.

src/core/html-autofix.ts.what: The registered deterministic HTML autofix rules and runAutofix, which runs all nine in sequence and reports the ones that changed the HTML.
src/core/html-autofix.ts.why: Mechanical HTML problems get fixed without a model call. Every rule is a pure string transform that is gated by its own check.
src/core/html-autofix.ts.gotcha: runAutofix records a rule only when its applied flag is set, so a rule that changes the HTML without setting the flag goes unreported. The comment above runAutofix says the rules run 'all five', but the registry holds nine, so that comment is stale. viewport-meta inserts after the <head> tag, so a page with no <head> is left untouched.

src/core/knowledge-promotion-gate.ts.what: Decides which live rulings are candidates for promotion to the shared knowledge core. A ruling qualifies on recurrence in the ledger, on corroboration by enough distinct source documents, or on both.
src/core/knowledge-promotion-gate.ts.why: Keeps promotion evidence-based instead of a manual judgment call.
src/core/knowledge-promotion-gate.ts.gotcha: For learning events only refs[] count toward recurrence; free text that mentions an id does not. Rulings that are not active are counted as notLive, not as candidates. The considered count is the usable rulings minus the notLive ones.

src/core/ksync-cli-io.ts.what: Shared IO and error helpers for the three `ui ksync` subcommands: a coded error class, a JSON file reader, and readers for string and required flags.
src/core/ksync-cli-io.ts.why: Every failure gets a code and a line saying what to do next, and the output is the same JSON or text in each subcommand.
src/core/ksync-cli-io.ts.gotcha: readJsonFile reports every read failure as FILE_NOT_FOUND, including permission errors, so that code can mislead. A bare --flag with no value is a BAD_ARG, not an empty string.

src/core/ksync-pins.ts.what: The ksync pins record: which Figma frame each built route was built against. It provides parsing, validation, upsert and serialization, all pure.
src/core/ksync-pins.ts.why: A pin is keyed by its file and node, not by its route, so a route with several states owns one pin per frame. Serialization uses a fixed key order, so the same pins always produce the same bytes.
src/core/ksync-pins.ts.gotcha: parsePins rejects unknown fields, duplicate file-and-node pairs, and a pinnedAt that does not parse as a date. upsertPin replaces the whole matching pin, so its route and builtFrom are overwritten by the new values.

src/core/layout-checks-hover.ts.what: The sticky-hover-unguarded warning: flags CSS :hover rules that sit outside an @media (hover: hover) guard on a document that shows mobile intent. It reports one finding with a count.
src/core/layout-checks-hover.ts.why: On a touch screen a tapped control keeps its :hover style and looks selected. The guard is the standard fix.
src/core/layout-checks-hover.ts.gotcha: Tailwind hover: classes are never flagged, because the framework guards them. The header lists a known limit where a brace inside a CSS string closes the guard early, but the check now blanks string literals before the brace walk, so that limit looks stale and was not reproduced.

src/core/memory-lesson-context.ts.what: Selects the lessons that apply to a memory-context call: accepted lessons on the current design-system revision, in scope for the requested targets, and with evidence that still verifies. It counts the exclusions by reason and parses the target list (CSV or JSON).
src/core/memory-lesson-context.ts.why: Lifecycle replay and current validity are kept apart. A lesson accepted under an older design system is excluded from context, not deleted from the ledger.
src/core/memory-lesson-context.ts.gotcha: With no verified design system, every requested target throws, and every accepted lesson is counted as staleRevision. Evidence is re-verified on every selection, not cached.

src/core/memory-seed-batch.ts.what: Seeds a batch of memory events. Each event is appended as it is produced, then the projection is compiled. If a later step fails, the events already committed are reported by id.
src/core/memory-seed-batch.ts.why: A seed that fails part-way must not be retried from the start, because the events already committed would be written twice. The error tells the owner not to repeat the seed.
src/core/memory-seed-batch.ts.gotcha: If nothing was committed, the original error is rethrown unchanged. When fewer events than expected were committed, the message tells the owner to append only the reviewed missing events.

src/core/token-import.ts.what: Converts a flat token file (category, then name, then value) into the DTCG shape the design store expects. It infers each leaf's $type from its value and from its category or name. Leaves it cannot type are skipped and reported.
src/core/token-import.ts.why: Lets a flat tokens file from a Figma or CSS ingest enter the design store. Skipping is deliberate: a token with an invented $type is never emitted.
src/core/token-import.ts.gotcha: Nested groups are hoisted into a category named <category>-<sub>. A leaf that is already DTCG passes through with its $extensions. A bare number becomes px only when its category or name looks dimensional. An alias with no literal to test is typed from a name hint and defaults to color.

src/adapters/template-catalogue-read.ts.what: Reads a template's description and recorded source hash from schemas/template-descriptions.json, instead of parsing template Markdown at runtime.
src/adapters/template-catalogue-read.ts.why: The kernel must not parse template Markdown at runtime, so the audited catalogue is the source. The file's comments say the catalogue hash is the right value to record, but not for the doctor drift check, which must hash the live bytes.
src/adapters/template-catalogue-read.ts.gotcha: A missing or unparseable catalogue throws, with the command that regenerates it. The hash read throws for a path that is not a registered template, while the description read returns null for it. The cache lives for the process.

src/adapters/wrapper-shapes-antigravity..what: Builds the Antigravity workflow wrapper (.agent/workflows/ui-<verb>.md) and the skill wrapper. Activation-only workflows get a capability-activation step instead of the schema check.
src/adapters/wrapper-shapes-antigravity..why: Each runtime's wrapper tells the host agent how to run a verb. The text is generated from the verb and template, not written by hand.
src/adapters/wrapper-shapes-antigravity..gotcha: A verb with no template path gets the init instructions rather than an error, so a missing template looks like an init step. The Antigravity skill is delegated to the Claude builder, so a change there changes both.

src/commands/brief-questions.ts.what: `ui brief questions <questions.json> --format claude|markdown`: parses a questions document and prints either a JSON payload for a host model (claude, the default) or a Markdown gap sheet.
src/commands/brief-questions.ts.why: One source file serves both a model and a human-readable gap sheet, so the two cannot drift apart.
src/commands/brief-questions.ts.gotcha: A file that is not valid JSON and a file that cannot be read both report the same message, cannot read as JSON, and differ only in code (BAD_JSON or FILE_NOT_FOUND).

src/commands/design-principles-index.ts.what: `ui design principles-index <principles.md> --out <principles.json> [--check]`: builds a JSON index of a principles file. With --check it compares the existing index byte for byte with what it would write, and exits 1 on drift.
src/commands/design-principles-index.ts.why: Lets a CI step catch an index that has fallen behind its markdown source.
src/commands/design-principles-index.ts.gotcha: --check never writes, and a missing index counts as a failure. Problems in the markdown stop the command with BAD_PRINCIPLES before the drift check runs.

src/commands/ingest-css-ds.ts.what: `ui ingest-css-ds <extract-tokens.json>`: compiles the custom properties from `ui designmd extract-tokens` into an unsealed tokens.json. Literals become primitives, var() aliases become semantics, and each theme selector becomes a mode.
src/commands/ingest-css-ds.ts.why: The CSS path of the design-system ingest. It is deterministic and needs no network, and the output is sealed later by ui ds import.
src/commands/ingest-css-ds.ts.gotcha: LEAF_COLLISION fails the whole run when two source properties map to the same token path. --name is only recorded in the JSON summary and defaults to the output directory's name. The command writes only tokens.json, never a manifest.

src/commands/knowledge-effect-matrix.ts.what: `ui knowledge effect-matrix`: reads knowledge/canvas-ui/catalog.json and prints the emitted effect matrix as markdown.
src/commands/knowledge-effect-matrix.ts.why: The matrix is generated from the ledger. The command prints only: writing into the direction file would overwrite its hand-written cells.
src/commands/knowledge-effect-matrix.ts.gotcha: A missing catalog is NO_LEDGER. A JSON parse error in the catalog is swallowed by the read that extracts captured, and only surfaces later as BAD_LEDGER from the emitter.

src/commands/knowledge-gradient-matrix.t.what: `ui knowledge gradient-matrix`: reads knowledge/shader-gradient/catalog.json and prints the emitted gradient matrix as markdown.
src/commands/knowledge-gradient-matrix.t.why: Same reason as the effect matrix. The refusal and fallback cells are hand-written in the direction file, so the command never writes there.
src/commands/knowledge-gradient-matrix.t.gotcha: Same as effect-matrix: a catalog parse error is swallowed by the captured read and surfaces later as BAD_LEDGER from the emitter.

src/commands/knowledge-ledger-run.ts.what: The dispatcher for `ui knowledge ledger`. It routes the lint and append verbs to their own modules and returns a usage error for any other verb.
src/commands/knowledge-ledger-run.ts.why: Keeps the two learning-ledger verbs under one command name, so the contract is documented in one place (LEDGER_HELP).
src/commands/knowledge-ledger-run.ts.gotcha: The verb is the first positional and the file is the second. Running the command with no verb returns the usage message as BAD_ARG.

src/commands/knowledge-rulings-lint.ts.what: `ui knowledge lint <rulings.json> [--root]`: runs the rulings linter over one file, checking that each anchored path exists under --root (default: the working directory). Exits 1 on any error-severity finding.
src/commands/knowledge-rulings-lint.ts.why: Catches a ruling whose anchor has moved or whose record is malformed before the ruling is trusted.
src/commands/knowledge-rulings-lint.ts.gotcha: Every finding that is not an error counts as a warning. A file that cannot be read is reported as FILE_NOT_FOUND whatever the actual cause was.

src/commands/ksync-pin.ts.what: `ui ksync pin <route> --file <key> --node <id>`: records, or updates, the pin that says which Figma frame a built route was built against. It stamps the time and the commit.
src/commands/ksync-pin.ts.why: Makes the link between a built route and its design frame explicit, so the census and the drift check can compare them later.
src/commands/ksync-pin.ts.gotcha: Without --commit the command runs git rev-parse HEAD in the working directory, and outside a repository it fails with BAD_ARG. Without --at the timestamp is the current time, so pinning the same frame again changes pinnedAt. An existing pins file that does not parse stops the command; it is never overwritten.

src/commands/memory-query-impl.ts.what: `ui memory query` filters raw ledger events by type, design and persona, newest first, with a default limit of 20. `ui memory status` reports the event count, graph freshness, the registry size and whether a profile exists. Both are read-only.
src/commands/memory-query-impl.ts.why: Lets an owner inspect the memory ledger without compiling anything.
src/commands/memory-query-impl.ts.gotcha: status never fails on a broken ledger: it reports the event count as -1. query does fail, with the ledger's own error code. --limit is read with parseInt, so a value such as 5abc is accepted as 5.

src/commands/product-context-io.ts.what: Shared IO for the product-context commands: bounded file reads with a ceiling per input kind (receipts 128 KB, compile input 512 KB, atlas 2 MB), strict UTF-8 decoding, argument-count checks, failure results in JSON or text, and per-file receipt decoding that names the file that failed.
src/commands/product-context-io.ts.why: A bounded read refuses an oversized input before it is parsed. Decoding one file at a time lets the operator see which receipt is bad, not just that one of them is.
src/commands/product-context-io.ts.gotcha: The read stops one byte past the limit, so an oversized file is detected without reading all of it. For a regular file the size is checked before any read. The terminal channel escapes its message through forTerminal, while JSON carries the raw string.

src/commands/taste-ingest-impl.ts.what: `ui taste ingest`: scans taste/inbox/<genre>/ and any --dir sources for PNG and JPEG images, skips exact duplicates by sha256, warns about near-duplicates by PNG dHash within a genre, and adds the rest to the corpus and the item ledger.
src/commands/taste-ingest-impl.ts.why: Builds the comparison corpus without duplicates, and never destroys originals: inbox files are moved, while --dir sources are copied.
src/commands/taste-ingest-impl.ts.gotcha: Inbox files are moved, so the inbox is emptied as the command runs. Near-duplicates are warnings only and the file is still added. A file that cannot be read during the scan throws out of the command rather than being reported in the result.

src/commands/taste-lint.ts.what: `ui taste-lint <file.html> [--tokens]`: runs the machine-checkable part of the taste rubric over one generated HTML file, after linked CSS has been inlined. It exits 1 on error-severity findings only.
src/commands/taste-lint.ts.why: The binary floor under the model's self-critique. A breach it flags is one the model cannot argue its way past.
src/commands/taste-lint.ts.gotcha: An unreadable linked stylesheet becomes a Consistency error finding. A --tokens file that cannot be read or holds no hex colours is ignored without a message, because the caller passes undefined on any failure. The run also passes through withOutcome to record the outcome.

src/commands/taste-next-impl.ts.what: `ui taste next --mode pair|study [--genre]`: proposes the next pair to compare, or the next item not yet studied. Read-only.
src/commands/taste-next-impl.ts.why: Lets a reviewer work through the corpus in an order chosen by the ranking, not by hand.
src/commands/taste-next-impl.ts.gotcha: Without a taste store it returns E_TASTE_ROOT. An item with no votes is reported at the default Elo of 1000. Only study mode loads the study ledger; pair mode never reads it.

src/commands/taste-record-impl.ts.what: `ui taste record --mode pair|study`: validates one pair vote or one study verdict and appends it to the matching ledger.
src/commands/taste-record-impl.ts.why: Keeps the taste ledgers well-formed, since every line is checked before it is written.
src/commands/taste-record-impl.ts.gotcha: The command checks that the two ids differ and that both exist, but it never checks whether the same pair was already voted on. Repeats are accepted, and only the optional --repeat-of flag links them.

src/commands/taste-status-impl.ts.what: `ui taste status [--genre]`: reports the item, vote and study counts, the item and vote count for each genre, the five highest-rated items, self-consistency on repeated votes, and the next unstudied item.
src/commands/taste-status-impl.ts.why: Gives a one-screen view of how far the taste corpus has been judged and how consistent the judgments are.
src/commands/taste-status-impl.ts.gotcha: The Elo ratings are computed over all items and all votes, even when --genre narrows the output, so a scoped view can show ratings that depend on votes from outside the genre. Self-consistency reads n/a until a pair has been repeated.

src/core/a11y-checks-focus-and-labels.ts.what: Two checks: input-unlabeled (an error under WCAG 3.3.2) flags a text control with no programmatic label, and focus-outline-removed (an error under WCAG 2.4.7) flags a focus rule that removes the outline with no visible replacement anywhere in the document.
src/core/a11y-checks-focus-and-labels.ts.why: A control with no label, or with no visible focus, blocks screen-reader and keyboard users. Both checks read only markup, not prose or code samples, so the findings stay precise.
src/core/a11y-checks-focus-and-labels.ts.gotcha: The focus check is document-wide: one replacement anywhere clears the finding, so a ring on a shared selector can hide a removal elsewhere. A placeholder never counts as a label. Programmatic focus targets with tabindex -1 are exempt. Node references use the id or name, so they stay stable when lines move above them.

src/core/capability-pilot-receipt.ts.what: The identity contract for retained capability pilots: the expected receipt for each registered pilot (native-macos, native-ios, native-ipados), the parser for a pin of the form knowledge/...#sha256, and a byte-exact check of a receipt and its source evidence.
src/core/capability-pilot-receipt.ts.why: An activation must match the retained pilot exactly. A receipt with edited fields, or a file that has moved, fails verification.
src/core/capability-pilot-receipt.ts.gotcha: A pin is checked against the digest of the exact stored bytes, so any edit to a pilot file, even whitespace, breaks verification. Symbolic links are refused before the path is resolved. The file's comment says these are identity contracts, not qualifications, and the iOS and iPadOS pilots still record pending-owner-review.

src/core/color-roles.ts.what: Classifies colour token names into design roles (primary, secondary, accent, success, warning, danger, info, neutral) by keyword, and builds an 11-stop OKLCH scale for each role.
src/core/color-roles.ts.why: Turns a set of named colour tokens into a usable palette without a person choosing the roles.
src/core/color-roles.ts.gotcha: Classification uses the name alone, and the first matching keyword wins, with primary checked first, so primary-danger is primary. A name containing baseline is not primary. generateSemanticPalette keeps only the first colour for each role, and generateScalesFromTokens drops colours whose chroma is below 0.01.

src/core/content-checks-voice.ts.what: Four advisory checks on generated prose: generic SaaS buzzwords, theatrical intensifiers, the 'not just X, it's Y' cadence, and em-dash overuse measured per 100 words. They read text facts only, and head metadata is excluded.
src/core/content-checks-voice.ts.why: These habits mark machine-written copy. They are advisory because each one is a smell, not a defect.
src/core/content-checks-voice.ts.gotcha: The em-dash rate counts every visible text run, headings included. The file records that limiting it to body text was tried and rejected, because the verdict then depended on which tag an author used. All four findings are advisory, so none of them fails a gate.

src/core/css-selector-mode.ts.what: A shared table that classifies a CSS selector as base (:root, html, body, @theme), as a named theme mode (data-theme, .dark, prefers-color-scheme: dark), or as unmapped.
src/core/css-selector-mode.ts.why: Keeps token ingest and token coverage agreeing on what counts as a token definition.
src/core/css-selector-mode.ts.gotcha: A selector list is base if any part is base. Otherwise the parts that are theme modes are kept and every other part is dropped silently, so '.dark, .btn' reads as mode dark alone and the .btn part disappears without a message.

src/core/design-dir-lint.ts.what: lintDesignDir applies the rules for the design/ folder layout: one token source, no second token file unless it is declared derived, the required files present, logs and caches not tracked, art direction inside design/art-direction, supersession recorded only in rulings, the principles index in sync, and stale ingests.
src/core/design-dir-lint.ts.why: Turns the folder contract into checks, so the layout can be verified instead of remembered.
src/core/design-dir-lint.ts.gotcha: The git rules are skipped with a warning when the project root is not its own repository. The log and cache checks apply only under design/. The stale-ingest check compares file modification times, which a fresh checkout resets, so it can fire on a clean clone.

src/core/design-facts/role-synthesis.ts.what: Derives card, icon and section roles for each structure fact from the facts around it (shadow, border, radius, own background, tag), instead of from class names.
src/core/design-facts/role-synthesis.ts.why: Name matching gave false positives (card-title counted as a card) and misses (a Tailwind surface with no card in its name). The file records the measurements that led to this design.
src/core/design-facts/role-synthesis.ts.gotcha: The card predicate is deliberately generous, and the rules carry the discrimination. Control tags such as button, input and kbd never count as cards. A card role never comes from a name claim, while icon and section roles can. An inline SVG is an icon from its tag alone.

src/core/design-facts/rule-requirements..what: The requirement contract: each rule declares the fact kinds it needs and, optionally, the minimum confidence. partition() splits the rules into runnable and not-evaluated for one extractor, and coverageMatrix() builds the full rule-by-extractor table.
src/core/design-facts/rule-requirements..why: A rule the extractor cannot feed is reported as not evaluated, never as a pass. That is what keeps 'I cannot see it' from reading as 'it is clean'.
src/core/design-facts/rule-requirements..gotcha: The default minimum confidence is heuristic, so any fact satisfies a rule unless the rule sets a stricter one. partition() checks only that the two buckets add up to the input length, so a rule listed twice is counted twice and not caught.

src/core/designmd-audit-types.ts.what: Shared types for the five DESIGN.md audit families: the row (family, rule, status, detail, optional fix), the aggregate result with per-family timings, and worstOf, which combines statuses.
src/core/designmd-audit-types.ts.why: Every family produces the same row shape, so one report can render all of them.
