src/core/designmd-audit-types.ts.gotcha: Exit codes come from the worst status: 0 for all PASS, 1 for any FAIL, and 2 for WARN with no FAIL. Code 2 is not the usual error code, so a caller that treats any non-zero as failure will read a WARN-only audit as a failure.

src/core/ds-guidelines-budget.ts.what: The bundle model for the Figma guidelines pack: sections of units, their rendering to markdown, and trimming to a byte budget in a fixed priority order (grammar, terminology, overview, apps, rulings). Every dropped unit is reported by id.
src/core/ds-guidelines-budget.ts.why: A guidelines pack has to fit a size budget without losing hard rules silently. Anti-patterns, vocabulary and components are never trimmed.
src/core/ds-guidelines-budget.ts.gotcha: The budget is not always reached: trimToBudget returns reached false once only untrimmable content is left. Rulings are dropped oldest first by their since date, and a unit with no date counts as the oldest. A file whose trimmable sections are all emptied is left out of the bundle.

src/core/ds-guidelines-lint-slots.ts.what: Lints the slots in one rendered guidelines file. A partly answered slot (some of Do, Don't and Why) is an error. An unanswered slot is a warning. Host-written text that cites a knowledge file without a gap id, or with a gap id the pack did not measure, is a warning.
src/core/ds-guidelines-lint-slots.ts.why: Knowledge enters the pack only as the answer to a measured gap, and these checks enforce that rule.
src/core/ds-guidelines-lint-slots.ts.gotcha: When no manifest could be read, gapIds is undefined and the unmeasured-gap check is skipped, while the missing-id check still runs. A wholly empty slot is only a warning, because the canonical pack allows open questions; a partly filled one is an error.

src/core/ds-guidelines-rulings-reader.ts.what: Reads the owner rulings file and sorts each ruling into a tier: superseded (never emitted), process (C, excluded), app-scoped (B), global in a design category (A), or other global (AOther).
src/core/ds-guidelines-rulings-reader.ts.why: Process rulings describe how the team works, not how the library is used, so they stay out of the pack. Superseded rulings must not be followed.
src/core/ds-guidelines-rulings-reader.ts.gotcha: A ruling is superseded only when its text opens with a (SUPERSEDED marker, in any case, before the matching closing parenthesis. The same word later in a text is a mention. Superseded is checked before the category, so a superseded process ruling counts as superseded. An unknown category falls to AOther, never dropped.

src/core/ds-guidelines-rulings-sections..what: Builds rulings.md (tier A and the other library-wide rulings) and one apps/<app>.md per app (tier B). Each file has one heading per category and one line per ruling. Tier C and superseded rulings are counted in the stats, not written.
src/core/ds-guidelines-rulings-sections..why: Each emitted ruling is a decision the library must follow. The excluded ones are counted with their source file, so nothing disappears without a trace.
src/core/ds-guidelines-rulings-sections..gotcha: A ruling scoped to several apps is written into each of those apps' files. That is intended, and it is not a duplicate. Rule ids are kept unique across all the files with one shared set.

src/core/extractors/scanner/line-scanner.what: The shared base for the SwiftUI, Flutter and JSX extractors. It blanks comments and string bodies while keeping every byte offset, builds a line index, reads numbers and hex colours, and names the values it cannot resolve.
src/core/extractors/scanner/line-scanner.why: One base, so comment handling and number reading are not copied per language, where the copies would drift apart. A value the scanner cannot resolve is counted by name, never guessed.
src/core/extractors/scanner/line-scanner.gotcha: The quotes stay but the string body is blanked, so a string value cannot be read at this stage. The hash-comment option is off unless asked for, so a language with # comments must pass it. An unclosed string blanks to the end of the file.

src/core/flow-model.ts.what: The shape of the flow artefact: screens with their data-lifecycle states, transitions between them, and entry points. parseFlow validates the structure and rejects duplicate screen and transition ids. splitNode splits a screen.state reference.
src/core/flow-model.ts.why: A flow is the smallest true model of a multi-screen design, so its shape must be strict before the graph checks run.
src/core/flow-model.ts.gotcha: Guards are declared for linting and handoff but never executed, by design. A screen with no states gets an implicit default state. Malformed optional fields (name, mode, label, guard) are dropped silently, while malformed required fields throw. Pointer states such as hover and focus are not flow nodes.

src/core/html-autofix-floor-repairs.ts.what: Three deterministic repairs for interface-craft floors: wrap unguarded :hover rules in @media (hover: hover), add tabular figures to numeric table columns, and restore the focus ring. Each rewrites only CSS or the class attribute, never copy text.
src/core/html-autofix-floor-repairs.ts.why: Each repair runs only when its own checker flags the document, and both use the same masking, so the checker can confirm the fix. A repair the checker cannot confirm would fix nothing.
src/core/html-autofix-floor-repairs.ts.gotcha: The hover repair skips a rule whose selector contains a semicolon, or whose comma-separated parts are not all :hover, and reports those as misses. The table repair never reuses an existing style block and does nothing when there is no head. The focus repair leaves programmatic focus targets (tabindex -1) alone.

src/core/knowledge-promotion-freshness.t.what: For each live ruling, works out its age in days since verified_at (falling back to since) and whether its repo-path source anchors still exist. The verdict is fresh, stale or unanchored. It reads no files: the caller supplies pathExists.
src/core/knowledge-promotion-freshness.t.why: Rulings go stale, and an anchor that no longer exists means the evidence behind the ruling is gone.
src/core/knowledge-promotion-freshness.t.gotcha: A ruling with no valid date is stale even when its anchors are fine. An invalid verified_at falls back to since. Only repo-path sources are checked against the disk; other source strings are ignored. Ages are whole days measured from the asOf date the caller passes.

src/core/knowledge-promotion-ledger.ts.what: Parses a learning ledger that is either JSON Lines or a JSON document with an array under entries, events, items or records.
src/core/knowledge-promotion-ledger.ts.why: Both shapes exist in real projects. Lines that cannot be read are counted, never dropped silently.
src/core/knowledge-promotion-ledger.ts.gotcha: A file whose every non-empty line is unreadable returns null, meaning it is not a ledger. A file with some unreadable lines returns the rest, with skippedLines set. A single JSON object with none of the array keys is treated as one record. Blank input is an empty ledger.

src/core/png-codec.ts.what: A zero-dependency PNG decoder and encoder for the visual-regression command, built only on node:zlib. It decodes non-interlaced 8-bit gray, RGB, RGBA and palette images into RGBA, and encodes RGBA as colour type 6.
src/core/png-codec.ts.why: Lets ui vr compare screenshots without an image library.
src/core/png-codec.ts.gotcha: Interlaced PNGs and bit depths other than 8 are refused with a message rather than decoded wrongly. The decoder does not verify chunk CRCs, and it ignores tRNS transparency, so gray and palette images come out fully opaque. The encoder writes filter 0 on every row, which makes the output larger than a filtered encoder would.

src/core/registry-shards.ts.what: Sharded storage for the component registry: one JSON file per component under design/registry/shards, plus an index that holds a hash per entry. writeShards writes only the shards whose content changed. registryFromShards rebuilds the registry from them.
src/core/registry-shards.ts.why: A registry change rewrites one shard instead of the whole file. A corrupt index is treated as absent rather than trusted.
src/core/registry-shards.ts.gotcha: The contract file component-registry.json is still written, and loadRegistry still reads only that file. An index with any malformed entry is discarded whole, so the next save reprocesses every component. When the index is missing or corrupt, orphan shards are reported but never deleted. Two names that share a slug would write to the same shard file, and the code does not check for that.

src/core/seam-model.ts.what: Builds a static model of one JS or TS source for the seam linter: its bindings (const, let, var, destructuring, arrow helpers), functions with their parameters and returns, call sites, and imports by local name. visibleBinding resolves a name through the scope chain.
src/core/seam-model.ts.why: Lets the seam scan trace where a path flows into a read without running any of the scanned code.
src/core/seam-model.ts.gotcha: This is a bounded analysis that follows bindings and parameters within one file. Type-only imports are skipped. A name with no visible binding resolves to nothing, and the trace stops there.

src/core/seam-scan.ts.what: Finds the file reads in the scanned sources (readFileSync, readFile, open and openSync) whose path argument resolves to a prose file, and returns the file, line, call text and resolved paths for each.
src/core/seam-scan.ts.why: The seam lint needs to know which code reads prose files, so that each such read can be allowed or flagged.
src/core/seam-scan.ts.gotcha: Opens that are write-only (w, wx, a, ax) are excluded. A path that resolves to nothing is dropped without a message, so an unresolvable read cannot be seen. The module never executes scanned code and never reads the prose itself.

src/core/tell-rules-rendered.ts.what: The seven rules that need a real browser render: content hidden at rest, text overflow, text occlusion, broken image, script error, first-viewport column overflow, and body text at the viewport edge. They are pure functions of the capture, so they can be tested on fixtures.
src/core/tell-rules-rendered.ts.why: Static analysis cannot see a blank page caused by an entrance animation that never fires. Only a settled render shows that copy is in the DOM but not on screen.
src/core/tell-rules-rendered.ts.gotcha: Three rules are errors (content hidden at rest, broken image, script error) and four are advisory. Text occlusion flags only text larger than 100 px² that is fully inside an opaque element, and it reports one finding per text node. These rules run only against a rendered capture, which the coverage matrix lists separately.

src/adapters/wrapper-shapes-claude.ts.what: Builds the Claude command wrapper (.claude/commands/ui/<verb>.md) and the Claude skill wrapper (SKILL.md) for each verb.
src/adapters/wrapper-shapes-claude.ts.why: Tells the host how to run each workflow. The text is generated from the verb and the template path, so it cannot drift from them by hand.
src/adapters/wrapper-shapes-claude.ts.gotcha: A verb with no template path gets the init instructions rather than an error, the same as the Antigravity wrapper. The skill wrapper has no skill-reference block and no entry glue, unlike the command wrapper, so the two are not interchangeable.

src/adapters/wrapper-shapes-codex.ts.what: Builds the sentinel-bracketed block that goes into AGENTS.md. The block names the workflow, skill and journey folders, lists the slash commands, and records each template's hash.
src/adapters/wrapper-shapes-codex.ts.why: The recorded hashes let drift be detected later. The block is regenerated by a forced init, so the user's own text outside the markers stays untouched.
src/adapters/wrapper-shapes-codex.ts.gotcha: The hashes are written sorted by key, so the same templates always produce the same bytes. The slash-command list is built from the workflow verbs only, so a skill or journey is never listed as a command.

src/commands/build-evidence.ts.what: `ui build-evidence lint <dir>`: checks a builder's evidence folder against the build-loop standard, rule by rule (r1 to r8), and reports each rule as PASS, FAIL or SKIPPED with a reason. A folder that does not exist exits 2.
src/commands/build-evidence.ts.why: Gives a builder a checklist it cannot argue with, since each screenshot and probe either exists or does not.
src/commands/build-evidence.ts.gotcha: The name is kept apart from `ui evidence` on purpose, because the two are different ledgers. Rule r8 applies only when the folder holds a contact sheet or concept file, or when --mode persuade is passed; otherwise it is SKIPPED. Exit code 2 means a missing folder, not a failed rule.

src/commands/doctor.ts.what: `ui doctor [--cwd <dir>]`: a read-only health check of the install (Node version, the bundled templates and knowledge roots) and, when a project directory is given, of its adapter manifest, knowledge path, template drift and generated wrappers.
src/commands/doctor.ts.why: A silent setup failure is the costly case, so each check reports by name.
src/commands/doctor.ts.gotcha: The project manifest is the first runtime manifest found, in RUNTIMES order, so a project with several runtimes is checked against whichever comes first. A bare positional path works the same as --cwd. Warnings never fail the run. The required knowledge files are a hard-coded list of four.

src/commands/ds-usage-lint.ts.what: `ui ds-usage-lint <file.html> --dir <project>`: checks whether a page's own CSS uses the design system's tokens. It reports undeclared token references (error), tokens the page declares that the design system does not (warning), and hard-coded colours in colour properties (error). Colour only in v1.
src/commands/ds-usage-lint.ts.why: The enforcement gate for the design-system context. None of the other floors checks token use.
src/commands/ds-usage-lint.ts.gotcha: It proves token use in the page's own CSS, not the rendered colour, and says so in its output note. Spacing and radius literals are deliberately not checked. A missing design.tokens.json is DS_NOT_FOUND, and an unreadable token file is BAD_JSON, both raised before the page is checked.

src/commands/evidence.ts.what: `ui evidence add | list | verify | show`: a ledger of findings that cite sources. A quote finding is accepted only when its quote is a verbatim substring of its source, and verify re-checks every quote.
src/commands/evidence.ts.why: An anti-fabrication gate: a finding cannot cite text that is not in its source, and the check is repeatable.
src/commands/evidence.ts.gotcha: Only quote findings are checked against the source. An observation is accepted but marked unsupported. Adding a source copies the file into the store, and a different file with the same name is refused as SOURCE_COLLISION. A non-numeric --n is stored as NaN, which the ledger writes as null, rather than being refused.

src/commands/flow.ts.what: `ui flow lint <flow.json>`: runs the deterministic checks on a flow graph. Dangling references, unreachable screens, dead ends, missing error states, invalid triggers, self-loops and a missing entry point are errors. Orphan screens, unreachable states, missing back paths, missing empty and skeleton states, and guards without a complement are warnings.
src/commands/flow.ts.why: Structural faults in a multi-screen design are easy to miss in review, and a graph check finds them mechanically.
src/commands/flow.ts.gotcha: Guards are linted but never run, so the lint cannot say whether a guard can ever be satisfied. A file that is not valid JSON is reported as BAD_FLOW with the parser's own message, the same code used for a wrong shape.

src/commands/memory.ts.what: The dispatcher for `ui memory`. It routes eight subcommands (record, compile, context, query, fingerprint, consolidate, status, export-corpus) to their implementation files, and holds the help text that lists the event types, flags and error codes.
src/commands/memory.ts.why: Keeps the public command surface in one place. The central flag guard rejects unknown flags before dispatch, so each implementation checks only values.
src/commands/memory.ts.gotcha: The help text is the only place the full event-type list is written down, and it lives here rather than beside the record implementation. A missing subcommand and an unknown one both return BAD_ARG.

src/commands/product-context-errors.ts.what: Turns product-context failures into messages: which file was refused and why, which part of an atlas failed, which receipt did not decode, and the code for a compile failure.
src/commands/product-context-errors.ts.why: A code names a class of failure and is a public contract. The message names the instance, so the operator knows which repair to try.
src/commands/product-context-errors.ts.gotcha: A replay mismatch and a non-canonical atlas both answer to BAD_PRODUCT_ATLAS and differ only in message. compileErrorCode maps just two named errors and returns BAD_PRODUCT_CONTEXT for every other failure, and a generic failure is recognised only by its exact text, 'invalid product context'.

src/commands/prompt-plan.ts.what: `ui prompt-plan validate|preflight <file.json>`: runs the prompt-plan v1 checks on one file. The two subcommands produce the same findings. Exit 1 when the plan is not ready.
src/commands/prompt-plan.ts.why: Lets the design pipeline gate generation on a plan that passes its contract.
src/commands/prompt-plan.ts.gotcha: The two subcommands really are identical; preflight exists only as a name. check() defaults to validate when no subcommand is given, but run() rejects a missing subcommand before check() is reached, so that default is never used.

src/commands/trace.ts.what: `ui trace summarize <dir>`: reads the append-only read trace that a host hook writes, and reports the bytes and files loaded before the first mutation, whether the orientation files were opened, whether es-designer was loaded and its checklist run, and how many gate runs there were.
src/commands/trace.ts.why: The evidence comes from a record the hook wrote, not from the agent's own account of its work.
src/commands/trace.ts.gotcha: A missing trace file is not an error: it is read as an empty trace, and the coverage is reported as none. --session keeps only the records of that session id. A bare --session with no value is BAD_ARG.

src/core/agents-gen.ts.what: The pure half of `ui agents`: the three launch roles (designer, curator, figma-hand), the agent name built from role, studio and project, an FNV-1a template hash, the placeholder renderer, and the stamp parser the linter uses to recognise its own generated files.
src/core/agents-gen.ts.why: An agent's identity is read at run time from the soul, never baked in, so editing the soul changes the agent with no regeneration. Only the name is baked.
src/core/agents-gen.ts.gotcha: sanitizeAgentName can return an empty string when nothing survives, for example a studio name with no ASCII letters, and the caller has to fall back. The template hash covers the raw template including its placeholders, so even a whitespace-only edit changes the stamp.

src/core/audit-spec.ts.what: Turns a DTCG token file and a component registry into the lookup surface for the audit detector: colour to token path, component names and the deprecated ones, whether an Icon component exists, the grid base, and the radius and spacing scales.
src/core/audit-spec.ts.why: The audit is a pure transform of its inputs. Tolerant parsing means one malformed record cannot crash it.
src/core/audit-spec.ts.gotcha: When two tokens share a colour, the one with the lexicographically smaller path wins, so the choice does not depend on file order. An invalid or non-positive grid base falls back to 4. A component counts as an Icon when its name or its category starts with Icon.

src/core/brief-questions-build.ts.what: Builds the questions document from a brief's blocking fields: one question per blocking field, route-changing ones first. On a BLOCKED receipt it adds one question per low-confidence assumption that no blocking field already covers. A recommended answer is included only where a rule can derive one.
src/core/brief-questions-build.ts.why: A blocked brief should put to the owner the questions that unblock it, in the order that matters.
src/core/brief-questions-build.ts.gotcha: The copy-language question always carries a recommendation, because deriveCopyLanguage always returns a language, even when the request does not name one. Transition and assumption questions have no recommendation unless a rule supplies one.

src/core/capability-activation.ts.what: Resolves an activation request against the capability catalog and builds a version 2 receipt. It checks the request shape, the selection evidence (a quoted substring of the request, or the documented web-marketing default), the surface and input kind, and the profile's consistency. The result is ROUTED or REFUSED.
src/core/capability-activation.ts.why: The receipt is a deterministic function of the request and the catalog, so it can be replayed and compared later. The digests bind it to both.
src/core/capability-activation.ts.gotcha: A request for an unavailable capability still produces a receipt, inside a failed result, so a caller must check ok before using the route. The documented default is valid only for web-marketing. Only version 2 receipts are built here, although a version 1 type is declared.

src/core/change-log-stream.ts.what: Reads the Figma change log from a byte offset instead of from the start. The offset is trusted only when it is 0, or when it sits just after a newline inside the file. Otherwise the module falls back to a full scan and reports why.
src/core/change-log-stream.ts.why: The cost of a run follows the unread tail, not the whole log, which grows without limit.
src/core/change-log-stream.ts.gotcha: A malformed line inside the range that is read still throws, so streaming changes when lines are read, never whether they are validated. A file that does not exist is read as empty, but a missing file at a non-zero hinted offset is a fallback of kind file-missing. A byte-past-size fallback is the signature of a rotated log.

src/core/delivery/delivery-art-direction.what: Validates the art-direction part of an art-directed variant: the six identity axes, the design read (page kind, audience, vibe, system family), three integer dials from 1 to 10, and the convergence check that stops every generated page looking the same.
src/core/delivery/delivery-art-direction.why: A repeated visual choice is allowed only when it is justified, so identical outputs across trials are caught as a defect.
src/core/delivery/delivery-art-direction.gotcha: A convergence verdict of default-convergence always fails, and any repeated axis that is not also listed as justified fails too. The axes are matched by name. The evidence check is delegated to delivery-art-evidence-validation.ts and is not read here.

src/core/delivery/delivery-section-archi.what: Validates the section architecture of a v2 contract (a page narrative, and a row per section with its purpose, role, layout, anchor, content dependency and responsive change). It also validates a qualification's section review, and cross-checks that review against the contract's sections.
src/core/delivery/delivery-section-archi.why: Stops a page whose sections repeat one layout, or whose sections do not fit their topic, from qualifying.
src/core/delivery/delivery-section-archi.gotcha: Three or more sections need at least two layout models, and a repeated layout needs a repetitionRationale. A QUALIFIED review row must have every observation true and no finding. A cause must be one of a fixed set, or null, and decision references must start with decision:.

src/core/designmd-audit-accessibility.ts.what: The accessibility audit for DESIGN.md. For each component with a textColor and a backgroundColor that resolve to hex, it computes the WCAG contrast ratio. A ratio below 3:1 is a FAIL, and a ratio from 3:1 up to 4.5:1 is a WARN.
src/core/designmd-audit-accessibility.ts.why: Checks the colour pairs the spec declares, before any page is built from them.
src/core/designmd-audit-accessibility.ts.gotcha: Every pair is judged against the 4.5:1 body threshold, because the spec does not say whether a component holds large text. A pair between 3:1 and 4.5:1 is therefore a WARN, never a PASS. A spec with no components block gets a WARN row instead of a failure. [found by reading the code; not reproduced] resolveRef's comment says it recurses once, but it recurses without a limit, so a reference cycle (A points at B and B at A) would recurse until the stack overflows.

src/core/ds-diff.ts.what: Classifies the change between two design-system states, tokens and components, as breaking, additive, patch or none, and recommends the semver bump. It is pure: the caller supplies both states.
src/core/ds-diff.ts.why: Makes 'visual breaking change' something that can be computed rather than judged by eye. A colour change is breaking when its perceptual distance (OKLab) exceeds 0.02, and a dimension change when it exceeds 5%.
src/core/ds-diff.ts.gotcha: Tolerances decide the bump: a change under the threshold is a patch, and a removed token or a dropped variant or state is breaking. A component left referencing a removed token forces a major bump. A component whose only difference is its markup is a patch. The bump is the highest severity found anywhere.

src/core/ds-guidelines-lint-pack.ts.what: Cross-file checks on a guidelines pack. Duplicate rules: the same rule text appears in two files. Completeness: the manifest lists a file or a generated block that is gone, or the manifest itself is missing or unreadable.
src/core/ds-guidelines-lint-pack.ts.why: A pack must not repeat a rule, and it must be complete, or it cannot prove that it is whole.
src/core/ds-guidelines-lint-pack.ts.gotcha: Rule text is compared after lower-casing and stripping punctuation, so a rule that differs only in case or punctuation counts as a duplicate. A normalised rule shorter than 20 characters is never a duplicate. The copy inside a generated block is treated as canonical, and app files may share a rule by design.

src/core/ds-usage-lint.ts.what: The algorithm behind ds-usage-lint. It finds var() references and colour literals in a page's own component CSS, skipping the token-declaration blocks, and reports undeclared references (error), tokens the page invents (warning) and hard-coded colours (error).
src/core/ds-usage-lint.ts.why: Enforces that a generated page uses the design system's tokens. None of the existing floors checks this.
src/core/ds-usage-lint.ts.gotcha: Comments are blanked before matching, so a commented-out reference is ignored. A var() with a fallback is still checked by name. Only the first hex or colour function in a colour-bearing property is reported. The module states that it is not a conformance claim, because it reads only the page's own CSS.

src/core/figma-conventions-synth.ts.what: The pure orchestrator that turns a Figma usage scan (usage-dna.json) into a CONVENTIONS.md document and a set of insights. When a token file is supplied, it compares the measured values with the design system's scale, so real deviations are separated from on-scale values.
src/core/figma-conventions-synth.ts.why: Learns how a design system is actually used, not only what it contains. The output is deterministic: the same input gives the same bytes.
src/core/figma-conventions-synth.ts.gotcha: A section marked missing is counted and listed, but adds nothing to the totals. The scale is built only from dimension tokens whose category name hints at radius or spacing, so a token in any other category is never a valid value. A dimension that is an alias is skipped.

src/core/figma-ds-registry.ts.what: Turns a Figma design-system scan into a registry. Icons are rolled up into one summary, screen frames are listed apart, and real components keep their exact Figma name.
src/core/figma-ds-registry.ts.why: The exact name is the key the live Figma file is resolved by, so it must not be normalised. The records are written directly rather than through the code-authored registration path, which has a stricter name pattern.
src/core/figma-ds-registry.ts.gotcha: Classification is by name first: a name that starts with a digit is a screen, and a name matching icon or lucide is an icon. The width rule for screens never fires, because the scan does not yet supply a width. Lifecycle status comes from green, blue or yellow circle emoji in the name, and those markers are stripped from the stored name. Scope is always local, because the scan carries no publish signal.

src/core/judge-store.ts.what: Reads and appends the judgments ledger (design/judgments.jsonl), with one judgment per line. A human decision is a second line that repeats the same id, and the last line for each id is its current state.
src/core/judge-store.ts.why: Keeps the record of judgments append-only, so an earlier decision is never rewritten.
src/core/judge-store.ts.gotcha: A line that is not valid JSON, or that fails validation, is reported as an error with its line number, and the other lines still load. A human decision must repeat the pending judgment exactly, and a judgment that already has a human decision cannot be appended to again. readLedger throws if the file cannot be read; it does not return an error.

src/core/knowledge-effect-catalog-check..what: Eight checks that tie the matrix in the effect-direction file to the effect catalog ledger: the revision matches, every slug appears on both sides, each row's name and family agree with the ledger, narrative cells are filled, object effects carry the Draco clause, and the catalog is not more than six months old (a warning).
src/core/knowledge-effect-catalog-check..why: Keeps the human-readable matrix and the machine ledger in step.
src/core/knowledge-effect-catalog-check..gotcha: The Draco rule takes the family from the ledger, not from the matrix row, so a drifted family cell is reported as row-drift and is not relied on. With a ledger but no matrix, there are no findings. With neither file, there are no findings either.

src/core/knowledge-frontmatter-check.ts.what: Routing front-matter checks for the top-level files in knowledge/. Each file needs a routing block whose id matches its filename, and the committed index.json must equal what the emitter produces from those blocks.
src/core/knowledge-frontmatter-check.ts.why: A file without a routing block cannot be found by a task, and a stale index sends consumers back to the prose table.
src/core/knowledge-frontmatter-check.ts.gotcha: Only top-level .md files are checked, and README.md is exempt because it is the map, not a destination. A missing index counts as drift. A declared id must equal the filename without its .md extension, since that is how a reference resolves.

src/core/knowledge-gradient-catalog-chec.what: The gradient-catalog checks for the ShaderGradient knowledge pair. They compare the preset matrix in the direction file with the catalog: revision, slugs on both sides, name and mesh agreement, filled narrative cells, and the fallback cell. A catalog more than six months old is a warning.
src/core/knowledge-gradient-catalog-chec.why: Each preset has two independent fallbacks, the reduced-motion frozen field and the no-WebGL CSS gradient. The file records that shipping only one of them as if it were both is the measured failure, so a fallback cell that never names the frozen state is an error.
src/core/knowledge-gradient-catalog-chec.gotcha: The fallback check is skipped for an empty cell, because the empty cell is already reported as field-empty, and reporting it twice would make one defect look like two. The mesh cell is compared with the ledger, and no other check reads it. With neither file present there are no findings.

src/core/knowledge-ledger-provenance.ts.what: Shared helpers for the knowledge ledger pairs: the first 40-hex git revision found in a direction file, and the number of months between two YYYYMM stamps.
src/core/knowledge-ledger-provenance.ts.why: Both ledgers must pin and age in the same way. Keeping these in one place means a change to the staleness rule reaches every ledger.
src/core/knowledge-ledger-provenance.ts.gotcha: The revision is the first 40-hex string anywhere in the file, so a commit hash mentioned earlier in the prose would be taken as the pin. monthsBetween returns null for a malformed stamp, and a null age is never reported as stale.

src/core/knowledge-web-technique-check.t.what: Checks the web-technique knowledge against its tracked source ledger: the path allowlist, no embedded base64 or data-URI payloads, the catalog shape, each adopted technique present in the catalog, each card's required headings, each handoff skill registered, and each workflow reachable. Every finding is an error.
src/core/knowledge-web-technique-check.t.why: Web-technique knowledge is admitted only when every adopted technique has a verifiable source and a card.
src/core/knowledge-web-technique-check.t.gotcha: The check fails open. If the source manifest or its decisions cannot be parsed, it returns no findings, so a broken ledger passes. [found by reading the code; not reproduced] Several branches also return at the first failure, so one defect can hide the ones after it.

src/core/layout-checks-craft.ts.what: Two web-craft checks, both warnings. clickable-no-pointer flags a non-native element made clickable with onclick or role=button and no pointer cursor. font-display-missing flags an @font-face with no font-display, or a Google Fonts stylesheet link with no display parameter.
src/core/layout-checks-craft.ts.why: Both are functional faults rather than taste. The first removes the hand cursor from a clickable element, and the second causes invisible text while a font loads, then a layout shift.
src/core/layout-checks-craft.ts.gotcha: A preconnect or DNS-prefetch link to the fonts origin is not flagged, because only stylesheet links load CSS. Native controls are exempt from the cursor check. Any provable cursor source exempts an element: a utility class, an inline style, or a CSS rule on one of its classes.

src/core/memory-corpus.ts.what: Builds the embeddable corpus from the memory ledger, one natural-language payload for each insight, reasoned token change, harvested source, vibe mapping and variant generation, tiered as episodic, semantic or procedural. It also parses a rank file.
src/core/memory-corpus.ts.why: This is the deterministic seam between the binary and the optional recall workspace. The same ledger always gives the same bytes, and the ledger stays the source of truth.
src/core/memory-corpus.ts.gotcha: A token change with no recorded reason is not embedded, because a bare value swap is not durable knowledge. Other event types carry no payload. The sinceId cut is numeric, so a cut point that no longer exists in the ledger still slices correctly.

src/core/memory-profile.ts.what: Builds the cross-project taste profile from the ledgers of registered projects: persona families, recurring vibes and avoided axes. It keeps only signals that recur in at least two projects, and keeps the insights across rebuilds.
src/core/memory-profile.ts.why: One project's quirk is not taste, so a signal counts only when it recurs across projects.
src/core/memory-profile.ts.gotcha: A registered project whose path no longer exists is skipped without a message. Recurrence is counted by project name, so two projects registered under the same name count once. Insights are deduplicated by exact text, and the first one seen wins.

src/core/product-context-model.ts.what: A re-export facade for the product-context value helpers, the receipt normaliser and the atlas normaliser.
src/core/product-context-model.ts.why: Gives the commands one import path.
src/core/product-context-model.ts.gotcha: It has no logic of its own. The names it re-exports are defined in product-context-value.ts and the two model files.

src/core/product-context-resolution.ts.what: Resolves each product field from the receipts' claims. It applies supersession, then takes one active value, or a set of active values that all agree. Disagreeing values are recorded as an atlas conflict error. Non-present dispositions become findings, and required ones are errors.
src/core/product-context-resolution.ts.why: A field has one agreed value or it is reported. Disagreement is never merged silently.
src/core/product-context-resolution.ts.gotcha: A supersession loop throws ProductContextError. A claim that supersedes another must be present, in a captured or capped receipt, or it throws. [found by reading the code; not reproduced] A field whose only claims sit in receipts that were not captured resolves as unresolved and adds no finding of its own.

src/core/registry-token-check.ts.what: Checks that every tokensUsed path in a registry record resolves to a real token in the compiled design system, when one is present. With no design system, only the format is checked.
src/core/registry-token-check.ts.why: A path that is well formed but unknown was accepted before, and this closes that gap.
src/core/registry-token-check.ts.gotcha: Modes are $extensions on a token, not tokens of their own, so a path that exists only under a mode is refused. The refusal message says the path is unknown, not malformed, because the format check has already run.

src/core/rendered/browser-session.ts.what: Launches an installed Chromium headless, in an isolated temporary profile, attaches over the DevTools protocol, and always removes the profile and stops the browser. It never installs a browser. When none is found, the rendered tier is reported as not evaluated, with the environment variable to set.
src/core/rendered/browser-session.ts.why: Lets the rendered checks run without a bundled browser, and never touches the operator's own profile or any browser they are using.
src/core/rendered/browser-session.ts.gotcha: An explicit --browser path that does not exist is a hard stop, not a fallback, so a render cannot quietly use a different engine. Port 0 lets the OS choose, and the port is read from the profile's DevToolsActivePort file. Cleanup sends SIGTERM, waits up to five seconds, and sends SIGKILL only if the process is still alive after two seconds.

src/core/role-recognition.ts.what: Annotates each colour token with the UI role its name implies (background, card, primary, destructive and so on) by adding a design-os.role extension. It never renames a token and never removes one.
src/core/role-recognition.ts.why: Keeps the design system's own names intact while the rest of the tooling reads each token's role.
src/core/role-recognition.ts.gotcha: A name that matches two families with equal strength is reported as ambiguous and left unannotated, rather than guessed. Hue names such as blue-100 and scale steps such as brand-500 are skipped on purpose. overlay and scrim are never mapped to popover, because they usually name the modal dimmer. Only colour tokens are annotated.

src/core/taste-checks-gradient.ts.what: Flags a large background gradient whose colour stops mostly fall in the indigo to magenta band (about 270 to 330 degrees OKLCH). This is the AI-glow default, an error. The whole check is skipped when the document declares its own brand colour in that band.
src/core/taste-checks-gradient.ts.why: Gradients in that band read as machine-default taste on enterprise surfaces, and the rubric treats a gradient as a design choice, not a default.
src/core/taste-checks-gradient.ts.gotcha: The brand exemption reads custom properties only from the same file, so an on-brand violet declared elsewhere still flags. Small elements are excluded by selector words, such as button or badge. Tailwind gradient stops are judged by colour name, with no colour lookup.

src/core/taste-checks-typography.ts.what: Three typography checks: italic display or heading type, all-caps text with a line height below 1.0, and at least three number-shaped table cells with no tabular figures (a warning).
src/core/taste-checks-typography.ts.why: Each is a generated-UI tell with its own line in the rubric.
src/core/taste-checks-typography.ts.gotcha: The italic check reports once per heading rule, with no line number, and reports each em or i inside a heading by line. The tabular check is skipped if a monospace family appears anywhere in the CSS, and it passes when tabular-nums appears anywhere. Date and phone cells count as numbers by design. line-height: 1 passes, because the floor is strictly below 1.

src/core/taste-checks.ts.what: The barrel for the per-axis taste checks. It holds the typography, spacing, iconography and depth checks itself and re-exports the motion and consistency checks from their own modules.
src/core/taste-checks.ts.why: Keeps one import surface for the taste linter.
src/core/taste-checks.ts.gotcha: The policy is precision over recall, so the chrome-role list is wide. Its leading word boundary is left out on purpose, so a class such as savatar or icode also matches and exempts a small size. The mixed-icon check flags two or more families among Phosphor, Lucide, Font Awesome, Material, Bootstrap, Heroicons, Feather, Ionicons and Tabler.

src/core/template-catalogue-build.ts.what: Builds the template catalogue (each registered template's path, description and source hash) from the raw bytes, and serialises it deterministically. The command reads the files; this module only transforms them.
src/core/template-catalogue-build.ts.why: The kernel reads this catalogue at run time instead of parsing Markdown, so the recorded hashes can be checked against it.
src/core/template-catalogue-build.ts.gotcha: The registered paths come from the adapter lists, so a template that is on disk but not registered is never catalogued. Entries are sorted by code point rather than by locale, so the output is the same on every machine.

src/commands/changelog.ts.what: `ui changelog [--dir] [--format markdown|json]`: folds the design system's manifest changelog and its recorded insight decisions from the memory ledger into one history, newest first. Read-only.
src/commands/changelog.ts.why: Lets a reader see a design's history without opening the manifest and the ledger separately.
src/commands/changelog.ts.gotcha: A missing manifest is reported as NO_MEMORY, which is the wrong name for a design that was never initialised. A malformed memory ledger is ignored without a message: readDecisions catches the error and returns no decisions, so they vanish silently.

src/commands/content-lint.ts.what: `ui content-lint <file.html>`: runs the twelve content checks over the page and its linked CSS, with errors sorted first. It exits 1 on any error-severity finding.
src/commands/content-lint.ts.why: A deterministic floor for copy that is wrong. Tone and fit are left to the curator.
src/commands/content-lint.ts.gotcha: Warnings such as plural-s-hack, click-here-link and dumb-punctuation never fail the command. Only error-severity findings set exit 1.

src/commands/critique-coverage.ts.what: `ui critique-coverage <spec> <manifest>`: counts which acceptance criteria the screens claim to cover. It reports uncovered criteria, the coverage percentage, assumptions, and broken evidence citations. It exits 1 on uncovered criteria, on assumptions under --require-evidence, or on broken evidence.
src/commands/critique-coverage.ts.why: A deterministic count for the goal axis of a design. The taste judgment stays with the model.
src/commands/critique-coverage.ts.gotcha: The tool accounts for a self-report: it shows that the claimed criteria are covered, not that the design meets the brief. An evidence id that is missing, or whose quote no longer matches its source, is broken evidence and fails the gate even without --require-evidence.

src/commands/designmd-extract-tokens-imp.what: `ui designmd extract-tokens <html> [--css a.css,b.css] [--out]`: reads the page and any linked CSS, and emits a frequency-ranked list of colours, fonts and custom properties, each with its line of provenance.
src/commands/designmd-extract-tokens-imp.why: This is the vocabulary input for ui ingest-css-ds.
src/commands/designmd-extract-tokens-imp.gotcha: A repeated --css flag is refused with REPEATED_FLAG rather than silently keeping the last value, so the files must be comma-joined. A missing CSS file stops the run before anything is written.

src/commands/designmd-snapshot-impl.ts.what: `ui designmd snapshot <html> --origin <url>`: produces a self-contained preview page. Linked CSS is inlined, scripts are stripped, reveal-state styles are cleaned, and root-relative URLs are made absolute against the origin.
src/commands/designmd-snapshot-impl.ts.why: Lets a site be previewed without its scripts or its network assets.
src/commands/designmd-snapshot-impl.ts.gotcha: --origin is required and must be a full URL, and only its origin is kept, so any path in it is dropped. A repeated --css keeps only the last value without any message. Unlike extract-tokens, this command does not refuse the repeat.

src/commands/ds-guidelines-write.ts.what: Writes a guidelines pack and a bundle export safely. The answers store and the parked answers are written first, each through a temp file and a rename. The other files are staged, then moved in together. For a bundle export, the previous bundle is kept aside and restored if anything fails.
src/commands/ds-guidelines-write.ts.why: A written answer is never lost to a failed write. A person's answer may exist only in the store, so the store is written before anything else.
src/commands/ds-guidelines-write.ts.gotcha: A backup left by an earlier interrupted export blocks the new export, and the command refuses rather than overwrite that backup; the error tells the owner to move it back. A failure to remove the staging folder is reported as a note, never as the error. The failure message describes the output folder from a before-and-after snapshot, not from an assumption.

src/commands/scroll-story.ts.what: `ui scroll-story <frames-dir>`: reads the ordered PNG frames of a scroll capture, decodes them, and reports whether the sequence is ACTIVE (content moves beyond a plain scroll reveal) or FLAT. The verdict is informational, and any readable directory exits 0.
src/commands/scroll-story.ts.why: Gives a critic a signal about a scroll capture without making it a gate.
src/commands/scroll-story.ts.gotcha: A frame that cannot be decoded is skipped and listed, and the pairs are then formed from the frames that remain. A gap in the sequence is therefore not visible in the verdict, because the two frames either side of it are compared as neighbours. A missing directory exits 2.

src/commands/scrub-lint.ts.what: `ui scrub-lint <file.mp4>`: checks a clip meant to be scrubbed (scroll drives playback) for faststart, audio, a video track and keyframe spacing. It reads the MP4 box tree and decodes nothing.
src/commands/scrub-lint.ts.why: A clip scrubbed without these properties seeks slowly, because each seek waits for the whole file or decodes a long run of frames.
src/commands/scrub-lint.ts.gotcha: The command is wrong for a playback video, and its help says so: a long-GOP demo recording would be flagged for a floor that does not apply, and the tool cannot tell the two apart. A file with no moov or mdat boxes is refused with NOT_ISO_BMFF rather than passed.

src/commands/taste.ts.what: The dispatcher for `ui taste`, routing ingest, next, record and status to their implementations. The help text documents the store layout and the error codes.
src/commands/taste.ts.why: Keeps the taste command surface in one place.
src/commands/taste.ts.gotcha: The header comment names a serve verb that is not registered, and the command signatures declare only the four shipped verbs. A missing or unknown subcommand returns BAD_ARG.

src/core/adapter-lint.ts.what: The adapter integrity checks for `ui doctor --cwd`: template drift, which re-hashes the live templates and compares them with the hashes recorded at init (reporting removed, changed and added templates), and the wrapper checks, which are delegated to another module.
src/core/adapter-lint.ts.why: Editing templates without re-running init used to leave every runtime silently stale, and a broken wrapper still reported healthy.
src/core/adapter-lint.ts.gotcha: A manifest with no recorded hashes gets a warning, not a failure, so older installs are not failed. The live list must enumerate the same templates as init, or drift is misreported; the file says so in a comment. A template that cannot be resolved is left out of the live list, so a deleted template shows up as removed from the package.

src/core/build-evidence-rules-probe.ts.what: Rule r3 (the scroll width is no greater than the inner width) and rule r7 (the font check passes, or the fallback face is noted) over the probe JSON matched to each screenshot. Real probes use different key names, and every form is accepted.
src/core/build-evidence-rules-probe.ts.why: Catches horizontal overflow and a font that did not render, which a screenshot alone can hide.
src/core/build-evidence-rules-probe.ts.gotcha: r7 accepts five key names, and an object passes only if every member is true. A probe with no font key at all makes r7 SKIPPED, not failed. r7's fallback test is a text search: any mention of 'fallback' in deviations.md passes the check, whatever the sentence says.

src/core/build-evidence-rules-shots.ts.what: Rule r1 (a probe JSON beside every screenshot) and rule r2 (every required width present as a PNG). It also holds the screenshot-to-probe resolver, which r3 and r7 share.
src/core/build-evidence-rules-shots.ts.why: Real evidence folders vary their file names and shapes, so the resolver accepts four layouts and nothing is required to match one fixed form.
src/core/build-evidence-rules-shots.ts.gotcha: The resolver tries the screenshot's own folder before the root, and the first match wins, so a stale probe in a subfolder hides a correct one at the root. A probe file that does not parse is passed over and the next layout is tried. r2 checks the widths only, not that each PNG is a real render.

src/core/check-catalog.ts.what: The roster of every check the composed gate can run, per family, with the context each one requires. The triage router reads this roster to decide which checks apply to an artifact.
src/core/check-catalog.ts.why: A router that reads this list cannot drift from the checks that actually exist. A test re-derives the ids from the family sources in both directions.
src/core/check-catalog.ts.gotcha: A check with no catalog row is missing from triage, and the test is what catches that, not the code. Some rows name a subject, the region a valid autofix patch may touch. requires has two forms, the legacy strings 'none' and 'tokens' and fact-kind objects, so a consumer must handle both.

src/core/css-selector-blocks.ts.what: A brace-nesting scan, not a CSS parser. It finds the selector enclosing a given byte offset, so the token extractor can record which selector a custom property sits under. For an HTML source it scans only inside style tags.
src/core/css-selector-blocks.ts.why: A scan over the whole HTML would read script braces as CSS and attach the wrong selector.
src/core/css-selector-blocks.ts.gotcha: A block whose closing brace is missing runs to the end of the file. Top-level semicolon-terminated at-rules are skipped, so they do not become part of the next selector. Comments are blanked first, so braces inside them do not count.

src/core/designmd-token-extractor.ts.what: Extracts hex colours (with counts and line provenance), font-family names, and custom properties with their enclosing selector, from HTML and CSS by regular expression. The result is the source list that the audit's source-fidelity check compares against.
src/core/designmd-token-extractor.ts.why: An audit can only check a DESIGN.md against what the source actually uses, so this scan defines the source side.
src/core/designmd-token-extractor.ts.gotcha: rgb, hsl and oklch values are not extracted, and a custom property resolves to a hex only when its value is a hex literal. Generic families and var() references are skipped, so a font known only through a variable is not recorded. Each token keeps at most five provenance entries, while its count includes every occurrence.

src/core/ds-fuel-line.ts.what: Wires the learning-loop configuration into a design store's design directory: a draft soul scaffold, a default heartbeat.json with four scheduled tasks, and an empty harvest-inbox directory. Each one is written only when it is absent.
src/core/ds-fuel-line.ts.why: A store that got a soul or a heartbeat through only one of the two roads gave the project no rhythm to learn from. Both init and import call this one helper, so the fix lives once.
src/core/ds-fuel-line.ts.gotcha: The task list is fixed here, so no figma-audit task is added, because that task needs a Figma file configured. The three files are outside the store's seal, so writing them can never trigger DS_TAMPERED. The inbox directory is created on every call, even when it already exists.

src/core/ds-guidelines-figma-scenarios.t.what: Rewrites a pack's scenario slots for the Figma bundle, dropping the QUESTION line and the slot id and showing each scenario as a heading, an evidence line and its answer. Also finds the scenarios in a rendered bundle that lack a complete answer.
src/core/ds-guidelines-figma-scenarios.t.why: Figma's agent reads the bundle as guidance, and the machine handle (the slot id) means nothing there.
src/core/ds-guidelines-figma-scenarios.t.gotcha: A look-alike-names slot has no title heading, so its prompt becomes the heading and its component names become the evidence. The open-scenario check finds each scenario by its evidence line, so a scenario whose evidence line was removed is not checked at all.

src/core/ds-guidelines-scenario-seeds.ts.what: Seeds the anti-pattern scenario slots from evidence: normative ruling text, the measured DON'T lines in CONVENTIONS.md, persona anti-patterns, and measured gaps that need a decision. A ruling counts as normative when its text contains never, always or do not.
src/core/ds-guidelines-scenario-seeds.ts.why: A rebuild must keep each answer attached to the right slot. Each slot id comes from its evidence, not from a counter, a line number or the order things arrive in.
src/core/ds-guidelines-scenario-seeds.ts.gotcha: The digits, percent signs and asterisks are removed from a DON'T line before it is hashed, so two lines that differ only in their figures are one slot, deliberately. The file records this as technical debt, because a line whose meaning lives in a number would be merged. Identical evidence gives one slot that lists every source.

src/core/ds-preview-sections.ts.what: The pure HTML fragments for the specimen page: colour pairs with their contrast ratio, the type ramp, shape and shadow chips, motion durations, and the components section taken from the registry. Text is escaped before it is injected.
src/core/ds-preview-sections.ts.why: The specimen shows only real token and registry values. It never authors component markup, because the registry is the only source of components.
src/core/ds-preview-sections.ts.gotcha: A colour pair is shown only when both sides are hex, so a pair written in rgba is silently left out. A component with no markup is listed by name only. Shadow chips depend on per-member CSS variables, so a shadow whose members were never emitted shows no visible shadow.

src/core/evidence-store.ts.what: Reads and writes the user-evidence store: a ledger of records plus a directory of verbatim sources. It copies sources in by basename and re-checks each quote record against its stored source.
src/core/evidence-store.ts.why: The store stays self-contained, so anyone who clones it can re-verify every quote.
src/core/evidence-store.ts.gotcha: Sources are named by basename only, so two sources with the same name from different folders collide, and a different text is refused. loadEvidence throws on the first malformed line, so one bad line blocks every read of the store. verifyRecord checks only quote records, and any other kind is reported as verified.

src/core/extractors/html/css-values.ts.what: Parses colour, length, gradient and shadow values from CSS text, returning undefined rather than guessing. Also a top-level splitter that ignores separators inside parentheses.
src/core/extractors/html/css-values.ts.why: One implementation for every CSS consumer, so a fix is not patched into one extractor while the others keep the blind spot.
src/core/extractors/html/css-values.ts.gotcha: rem and em are converted at 16px (em uses the base the caller passes), while viewport and percentage units are not converted at all. The shadow parser reads only the first shadow in a list. A colour name outside the short table is undefined, not an approximation.

src/core/extractors/html/html-dom.ts.what: Parses HTML with source offsets on every node. It collects inline stylesheets and linked local ones, records remote links as unresolved, and gives each element a stable locator. The parse never throws, and a failed parse is marked degraded.
src/core/extractors/html/html-dom.ts.why: A finding needs a line number to be actionable, and a remote stylesheet has to be declared unread rather than assumed clean.
src/core/extractors/html/html-dom.ts.gotcha: A linked stylesheet is read only when it exists locally, and its declarations are tagged with that file's path rather than an HTML line. lineOfOffset rescans from the start of the file on each call, so anything inside a loop must use lineIndexFor.

src/core/figma-comment-types.ts.what: Type definitions for Figma comment triage: the two anchor kinds (a frame or a bare canvas point), threads with their replies, the fold statistics, the node shape, and the resolved anchor with its confidence. The shapes mirror the Figma API.
src/core/figma-comment-types.ts.why: Kept apart from the logic, as the file-size rule requires.
src/core/figma-comment-types.ts.gotcha: A pin is always anchored to a frame, never to an element, because Figma does not report the element. The element name is therefore inferred from the chain. The fold statistics must add up to the number pulled, so a silently dropped comment shows as a mismatch.

src/core/flow-lint.ts.what: The deterministic information-architecture checks on a parsed flow: dangling references, invalid triggers, self-loops, a missing entry point, unreachable screens and states, dead ends, missing error and empty states, and guards with no complement.
src/core/flow-lint.ts.why: Nothing else lints an information architecture deterministically, and these checks catch structural faults before anyone reviews the screens.
src/core/flow-lint.ts.gotcha: Reachability is computed over screens only. A state that some transition names is never reported as unreachable, even when that transition itself cannot be reached. A guard counts as complemented when any other transition leaves the same state, whatever its trigger.

src/core/html-autofix-font-display.ts.what: The autofix for font-display-missing. It adds font-display: swap to each @font-face block that lacks one in real CSS, and appends display=swap to a Google Fonts stylesheet link that has no display parameter. It runs only when the checker flags the document.
src/core/html-autofix-font-display.ts.why: The repair and the checker share one mask, so they agree about which text is live.
src/core/html-autofix-font-display.ts.gotcha: @font-face is repaired only inside real CSS, in style blocks and style attributes, never in prose that quotes CSS. The link edit is located by capture indices, so a duplicate URL elsewhere in the tag is not touched. When two edits overlap, the later one is skipped, which leaves a miss rather than a corrupted file.

src/core/knowledge-promotion-draft.ts.what: Turns an approver's correction (the screen, what was wrong, what is right, and the evidence) into a draft ruling stub with status draft and verified_by unverified. The stub is validated against the rulings schema before it is returned.
src/core/knowledge-promotion-draft.ts.why: A correction becomes a candidate ruling that someone must still promote, so a correction never goes straight into the rulings.
src/core/knowledge-promotion-draft.ts.gotcha: The id comes from the screen and a hash of the three texts, so the same correction always gives the same id, and submitting it again does not create a second ruling. The date is supplied by the caller, which keeps the output deterministic.

src/core/persona-loader.ts.what: Loads and strictly validates the personas index. Unknown properties are rejected at every level, and every hex colour and enum is checked. The path comes from an explicit argument, then the UI_PERSONAS_PATH variable, then a folder next to the built binary.
src/core/persona-loader.ts.why: A persona record is data the generator trusts, so the additionalProperties rule is enforced by hand here.
src/core/persona-loader.ts.gotcha: Validation stops at the first bad record and reports only its index, so a bad entry in a long index must be found by position. The default path is resolved relative to the built file, so an installed binary looks in the package's knowledge folder.

src/core/preview-link.ts.what: Formats a generated file's location as a bare file:// link on a labelled line. Also a fixed one-line note that Figma links come from figma-agent, because the kernel constructs none.
src/core/preview-link.ts.why: A bare URL is the form a terminal turns into a clickable link, and the channel drops markdown link syntax.
src/core/preview-link.ts.gotcha: The path must already be absolute, because pathToFileURL throws on a relative path. The URL is percent-encoded, so spaces and symbols in the folder name still produce a valid link.

src/core/project-scan.ts.what: Read-only detection of the design signals already in a project: framework, styling systems, the Tailwind config, the largest CSS and HTML files, component folders, DESIGN.md, and the design-system status. It gives a verdict of greenfield, brownfield-code, brownfield-html or ds-present. The walk is breadth first and skips a fixed list of folders.
src/core/project-scan.ts.why: Routes a new run to the right path and maps what already exists, without reading every file.
src/core/project-scan.ts.gotcha: Reaching the entry cap sets truncated, but the depth cap does not, so a branch deeper than six levels is silently absent and the scan is still reported as complete. The design folder is on the skip list. A design system that is present wins the verdict even when there is also application code.

src/core/registry-markup-reader.ts.what: Reads the markup for `ui registry register --markup`, from a file, or from stdin when the value is a dash. A missing file is FILE_NOT_FOUND and any other read failure is READ_ERROR. It re-exports the stdin reader from its own module.
src/core/registry-markup-reader.ts.why: A thin seam, so the registry command can be tested with synthetic input.
src/core/registry-markup-reader.ts.gotcha: The markup is read but not checked: whatever the file holds is stored as the component's markup.

src/core/rulings-lint.ts.what: Lints a rulings file. It runs the schema check, then the checks a schema cannot express: a source that looks like a repository path but does not exist, duplicate ids, SUPERSEDED in the text without a superseded_by field, and links to ids that are not in the file.
src/core/rulings-lint.ts.why: Keeps a rulings file's references honest, so a ruling cannot cite a file that has moved.
src/core/rulings-lint.ts.gotcha: A source counts as a repository path only when it is a single token ending in a short extension. Prose sources and URLs are skipped without any warning. The link check looks only inside the same file, so a link to a ruling in another file is reported as dangling.

src/core/seam-paths.ts.what: Works out the values a file read's path argument can take, by static evaluation over the modelled sources: string and template literals, concatenation, path.join and path.resolve, both branches of a conditional, and the arguments of local functions traced back to their callers. It returns the set of possible paths. It also decides which paths are prose.
src/core/seam-paths.ts.why: The seam lint can see which file a read may open without running the code.
src/core/seam-paths.ts.gotcha: The evaluation is bounded. More than 512 combined alternatives throws, and the seam command reports that as READ_ERROR. A value it cannot follow becomes a wildcard, not an error. A conditional gives the union of its branches, never a chosen one. isProsePath accepts README at any depth and markdown under knowledge, templates or docs.

src/core/seam-tokens.ts.what: A small lexical scanner for JavaScript and TypeScript. It produces tokens, pairs brackets, tracks scope, and treats comments and string contents as non-executable. It also has helpers that split a span on separators and find the end of a statement.
src/core/seam-tokens.ts.why: The seam model needs to locate a read call without a full parser.
src/core/seam-tokens.ts.gotcha: This is not a parser. A regular expression is recognised only from the token before it, so one that follows a closing bracket is read as division. Template literals are one token, and a backtick inside an interpolation ends the literal early.

src/core/stdin-reader.ts.what: Drains stdin completely into a UTF-8 string, through an injectable reader so that tests can pass in synthetic input. Also the real reader, which reads the stdin file descriptor.
src/core/stdin-reader.ts.why: Several commands accept a dash for stdin, and a single reader keeps them consistent.
src/core/stdin-reader.ts.gotcha: The read is synchronous and waits for end of input, so a command given a dash with nothing piped in blocks until the terminal sends end-of-file. Chunks are joined before decoding, so a multi-byte character split across two chunks is decoded correctly.

src/core/taste-checks-consistency.ts.what: The raw-hex check for the Consistency axis. It flags a colour that is not one of the design system's token colours, in two forms: a Tailwind arbitrary-value utility such as bg-[#…], and an inline colour or background in CSS. It is skipped when no token set is supplied.
src/core/taste-checks-consistency.ts.why: A colour that ignores the palette is the violation the rubric names. A colour that matches a token is left for the model to judge.
src/core/taste-checks-consistency.ts.gotcha: Only a value outside the token set is flagged, so a correct token value spelled as a literal passes. Short hex is expanded and alpha is dropped before the comparison. The Tailwind check matches only the listed utility prefixes.

src/core/taste-checks-motion.ts.what: Three motion checks, all errors. linear-easing and transition-all flag a transition that uses linear timing or the all shorthand. animation-no-reduced-motion flags a page with keyframes, an animation declaration or an animation-library script but no reduced-motion guard. keyframes-layout-props flags a keyframes block that animates a layout property.
src/core/taste-checks-motion.ts.why: Each is a motion rule in the taste rubric: directional easing, transform and opacity rather than layout, and a reduced-motion fallback.
src/core/taste-checks-motion.ts.gotcha: The reduced-motion check passes whenever the words prefers-reduced-motion appear anywhere in the document, so a guard that does nothing still clears it. The layout check reports only the first offending property in each keyframes block.

src/core/taste-rank.ts.what: Deterministic ranking over the taste ledgers. Elo is replayed from the votes in file order and never stored. The pair picker and the study picker choose their items from the ledger, and the self-consistency measure compares repeated votes with their originals.
src/core/taste-rank.ts.why: The next pair to vote on is reproducible from the ledger, and nothing random is used.
src/core/taste-rank.ts.gotcha: Swap parity comes from a hash of the pair and the vote count, so a ledger always yields the same proposal. Every tenth vote repeats an earlier pair with its sides swapped, if one is still unrepeated. Skip votes count as showings for the picker but do not move Elo.

src/core/tell-rules-color.ts.what: The colour and light tells: purple and cyan accents, warm cream surfaces, gradient text, a saturated glow on a dark surface, radial halos, stripe gradients, grey text on a saturated colour, a hairline border with a wide shadow, and a graph-paper background. Most are advisory.
src/core/tell-rules-color.ts.why: Precision over recall: each threshold is set so that a legitimate palette stays quiet.
src/core/tell-rules-color.ts.gotcha: The family accent context is a module-level variable set and cleared around a run. A run that does not clear it leaves the next run treating that hue as licensed. A purple that matches the declared family accent is reported as an advisory note, not as the generated-UI tell.

src/core/template-catalogue-check.ts.what: Lints the template description catalogue for its shape, duplicate and unsorted paths, and coverage of the registered templates, checked in both directions.
src/core/template-catalogue-check.ts.why: The catalogue is generated, so a stale or hand-edited file has to be caught.
src/core/template-catalogue-check.ts.gotcha: If the shape is wrong, the check returns only the shape errors and reports nothing else. The order check compares each path with the one before it using plain string comparison, so the builder's sort has to match it.

src/core/token-coverage-classify.ts.what: Classifies one CSS value as token (a declared custom property, or a literal equal to a token value), derived (calc, a percentage, or a relative unit), or raw. It also builds the literal index from the resolved tokens.
src/core/token-coverage-classify.ts.why: Coverage measures how much of the CSS draws on the token system, so each value has to land in one of the three classes.
src/core/token-coverage-classify.ts.gotcha: A percentage in a spacing, radius, font-size or shadow value counts as derived, so it is kept out of the raw count. Colour is excluded from the derived rule, because colour functions use percentages for saturation and lightness.

src/commands/a11y-lint.ts.what: `ui a11y-lint <file.html>`: runs the static accessibility checks on the page with its local linked CSS inlined. It exits 1 on any error-severity finding.
src/commands/a11y-lint.ts.why: The cheapest accessibility floor. The output repeats that a pass is not a conformance claim.
src/commands/a11y-lint.ts.gotcha: Errors about an unreadable linked stylesheet get the WCAG value n/a, so they appear without a success criterion attached. A clean run prints a note that rendered and behavioural criteria need a browser or a person.

src/commands/audit.ts.what: `ui audit <nodes.json>`: detects design-system violations in an exported node tree. It covers unbound fills that match a token, detached instances, raw icons where an Icon component exists, off-grid radii and spacing, and deprecated components. It can also emit a remap table.
src/commands/audit.ts.why: Detection is deterministic and needs no model. The remap table lets the canvas step apply the snap, so the edit is repeatable.
src/commands/audit.ts.gotcha: Without --tokens or --registry, the families that need them are not checked, and the output does not say so. The grid must be a positive integer. The warning count is always zero.

src/commands/chart.ts.what: `ui chart lint <chart.html>`: checks that a chart's self-contained HTML and its owned inline SVG follow the contract. It exits 1 on any error finding.
src/commands/chart.ts.why: Keeps a chart's output self-contained and its SVG in the form the rest of the tooling expects.
src/commands/chart.ts.gotcha: The lint reads only the file it is given, so anything a chart pulls in from elsewhere is not checked.

src/commands/color-format.ts.what: The text rendering helpers for `ui color`: the conversion line, a scale table with a WCAG label for each stop, a contrast line, and the semantic palette tables. Pure string formatting.
src/commands/color-format.ts.why: Keeps the colour command's output in one place, away from the colour maths.
src/commands/color-format.ts.gotcha: The WCAG levels in the scale table are computed inline with the thresholds 7, 4.5 and 3, not taken from the contrast module. A change to those thresholds there would not reach this table.

src/commands/designmd.ts.what: The dispatcher for `ui designmd`, routing extract-tokens, snapshot and audit to their implementations. The help text documents the audit exit codes and the --css rule.
src/commands/designmd.ts.why: One entry point for the DESIGN.md toolchain.
src/commands/designmd.ts.gotcha: The audit uses exit 2 for a warning-only result, which differs from most commands. A caller that treats any non-zero code as failure will read a warning-only audit as a failure.

src/commands/diagram.ts.what: `ui diagram lint <diagram.html>`: checks that a diagram's HTML is self-contained and that its inline SVG follows the owned contract. It exits 1 on any error finding.
src/commands/diagram.ts.why: The diagram contract requires self-contained HTML, so the file can be shared on its own.
src/commands/diagram.ts.gotcha: The lint reads only the file it is given, so anything the diagram loads from elsewhere is not checked.

src/commands/figma-reconcile-render.ts.what: The human text rendering for `ui figma reconcile`, in both dry-run and applied forms, over the same data as the JSON envelope. Control characters are stripped from node names, so an untrusted name cannot change the printed text.
src/commands/figma-reconcile-render.ts.why: The JSON envelope is the authoritative form, so the text must not claim more than it does.
src/commands/figma-reconcile-render.ts.gotcha: The applied line counts records that changed, never raw log events. The pending-target line suggests the skip command only when a blocking target exists. Names are cut to 80 characters unless a caller asks for more.

src/commands/ksync.ts.what: The dispatcher for `ui ksync`, routing pin, census and drift to their implementations. The help text describes the two frames-file shapes and the error codes.
src/commands/ksync.ts.why: One entry point for the Figma-to-code sync commands.
src/commands/ksync.ts.gotcha: A missing or unknown subcommand returns BAD_ARG. The command makes no network call and no model call, as its header says.

src/commands/onboard.ts.what: `ui onboard`: a read-only setup checklist for the project in the working directory. It covers the runtime adapters, git, the design system, the soul, the learning loop, and the optional project agents and Figma agent, and it names the next command to run. It always exits 0.
src/commands/onboard.ts.why: Tells a newcomer what is missing without changing anything.
src/commands/onboard.ts.gotcha: The git step looks only for a .git folder directly in the project directory, so a project inside a larger repository reports git as missing. The Figma hint depends on whether figma-agent is on PATH, which is checked by looking for the file rather than by running it.

src/commands/persona.ts.what: `ui persona lint <families.json>`: the thin-family floor. It flags a persona family whose screens-per-app ratio is below the floor, or that has fewer than three apps. It exits 1 when a thin family has no history note that excuses it.
src/commands/persona.ts.why: A family spread over too few screens or apps is not a dependable persona. The excuse rule turns a silent gap into a declared one.
src/commands/persona.ts.gotcha: The help text defines an excuse as a history note containing thin or provisional. The default floor is six screens per app, and the check is skipped entirely for a file that has no families array, which is reported as BAD_JSON.

src/commands/token-coverage.ts.what: `ui token-coverage <file.html>`: reports the share of colour, font, size, spacing, radius and shadow values the page takes from its tokens, and exits 1 below the floor. It also fails when a linked stylesheet cannot be read.
src/commands/token-coverage.ts.why: A page that hardcodes values a token already covers drifts away from the design system.
src/commands/token-coverage.ts.gotcha: With no --tokens, the command looks for a token file through the design-directory contract and then at brand/design/design.tokens.json. An unreadable linked stylesheet forces a failure even when the number clears the floor, because that number was computed over an incomplete page.

src/commands/validate-layout.ts.what: `ui validate-layout <file.html>`: the static structure and overflow linter. It runs 13 heuristic checks, such as a missing html, body or doctype, unbalanced tags, overflowing widths and viewport units. It exits 1 on error-severity findings only.
src/commands/validate-layout.ts.why: Catches structural faults that a browser would hide or silently repair.
src/commands/validate-layout.ts.gotcha: The command's one-line summary says it runs 12 checks, but the help text lists 13, so the summary is stale. Warnings never change the exit code.

src/core/adapter-wrapper-lint.ts.what: The wrapper half of `ui doctor --cwd`. Each generated wrapper must exist, carry frontmatter, and point at a template that still resolves. Antigravity bash blocks need a turbo marker, and a Codex file needs exactly one sentinel pair. The routing rule wrapper has its own strict frontmatter and reference checks.
src/core/adapter-wrapper-lint.ts.why: A wrapper that points at a missing template sends the host agent to nothing, and nothing else reports it.
src/core/adapter-wrapper-lint.ts.gotcha: Only the first problem in each wrapper is reported. The routing rule's frontmatter is parsed strictly: duplicate keys and a paths scope are both rejected.

src/core/brief-validate.ts.what: Validates a design brief against the bundled brief schema, including every nested rule, and reports each violation with its field path.
src/core/brief-validate.ts.why: One source for the brief's shape, so the schema and the validator cannot disagree.
src/core/brief-validate.ts.gotcha: The route lists exported beside the schema are for the route rules, not for validation. A test, not the code, keeps those lists in step with the schema.

src/core/build-evidence-rules-persuade.t.what: Rule r8 for a Persuade folder: both contact sheets (or a note recording why the bar sheet was not captured), a critic file with a rubric total out of 16 and a verdict, and a scroll-story probe output. Other folders are reported as SKIPPED.
src/core/build-evidence-rules-persuade.t.why: Adds the marketing-page proof that the general evidence rules do not ask for.
src/core/build-evidence-rules-persuade.t.gotcha: A folder counts as Persuade when it holds concept.md or a build contact sheet, so a folder with only a concept note is held to all of r8. The scroll-story check needs a file whose name contains scroll-story. The critic check accepts any file whose name starts with critic-.

src/core/content-checks-punctuation.ts.what: The dumb-punctuation warning: flags typewriter substitutes in visible copy, namely three or more dots instead of an ellipsis, straight apostrophes in contractions, and straight-quoted phrases instead of curly quotes. Scripts, styles, tags, attribute values and code containers are blanked first.
