src/core/content-checks-punctuation.ts.why: Typeset copy uses the typographic characters, and the substitutes read as unfinished.
src/core/content-checks-punctuation.ts.gotcha: Prime and inch marks after a digit, such as 8"x10", are never flagged. A quoted phrase is not flagged when a sentence boundary falls inside it, and it is cut off after 60 characters. Line numbers refer to the original source, because blanking keeps every newline.

src/core/delivery/delivery-art-evidence-.what: Validates the evidence behind an art-directed variant: the section boards, the fidelity references, and the asset manifest. Each section needs a board with a rationale and a reroll decision, and each production asset needs provenance and a local reference.
src/core/delivery/delivery-art-evidence-.why: An art-directed claim has to show which board covers which section, and where every production asset came from.
src/core/delivery/delivery-art-evidence-.gotcha: The board coverage check compares sets, so a duplicated section or board reference is caught separately. A production asset with no usage, or from source type none, is invalid. The validator checks the shape and the links between records, not the images themselves.

src/core/delivery/delivery-learning-prom.what: Validates the learnings in a learning record: each lesson's class and status, its links to known evidence cases, and whether a lesson marked promoted is supported. Support is either an expert approval with a reference, or winning evidence across three cases and two categories.
src/core/delivery/delivery-learning-prom.why: A lesson cannot be promoted on a single observation. The promotion gate asks for either a person's approval or a repeated pattern.
src/core/delivery/delivery-learning-prom.gotcha: A winning case counts only when the art-directed variant has zero critical failures and a higher mean score than the qualified variant. A missing score on any axis counts as minus one, so that trial cannot win.

src/core/designmd-audit-format.ts.what: The format audit family for DESIGN.md. It checks that the front matter parses, that all eight spec sections are present and in order, that there are no duplicate headings, that version is alpha if declared, and that every colour is a six-digit hex, every spacing and radius value has a px, em or rem unit, and every font size is a dimension.
src/core/designmd-audit-format.ts.why: Catches a file that is not shaped correctly before any source comparison starts.
src/core/designmd-audit-format.ts.gotcha: Synonymous section names are accepted. Each check adds one row, so a file with several problems gets several rows, not one. Colour and dimension checks run only when the group exists, so a missing group is not reported as a failure.

src/core/designmd-audit-ref-integrity.ts.what: The ref-integrity audit family for DESIGN.md. Every {group.name} reference in the YAML must resolve to a defined node.
src/core/designmd-audit-ref-integrity.ts.why: A reference that resolves to nothing ships a DESIGN.md that another tool cannot read.
src/core/designmd-audit-ref-integrity.ts.gotcha: The reference pattern is applied to every leaf value, so a literal brace in a description would be treated as a reference and reported if it does not resolve.

src/core/designmd-audit-source-fidelity..what: The source-fidelity audit family. It compares the colours and font families in the DESIGN.md with the source tokens from the extraction. It fails on any colour that is not in the source, warns about frequent source colours the document leaves out, and fails on any font family the source does not contain.
src/core/designmd-audit-source-fidelity..why: This is the check that catches an invented value: a colour or font the source never used.
src/core/designmd-audit-source-fidelity..gotcha: With no source tokens at all, every row downgrades to a warning. Pure black and white are excluded from the frequent-colour warning. A colour counts as in the source if it appears among the custom properties' resolved hex values as well.

src/core/ds-context-guidelines.ts.what: Builds the guidelines section of `ui ds context`: the pack's file index, its anti-pattern scenario titles with their status, and the tier-A rulings. The section fits the byte budget by dropping rulings from the tail first, then scenario titles, and it never drops the file index.
src/core/ds-context-guidelines.ts.why: A pack can be large, but a context block has a fixed budget, so the block has to say what it dropped.
src/core/ds-context-guidelines.ts.gotcha: A manifest that cannot be read is reported as unreadable in one line. The hard truncation cuts the encoded bytes, so a cut through a multi-byte character leaves a replacement character at the end of the text.

src/core/ds-guidelines-figma-upload.ts.what: Writes UPLOAD.md beside the Figma bundle folder, with the manual upload steps, the file table with sizes, the Figma limits, any warnings and trims, and any sources that no longer matched their seal.
src/core/ds-guidelines-figma-upload.ts.why: Figma offers no API for guidelines files during its beta, so the upload has to be done by hand, and the note explains how.
src/core/ds-guidelines-figma-upload.ts.gotcha: The file sits beside the folder, not inside it, so it is not uploaded by mistake. The Figma limits are a snapshot with a checked-on date, so they go stale and the note carries that date.

src/core/ds-guidelines-glossary-reader.t.what: Reads the terms from CONTEXT.md (the Language section, when there is one) and from ontology/glossary.yaml, which must use the flat shape, and merges them. Terms are matched case-insensitively, and the file read first wins.
src/core/ds-guidelines-glossary-reader.t.why: One merged vocabulary for the pack, with every disagreement recorded as a conflict instead of hidden.
src/core/ds-guidelines-glossary-reader.t.gotcha: The YAML reader is hand-written and accepts only the flat shape. Any other shape returns null, so the whole glossary is skipped with a reason rather than read in part. Parenthetical notes in an avoid list are dropped before the words are compared.

src/core/ds-soul-factory.ts.what: The factory soul: the stance design:os ships with, held as a compiled-in constant. It sits below the studio and project souls in the precedence chain, and each of those can override it clause by clause.
src/core/ds-soul-factory.ts.why: A product-design baseline that applies to every project out of the box, with no setup.
src/core/ds-soul-factory.ts.gotcha: The text is verbatim by design, and a test requires that it produce zero findings from the soul linter. Any change has to pass that test, so the baseline cannot drift from the check that teaches it.

src/core/evidence-model.ts.what: The pure shape of a user-evidence record (quote, metric or observation) and the anti-fabrication gate. quoteMatches checks that a quote appears verbatim inside its source text after whitespace normalisation, validateForAdd enforces the fields each kind needs, and parseEvidence validates one stored JSONL record.
src/core/evidence-model.ts.why: A design decision should trace back to what a real user said. Matching is verbatim and case-preserving, so the binary cannot put words in a user's mouth, and a quote shorter than 8 characters is rejected because a substring that short matches almost anything.
src/core/evidence-model.ts.gotcha: The quote rules run only when a record is added. parseEvidence accepts a stored record with kind quote and no quote field, so a hand-edited store can hold an unverifiable quote record that still reads as quoted.

src/core/figma-change-log-parser.ts.what: Parses and validates the append-only Figma change log, one JSON frame per line. It checks the schema version, timestamp, operation, node fields, origin, scope hint and page, then returns a typed ChangeFrame.
src/core/figma-change-log-parser.ts.why: The log is written by a separately bundled figma-agent, so this kernel validates the bytes it receives and does not import the producer's code. A malformed record fails the whole parse, so audit history is never skipped silently.
src/core/figma-change-log-parser.ts.gotcha: Blank lines are skipped, but a line that is only whitespace is also skipped without a warning. The fileName field is copied only when it is a string, so a record that carries it with the wrong type is rejected rather than cleaned up.

src/core/html-export.ts.what: String-only HTML export helpers: enhanceAccessibility adds lang, alt, rel and role attributes where they are missing, cleanHtmlForExport wraps a fragment in a full document and adds a title, minifyHtml strips comments and collapses whitespace, and toSafeFilename and toProjectPrefix build file names.
src/core/html-export.ts.why: Exported components have to open as standalone documents in any browser without a DOM. The helpers are pure strings, so the export is deterministic and testable in plain Node.
src/core/html-export.ts.gotcha: minifyHtml collapses all whitespace runs and removes the space between adjacent tags, so a space that separates two inline elements is lost. It also rewrites whitespace inside pre and textarea, which changes what those elements display.

src/core/knowledge-capability-check.ts.what: Cross-checks the capability catalog against the knowledge index, the need-routing Surface activation table, the workflow verbs, the command names and the repo files. It returns knowledge findings for missing witnesses, unknown workflows, unresolved evidence, incomplete refusals and drift between the table and the catalog.
src/core/knowledge-capability-check.ts.why: A capability can be marked available only when its knowledge, its machine, rendered and manual witnesses, and its evidence file all exist. Keeping the routing table and the catalog in agreement stops an agent from being routed to a capability that is not qualified.
src/core/knowledge-capability-check.ts.gotcha: indexIds returns an empty set when the knowledge index is not valid JSON, so every required knowledge id then reports as unknown. The real fault, a broken index, is never named. Evidence is resolved only up to the first # in the reference.

src/core/knowledge-source-ledger-check.t.what: Verifies the tracked MengTo source ledger. It checks the fixed JSON allowlist, the SHA-256 of each part, the embedded-payload rule, the tree and skill record shapes, the counts, the sort order, the decision mapping for each skill, and the duplicate blob groups.
src/core/knowledge-source-ledger-check.t.why: The ledger records which third-party skill files were adopted, covered, rejected or left out of scope, and that record must stay consistent with the files it describes. Metadata only: no base64 or data URI is allowed in it.
src/core/knowledge-source-ledger-check.t.gotcha: Every check returns as soon as it fails, so only the first problem in the ledger is reported. Fixing that one can reveal the next on a re-run.

src/core/layout-checks-delivery.ts.what: The avoidable-screenshot-crop warning. It fires when an img points at a crops/ path and the same document also references a real/ asset with the same role stem.
src/core/layout-checks-delivery.ts.why: The delivery-assets rule says to use the original when the source is already in reach. A crop that sits next to its own original is the avoidable case, and this check flags it.
src/core/layout-checks-delivery.ts.gotcha: It needs both images in the same HTML. A lone crop is never flagged, because the linter cannot see the original. The stem ignores dimension and DPR suffixes, so crops/hero-1560x1248.png and real/hero.webp match.

src/core/layout-checks-mobile.ts.what: Three mobile-reliability warnings: tap-spacing-cramped for a flex or grid container with a gap under 8px around two or more controls, input-font-below-16 for a text input under 16px, and edge-bar-no-safe-area for a fixed or sticky bottom bar with no safe-area padding.
src/core/layout-checks-mobile.ts.why: Each rule matches a known phone-browser failure: adjacent taps are mis-hit, iOS Safari zooms on focus of a small input, and the home indicator covers a bottom bar. Each check fires only on positive markup evidence, so ambiguous markup is left alone.
src/core/layout-checks-mobile.ts.gotcha: tap-spacing-cramped reads each container's contents only up to the first matching close tag, so nested containers are under-counted and missed. text-xs and text-sm always count as under 16px, even when an override class later sets a larger size.

src/core/layout-checks-viewport.ts.what: Three viewport and overflow warnings: css-100vw-width for a width that includes the scrollbar gutter, root-overflow-x-hidden for overflow hidden on html, body or :root, which breaks sticky, and dvh-over-100vh for a full-viewport height that jumps on mobile.
src/core/layout-checks-viewport.ts.why: Each one covers a horizontal overflow or mobile-height trap that the other layout checks do not see. The 100vh check exists because the mobile URL bar resizes the viewport, so 100vh clips content and then jumps.
src/core/layout-checks-viewport.ts.gotcha: The h-screen scan runs over the whole HTML, not only class attributes, so the word h-screen in visible text is flagged. The CSS-based findings carry no line number.

src/core/layout-checks.ts.what: The core static layout checks, each a pure regex function over the HTML: doctype, html and body roots, balanced structural tags, fixed widths over 1280px, viewport units on body, nested scroll containers, absolute without relative, images without dimensions, and empty flex or grid containers.
src/core/layout-checks.ts.why: They catch layout drift that a reviewer would otherwise find only by rendering the page. They are heuristics on purpose, because the linter has no DOM and no browser.
src/core/layout-checks.ts.gotcha: Two checks read words, not markup. absolute-without-relative matches the bare word anywhere in the page, including prose, and nested-scroll-container counts scroll declarations rather than true nesting. missing-doctype sits under the heading Error-severity checks, but it is emitted as a warning.

src/core/lint-target.ts.what: Resolves the lint arguments, which can be files, directories or globs, into one sorted list of lintable targets. Anything that no extractor claims is reported as skipped with a reason, and a walk that hits its entry budget reports that it was truncated.
src/core/lint-target.ts.why: A linter that silently drops files reads as covered when it is not. Alphabetical order and collapsed duplicates keep two runs over the same arguments byte-identical.
src/core/lint-target.ts.gotcha: One entry budget is shared across all the arguments, so a large first directory can use it up and leave the later arguments unexamined. describeResolution takes a cwd argument and a relative import that it never uses (void cwd; void relative;).

src/core/method-lint.ts.what: Lints a method run document. It validates the shape against the run schema, then applies the rules a schema cannot express: a skipped step needs a reason code and detail, a done decide or verify step needs every human question answered, define must reference a brief.json that passes the design-brief schema, and methodStatusLine renders one mark per step.
src/core/method-lint.ts.why: A method run is a record of human decisions. The skip-reason and unanswered-human rules keep a step from being marked done when the person it depends on has not answered.
src/core/method-lint.ts.gotcha: A shape error that does not name a step is treated as global, so every step in the status line shows a cross mark. The needs_humans rule is checked only for decide and verify, so an unanswered question on another step passes.

src/core/pattern-lint.ts.what: Pure linter for pattern cards. It adds the arithmetic a JSON schema cannot check: counts against n, evidence length against n, the floor of 8 screens, the rule that a single-valued distribution cannot sum above n, unreliable paths that must name an attribute the card carries, and the cross-check range. It also rejects any image path, image extension or URL, and checks the platform and archetype against the folder.
src/core/pattern-lint.ts.why: A pattern card summarises how many screens showed a pattern. The counts must add up, and a card with a small sample must say so. No image may enter a card, so the evidence stays as observed(mobbin:id) references.
src/core/pattern-lint.ts.gotcha: Only the single-valued distributions are summed. A multi-valued distribution can exceed n without a finding, which is intended. The floor check passes a card with n of 8 or more only when n_below_floor is absent or false.

src/core/prompt-plan/prompt-plan-directi.what: Validates the three design directions in a prompt plan. It requires exactly three directions, each with a score and the six structural fields, a selectedDirectionId that resolves, and a pairwise divergence test that needs at least four differing structural fields, including structuralThesis, focalMechanism and signatureTechnique.
src/core/prompt-plan/prompt-plan-directi.why: A direction set is only useful when the directions differ in structure, not in colour or copy. The divergence test is how the plan proves three options were actually explored.
src/core/prompt-plan/prompt-plan-directi.gotcha: Divergence is compared with strict equality on the raw values, so a whitespace or case change counts as a structural difference. If the set is incomplete, the function returns early and never checks the selection.

src/core/prompt-plan/prompt-plan-facet-v.what: Validates facet bindings and product truth. Every one of the seven facets and five cross-cutting layers needs one provenance-bound decision, a low-confidence assumption may not settle a decision-changing ambiguity, and the product truth block needs its audience, outcome, action, proof, claims and content inventory.
src/core/prompt-plan/prompt-plan-facet-v.why: Each design choice must trace back to a source, and an assumption cannot quietly decide something that would change the design. The product truth block keeps the plan tied to what the product actually does.
src/core/prompt-plan/prompt-plan-facet-v.gotcha: The product-truth check only confirms that availableProof, prohibitedClaims and contentInventory are arrays. An empty prohibitedClaims passes, so the check cannot tell a plan with no limits from one that has not listed any.

src/core/prompt-plan/prompt-plan-preflig.what: Validates the preflight checklist and the builder packet. The checklist must contain every required hard group, hard check and contextual check. A failing hard check becomes an error and a failing contextual check becomes a warning. The builder packet must stay within 6,000 tokens.
src/core/prompt-plan/prompt-plan-preflig.why: Preflight is the last gate before a plan goes to a builder. Requiring a fixed list means a check cannot be quietly dropped, and the token budget keeps the packet small enough to hand over whole.
src/core/prompt-plan/prompt-plan-preflig.gotcha: The budget is inclusive, so exactly 6,000 tokens passes and 6,001 fails. builder-packet-over-budget is also a listed hard check id, so the same finding name can come from two places.

src/core/prompt-plan/prompt-plan-proport.what: Validates the two proportion candidates, content-led and golden. Each needs a complete grid, scale, measure, breakpoint, region and ratio plan. Golden ratio applications need a content rationale and fallback, the golden ratio may dominate at most 40% of major regions, nesting is limited to two levels, and the golden candidate must declare the rules that release the ratio for responsive layouts.
src/core/prompt-plan/prompt-plan-proport.why: The golden ratio is easy to apply everywhere and then looks like decoration. These limits keep it in the few places where the content justifies it.
src/core/prompt-plan/prompt-plan-proport.gotcha: A row that leaves out nestingDepth or applicationsInRegion defaults to 1, so it always passes the nesting rule. The 40% rule is skipped entirely when the region count is zero.

src/core/prompt-plan/prompt-plan-region-.what: Validates the major regions of a prompt plan. Each region needs a complete production brief of 17 fields, unique ids, a repetition rationale when a layout model is reused, a supported visual type with a rationale, and a planned asset id for every image-led region.
src/core/prompt-plan/prompt-plan-region-.why: A region is the unit a builder works from, so each one has to say what it is for, how it is laid out and what visual it uses. Requiring a rationale for repeated layouts stops the page from defaulting to the same card in every section.
src/core/prompt-plan/prompt-plan-region-.gotcha: The visual-asset rule applies only to the four image types. A region set to none passes the visual checks once it has a rationale, so a region can be left without any visual and still validate.

src/core/prompt-plan/prompt-plan-system-.what: Validates the visual system and the delivery plan. The visual system needs eleven actionable fields, and a field may not be a bare mood word. The icon family must be Phosphor or have an exception reference. The delivery plan needs viewports, states, motion, reduced motion and a JavaScript fallback, with valid provenance and a complete contract on every visual asset.
src/core/prompt-plan/prompt-plan-system-.why: Mood words such as premium do not tell a builder what to build, so each field must name something implementable. Asset provenance keeps fake product or logo evidence out of the plan.
src/core/prompt-plan/prompt-plan-system-.gotcha: The mood-word test matches a single word only. clean, minimal passes, because the value is not exactly one of the listed words.

src/core/rendered/capture-page.ts.what: Renders a page in headless Chromium through the CDP client and records what the engine saw. It reads every body element in one injected expression, storing its computed styles, box, direct text, image state and scroll overflow. Console errors are collected from listeners attached before navigation, and the session is closed on every exit path.
src/core/rendered/capture-page.ts.why: The rules that judge a rendered page are pure functions of this capture, so they can be tested on fixtures with no browser. Reading everything in one expression avoids hundreds of protocol round trips for a large page.
src/core/rendered/capture-page.ts.gotcha: The settle time is a fixed 700 ms, so an animation that runs longer is read partway through. Only body and its descendants are captured, so anything in head is missing from the result.

src/core/rendered/cdp-client.ts.what: A zero-dependency Chrome DevTools Protocol client built on the global WebSocket and fetch of Node 22. It opens a page target, runs calls with a 15-second ceiling, routes events to listeners, and enables only the Runtime and Log domains. It reports a clear reason on Node builds that have no global WebSocket.
src/core/rendered/cdp-client.ts.why: The repo takes no browser dependency. Puppeteer would download its own Chromium and could give two machines different verdicts, so this drives the browser already installed. The 15-second ceiling stops a hung page from hanging the command.
src/core/rendered/cdp-client.ts.gotcha: If the attach or enable call fails, connect rejects without closing the socket or the target it has already created, so a failed start can leave a tab and a socket open.

src/core/rulings-validate.ts.what: Structural validation for a rulings file, mirroring schemas/rulings.schema.json by hand. It checks the schema header, the required and optional fields of each ruling, date formats, scope shape, status values, approver roles and supersession fields.
src/core/rulings-validate.ts.why: The kernel takes no schema library, so the validator is hand-written and a test pins its field lists to the schema file. A ruling that is not valid cannot quietly bind a design decision.
src/core/rulings-validate.ts.gotcha: Every finding is reported as an error, so the warning level in the finding type is never used. A malformed ruling is reported and the rest of the file is still checked.

src/core/snapshot-diff.ts.what: Compares two screenshots pixel by pixel. It is a zero-dependency port of the pixelmatch algorithm, using a YIQ colour delta and an anti-aliasing check, with rectangular masks for dynamic regions. It returns the count of real differing pixels, a diff ratio and a diff image.
src/core/snapshot-diff.ts.why: The binary never renders. It only compares PNGs that the host produced, so the comparison has to be deterministic and needs no browser. Anti-aliased edges are excluded by default because they are rendering noise, not design changes.
src/core/snapshot-diff.ts.gotcha: Two images of different sizes give a diff ratio of 1 and a blank white diff image, so the output does not show where the layout moved. Masked pixels are painted grey and never counted, so a mask that is too large hides real change.

src/core/taste-checks-concentric-radius..what: The equal-nested-radii warning, the concentric-corner check. It flags a padded container with an all-corners radius that holds a child with the same radius. Only the Tailwind radius utilities are compared, and the rule is closed by an emitter and a linter, as the repo requires.
src/core/taste-checks-concentric-radius..why: With padding between two surfaces, an inner corner at the outer radius looks pinched. The rule is written down in the design rubric, and this check makes it enforceable.
src/core/taste-checks-concentric-radius..gotcha: The check stops at the first rounded child of each container, so a parent whose first rounded child differs but whose second matches is not flagged. Raw CSS radii are not compared, because the cascade cannot be paired with a DOM path by a static scan.

src/core/taste-checks-depth.ts.what: Two stacking checks on the Depth and Surface axis. z-index-inflation is an error for all-nines or 32-bit maximum values. z-index-off-ladder is a warning for a value above nine that is not a multiple of ten.
src/core/taste-checks-depth.ts.why: A stacking order should be a designed scale. All-nines values mean someone ended an argument by making a value very large, and off-ladder values show that the scale was improvised.
src/core/taste-checks-depth.ts.gotcha: The off-ladder check compares magnitudes, so negative values are judged by their absolute value, and z-index: -15 is flagged while -20 is accepted. Values from zero to nine are never flagged, even though they are often unplanned.

src/core/taste-checks-font-scale.ts.what: The font-scale-sprawl check. It counts the distinct hand-picked font sizes in the document, meaning Tailwind arbitrary text sizes and raw font-size declarations in px, rem, em or pt, normalised to px. More than seven is a warning and more than ten is an error.
src/core/taste-checks-font-scale.ts.why: A designed type scale is a few steps on one ratio. Many unrelated sizes make a page look unauthored and break vertical rhythm.
src/core/taste-checks-font-scale.ts.gotcha: em is converted at a fixed 16px root, whatever the parent size, so a nested em value is deduplicated against the root value and can be undercounted. Named Tailwind steps and var() token references are never counted.

src/core/taste-checks-gsap.ts.what: Six machine checks for the GSAP part of the motion rules: development markers left in a delivered file, scrub and toggleActions set on one ScrollTrigger, plugins used without registerPlugin, a pinned element that is also transformed, GSAP motion with no reduced-motion branch, and will-change parked in a static rule. Each check is silent unless GSAP is in use.
src/core/taste-checks-gsap.ts.why: The motion guidance was prose only, and a standard that exists only as prose drifts. These rules are the part a static reader can decide, and the rest is left to the model.
src/core/taste-checks-gsap.ts.gotcha: The ScrollTrigger block match stops at the first brace, so a trigger whose config holds a nested object, such as a callback body, is not matched and its scrub and toggleActions are not compared. Attributes are blanked before plugin names are searched, so a plugin loaded by file name in a script tag is not read as a use.

src/core/taste-checks-invisible-surface..what: The mode-invisible-surface error. It flags a low-alpha white border, fill or ring on a light document, or a low-alpha black one on a dark document, because such a surface passes text-contrast checks and still separates nothing. The mode is read from the root element only.
src/core/taste-checks-invisible-surface..why: The classic bug is copying a dark-theme hairline onto a light page. Accessibility linters miss it because there is no text pair to test, so only this craft check catches it.
src/core/taste-checks-invisible-surface..gotcha: On a mixed page, with a light body and a dark section, the check gives up entirely and reports nothing, even for a real light-page fault elsewhere on that page. Text tints such as text-white/10 are never flagged, because only surface properties are compared.

src/core/taste-checks-motion-state.ts.what: Two motion checks for state changes. overshoot-easing is an error for a transition whose cubic-bezier control point lies outside the zero-to-one range. focus-ring-animates-in is an error when a focus indicator transitions into view, either through an outline in a transition list or through a focus rule that transitions box-shadow or outline.
src/core/taste-checks-motion-state.ts.why: Bounce easing on a state change looks generated, and a focus ring that fades in is slow to appear for keyboard users, who need an immediate indicator.
src/core/taste-checks-motion-state.ts.gotcha: The outline check searches every transition declaration in the stylesheet, not only focus rules. A button that fades its outline on hover is therefore reported as a focus-ring fault, even though it is not one.

src/core/taste-checks-nesting.ts.what: The container-nesting-depth warning. It walks the tags with a stack and counts runs of decorative container elements three or more levels deep. Landmarks, lists, tables, forms and any element with a role or aria attribute reset the count. A grid or flex parent's direct children count as track cells, not an extra level.
src/core/taste-checks-nesting.ts.why: Container soup, with a section inside a card inside a pill inside a tag, adds DOM weight and paint cost without adding structure. The check reports each independent chain once, at its deepest point.
src/core/taste-checks-nesting.ts.gotcha: Any role or aria attribute resets the count, so one aria-hidden wrapper stops the chain beneath it from being counted. Script and style contents are blanked before the walk.

src/core/taste-checks-radius.ts.what: The radius-sprawl warning. It counts the distinct non-zero border-radius values in the document, from CSS, inline styles, and Tailwind rounded utilities, normalised to px. All fully round values count as one pill bucket. More than four distinct values is a warning.
src/core/taste-checks-radius.ts.why: A designed surface uses a small radius scale. Many hand-picked corner radii make each card and input look like an independent choice.
src/core/taste-checks-radius.ts.gotcha: A bare rounded utility is counted as 4px, which is Tailwind's default, even if the project has overridden that default. Keys are compared after conversion, so 16px and 1rem count as one value.

src/core/taste-checks-tap-target.ts.what: The tap-target-undersized warning. It flags an interactive control, a button, a link or an input, or any element with a button role or onclick, whose fixed or minimum height is provably under 44px. It also flags an icon-only button with almost no vertical padding and no height token.
src/core/taste-checks-tap-target.ts.why: Touch targets under about 44px are hard to hit reliably on a phone, and the rubric's spacing rule depends on it. The check fires only on explicit size tokens, so a control styled in an external sheet is left alone.
src/core/taste-checks-tap-target.ts.gotcha: The icon-only prong looks only at button and a elements. A div with role=button that holds only an icon is never checked by that prong, even though the first prong would catch an explicit size on it.

src/core/taste-checks-video-scrub.ts.what: Four checks for scroll-scrubbed video. video-scrub-no-reduced-motion is an error when scroll drives currentTime with no reduced-motion branch. video-scrub-attrs is an error when a scrubbed video lacks muted or playsinline. safe-area-viewport-fit is an error when env(safe-area-inset) is used without viewport-fit=cover. video-poster-missing is a warning when a scrubbed video has no poster.
src/core/taste-checks-video-scrub.ts.why: Each rule guards a failure that a desktop review never shows. iOS paints a blank frame without the video attributes, and safe-area insets resolve to zero without viewport-fit=cover.
src/core/taste-checks-video-scrub.ts.gotcha: Once scrub wiring is detected, the attribute and poster checks test every video tag in the file, including an unrelated decorative video elsewhere on the page. The safe-area check is not gated on scrubbing, so it runs on any page that uses safe areas.

src/commands/autofix.ts.what: The ui autofix command. It reads one HTML file, applies the deterministic fix rules, and prints the fixed HTML to stdout with a summary on stderr. With --write it overwrites the file in place, and with --json it returns an envelope.
src/commands/autofix.ts.why: The fixes are mechanical and idempotent, so an agent can run them without review. Writing is opt-in, and a successful write with fixes is recorded in the audit trail.
src/commands/autofix.ts.gotcha: The audit record is written only when --write succeeds and at least one fix was applied. A run without --write, and a run that changes nothing, leave no trace in the audit log.

src/commands/brief.ts.what: The thin ui brief command. It routes the lint subcommand to the brief linter and the questions subcommand to the question renderer, and it returns BAD_ARG when no subcommand or an unknown one is given.
src/commands/brief.ts.why: The intake contract for a design brief is split so that linting, the D4 receipt and question rendering each live in their own module, and this file only dispatches.
src/commands/brief.ts.gotcha: The help text lists the exit codes for lint, but the dispatcher never sets an exit code itself. Those codes come from the lint module, so the help and the dispatcher can drift apart without a test failing.

src/commands/design.ts.what: The ui design command. It routes the lint subcommand to the design-directory linter and principles-index to the principles index writer, and it returns BAD_ARG for any other subcommand.
src/commands/design.ts.why: It owns the help text and error codes for the design/ directory contract, so an agent can learn the whole contract from one command.
src/commands/design.ts.gotcha: The error message for a missing subcommand names both subcommands, but the help text's error-code list does not include a code for an unknown subcommand, so the returned code is BAD_ARG only by convention.

src/commands/figma.ts.what: The ui figma command, which holds the help text and routing for two subcommands: reconcile, which previews or commits the change-log delta into the component registry, and comments, which triages a captured comments payload. It returns BAD_ARG for a missing or unknown subcommand.
src/commands/figma.ts.why: The kernel never calls Figma. The host captures payloads and this command only reads them, so the same input always gives the same answer and a run is repeatable.
src/commands/figma.ts.gotcha: reconcile previews by default, and --apply advances the persisted cursor. A retry-queue target with no timeout blocks the cursor until someone passes --skip by hand, and --skip cannot be combined with --apply or --dry-run.

src/commands/judge.ts.what: The ui judge command. It routes record, which appends one shadow judgment to a ledger, and report, which computes agreement between the shadow pick and the human decision, and it returns BAD_ARG for a missing or unknown subcommand.
src/commands/judge.ts.why: The System One judge records what a model would have picked next to what the human chose. It never enforces anything, so it can be trusted to run beside real decisions while the team decides whether to rely on it.
src/commands/judge.ts.gotcha: Like the other thin dispatchers, this file never touches the ledger itself, so the only checks that protect the data are the ones inside the record and report modules.

src/commands/parse-json-stream.ts.what: The ui parse-json-stream command. It reads a file or stdin, extracts every complete JSON object from the stream, and prints them as NDJSON, with a summary on stderr. With --strict it fails when unparsed bytes remain, and with --json it returns the objects and the remainder.
src/commands/parse-json-stream.ts.why: Model output and log streams often arrive as concatenated JSON. The parser keeps whatever is complete and reports the rest, so a truncated stream is visible instead of silently dropped.
src/commands/parse-json-stream.ts.gotcha: The stderr count uses the raw remainder length, but --strict decides on the trimmed one. A remainder that is only whitespace is therefore reported as trailing bytes and still passes --strict.

src/commands/strip-fences.ts.what: The ui strip-fences command. It reads a file or stdin, removes the code-fence wrappers that a model puts around HTML, and writes the result to stdout. It never writes a file, and --json reports which fences were removed.
src/commands/strip-fences.ts.why: Models often wrap an HTML answer in a markdown fence or add prose around it. Stripping those wrappers before the HTML is linted or published stops the wrapper from being read as page content.
src/commands/strip-fences.ts.gotcha: Text mode always adds a newline, so output that already ends with one gets an extra blank line. The fence stripping itself is not repeated here, because it lives in the shared stream module.

src/commands/tenant-lint.ts.what: The ui tenant-lint command. It loads the file's linked stylesheets, lints the markup against the Tenant contract for embeddable motion sections, and exits 1 when any finding exists. Every finding is an error, because a breach of the Tenant Law is absolute.
src/commands/tenant-lint.ts.why: An embeddable motion section must not touch global page state, such as window scroll, the body height or the root variables, or it breaks the page it is dropped into. This command is the deterministic floor for that contract.
src/commands/tenant-lint.ts.gotcha: A stylesheet that fails to load is reported with line 0, because the loader has no line to give. The report therefore prints it as file:0, which points at nothing in the file.

src/core/brief-rules.ts.what: The route rules and the D4 receipt for a design brief. findBlockingFields lists the fields that still block an app-style route, such as screens, states, roles, status transitions and copy language, and open assumptions. d4Receipt counts those blockers and returns CONTINUE only when at most two block, none of them changes the route, and at most three assumptions are low-confidence.
src/core/brief-rules.ts.why: An intake should stop before work starts when a wrong guess would change the route or cannot be undone. The receipt turns that judgment into a fixed rule that a reader can check.
src/core/brief-rules.ts.gotcha: Landing pages return no blockers at all, even when they have assumptions with unknown provenance, so the open-question rule does not apply to them.

src/core/build-evidence-rules-deviations.what: Rule r5 of the build-evidence linter. It requires a deviations.md file and checks that every entry, a bullet, a D-numbered paragraph or a table row, names a measurement with a unit or a ratio. It also exports the helpers that find and read deviations.md for the other rules.
src/core/build-evidence-rules-deviations.why: A deviation from the design has to be a measured claim, not a feeling. An entry with no number and unit cannot be checked later, so the rule makes each one checkable.
src/core/build-evidence-rules-deviations.gotcha: Only px, ms, pt, em, rem, percentages and N:1 ratios count as measurements. An entry such as 16 pixels or 3 seconds names a number but fails the rule, because the unit is not on the list.

src/core/build-evidence-rules-gates.ts.what: Two rules over the gate logs. r4 requires gates.txt to name an inlined variant and requires every non-zero exit= line to be explained by a keyword in deviations.md. r6 requires a deliberately bad run with a non-zero exit, a red probe, to appear in gates.txt or falsification.txt.
src/core/build-evidence-rules-gates.ts.why: A passing gate proves little unless a failing one was seen, and a failure is only acceptable when it is written down as a known deviation. These rules check both halves.
src/core/build-evidence-rules-gates.ts.gotcha: r4 accepts an exit code when any keyword appears as a substring of deviations.md, so a short keyword such as gate matches any word that contains it, for example aggregate.

src/core/chart-lint.ts.what: The chart linter, the checking half of the chart emitter. It requires a supported grammar, a reading order, a focal element, a source kind and a declared baseline. Bar and pyramid charts must use a zero baseline, series need stable ids and labels, and two value axes on one frame are refused.
src/core/chart-lint.ts.why: A chart can lie through its baseline, its colours or a second scale, and this check makes each of those declared and visible. The check proves the contract holds, and the taste rubric judges whether the encoding is honest.
src/core/chart-lint.ts.gotcha: warningCount is always 0, because every chart check reports as an error. A caller that expects warnings from this linter will never see them.

src/core/design-dir-principles.ts.what: Builds the machine index of design principles from the level-three headings of design/principles.md. It records each principle's id, title, yields-when text and test text, and reports duplicate ids and missing bullets. Headings inside code fences are ignored.
src/core/design-dir-principles.ts.why: Every other tool reads the JSON index, so the markdown is parsed in one place. The index lets a checker quote a principle by its id without reading the whole prose file.
src/core/design-dir-principles.ts.gotcha: Only level-three headings are recognised. A principle written as a level-two or level-four heading is skipped silently, and no problem is reported, so the index can be quietly short.

src/core/design-dir-scan.ts.what: The filesystem and git view of a project root for ui design lint. When the root is its own git repository it lists tracked and untracked but not ignored files from git, otherwise it walks the directory itself. It exposes read and mtime lookups, and the rule code never touches the disk.
src/core/design-dir-scan.ts.why: Keeping the disk access in one place lets the lint rules be tested against an in-memory view. Using git's file list keeps ignored build output out of the contract checks.
src/core/design-dir-scan.ts.gotcha: The walk stops at 200,000 entries with no warning, so a very large tree is checked only in part and the report does not say so. When the root is not its own repository, the walk also ignores .gitignore and lists ignored files.

src/core/designmd-audit-report.ts.what: Assembles the five audit families into one result, with the counts, the timings and the worst status, and renders it as audit.md and audit.json. The worst status sets the exit code: PASS is 0, WARN is 2 and FAIL is 1.
src/core/designmd-audit-report.ts.why: Keeping the report a pure transform means the same rows always give the same file. A reviewer reads the Markdown and a script reads the JSON, and both come from one result.
src/core/designmd-audit-report.ts.gotcha: Rows are collected by walking the fixed FAMILY_ORDER list. A family added to the type but missing from that list would have its rows dropped without any count showing the loss.

src/core/diagram-lint.ts.what: The diagram linter, the checking half of the diagram emitter. It requires a supported grammar, a reading order, a focal element and a source kind, and it requires product-flow diagrams to come from flow-json with a source id on every node and edge. Connectors must be orthogonal, except in loop, org-chart and tree diagrams, and no two connectors may share geometry.
src/core/diagram-lint.ts.why: Orthogonal routing and unique connectors are what make a diagram readable. The product-flow source rule keeps a diagram traceable to the flow it was drawn from.
src/core/diagram-lint.ts.gotcha: Duplicate connectors are compared as text after whitespace is collapsed, so the same path written with different number formats, such as 10 and 10.0, is not reported as a duplicate.

src/core/ds-docs.ts.what: Builds the component reference from the registry, with the variants, states and tokens of each component grouped by category, and renders it as Markdown. Each component also lists the common states it does not declare.
src/core/ds-docs.ts.why: Generated reference docs do not decay the way hand-written ones do. The missing-states prompt points a designer at the states that most often get forgotten.
src/core/ds-docs.ts.gotcha: The same five states, focus, disabled, loading, error and empty, are suggested for every component, including static ones such as a divider. A static component therefore always shows a Consider adding line that does not fit it.

src/core/ds-guidelines-figma-sections.ts.what: Splits a canonical guidelines file into sections on its level-two headings, skipping generated blocks, and turns a section's bullets into individually droppable units. Each unit takes its id from the bold ruling name, the term id or the first 40 characters, and reads a since date when one is present.
src/core/ds-guidelines-figma-sections.ts.why: When the pack must fit a token budget, whole rulings can be dropped and the rest kept. Splitting on bullets is what lets a single ruling go without taking its neighbours.
src/core/ds-guidelines-figma-sections.ts.gotcha: Continuation lines of a multi-line bullet are not part of its unit, so they stay in the section when the bullet is dropped. Two bullets that share their first 40 characters also share an id.

src/core/ds-guidelines-grammar-soul-sect.what: Builds grammar.md by copying every CONVENTIONS.md section that has DO or DON'T lines into generated blocks, and builds the stance summary for overview.md from soul.md, capped at 40 lines. When a source is missing or has nothing to copy, it writes a not-measured placeholder and records the skip.
src/core/ds-guidelines-grammar-soul-sect.why: The grammar is copied, never re-derived, so the pack can only say what the project measured. The cap keeps a long stance from crowding out the rest of the overview.
src/core/ds-guidelines-grammar-soul-sect.gotcha: The stance summary starts at the first level-two heading, so any text in soul.md before that heading is dropped without a skip record. A short preamble that carries a rule is lost quietly.

src/core/edit-strategy-apply.ts.what: Applies a line-number diff to HTML. Each chunk is tried at its stated line and then within five lines either way, and the whole patch fails if any chunk fails. On failure it reports, for each chunk, the nearest matching window in the document, so a model can repair the diff before a full regeneration is needed.
src/core/edit-strategy-apply.ts.why: Patching a few lines is far cheaper and safer than regenerating a whole page, and a near-miss should be repaired rather than thrown away.
src/core/edit-strategy-apply.ts.gotcha: A chunk with no old lines can never match, because both the exact and the fuzzy path require at least one line to compare. A pure insertion therefore cannot be expressed in this format and always forces a full regeneration.

src/core/edit-strategy.ts.what: Chooses an edit strategy for a change request: deterministic for simple colour or text swaps, full regeneration for large structural changes, and a line-number diff otherwise. It also numbers lines for the model and parses the diff format, and it re-exports the patcher from its sibling module.
src/core/edit-strategy.ts.why: Routing small edits to a diff keeps the model's output short and leaves the rest of the page untouched. Routing big rebuilds to a full regeneration avoids patching a page that needs redrawing.
src/core/edit-strategy.ts.gotcha: The full-regeneration patterns match substrings without word boundaries, so the word all matches inside call. A request such as making the call-to-action text bigger is sent to full regeneration instead of a diff.

src/core/figma-change-coalescer.ts.what: Reduces the validated change frames of one batch to one state per file and node pair. It keeps the strongest operation, the latest name and page, and the widest scope, and it returns each node's changed properties and frame range in a stable order.
src/core/figma-change-coalescer.ts.why: A batch often holds many edits to the same component. Reducing them to one record per node lets the registry be updated once, in a deterministic order.
src/core/figma-change-coalescer.ts.gotcha: BUG (read, not reproduced): The operation rank puts deleted above created, so a node deleted and then recreated in the same batch is still reported as deleted. The later creation is never applied to the record.

src/core/figma-comment-delta.ts.what: Reports what changed in a Figma comment payload after a given time. It counts new threads, new replies, threads resolved since the cutoff, and resolved threads that still received replies, which the resolve-only view would hide.
src/core/figma-comment-delta.ts.why: Resolution cannot be the only filter. A reply inside a resolved thread is often a live instruction from the owner, and a timestamp is the only reliable way to see what moved since the last triage.
src/core/figma-comment-delta.ts.gotcha: parseSince rejects only strings that Date.parse cannot read, so it accepts forms other than ISO 8601, such as 15 Aug 2026, even though its error message says ISO 8601 is required.

src/core/figma-comment-verdict.ts.what: Reads the owner's verdict on a thread that the owner posted. A thread with no reply is silent, which is not acceptance. Otherwise the last reply is classed as accepted for a bare acknowledgement, reversed for a withdrawn or inverted requirement, and conditional for anything else.
src/core/figma-comment-verdict.ts.why: A resolved Figma thread does not mean the work was accepted, and a shipped task once contradicted its own thread. Only the owner's words count as a verdict, so completion comes from the person who set the requirement.
src/core/figma-comment-verdict.ts.gotcha: The verdict reads the last reply whoever wrote it, so a reviewer's bare ok after the owner's reversal reads as accepted. Only the thread's root author is checked.

src/core/figma-preview-delta.ts.what: Turns coalesced Figma changes into a preview of the component registry: what would be added, updated, deprecated, or left unresolved. A deletion becomes a deprecation. A name that appears in more than one file in the same batch is held back as a collision, and a component with no name is held back as unresolved.
src/core/figma-preview-delta.ts.why: A preview lets a designer see the registry change before anything is written. Holding collisions back means two files that share a name cannot silently overwrite one component.
src/core/figma-preview-delta.ts.gotcha: Any changed component that already exists goes into the updated list, even when every changed property is visual and maps to no registry field. Such an entry carries an empty fields list, so a visual-only change still shows up as an update.

src/core/figma-sync-state.ts.what: Reads and writes the Figma sync state file, which holds the apply cursor, the per-file cursors, the retry queue, the forced-bypass log and the skip history. Bad entries are dropped one at a time, and the audit trails are capped at 500 entries with a running count of what was evicted.
src/core/figma-sync-state.ts.why: The change-log is the source of truth, and this file is the one mutable marker that says how far it has been applied. Rejecting bad entries one at a time keeps one corrupt target from stalling every other target.
src/core/figma-sync-state.ts.gotcha: A state file that is not valid JSON is read as cursor 0 with nothing else, so the whole log is applied again and any skip acknowledgements or retry-queue entries in it are lost without a record.

src/core/json-schema-subset.ts.what: A small validator for the draft-07 keywords the shipped schemas use. It checks type, const, enum, required, properties, additionalProperties, items, minItems, minLength, pattern, allOf and if/then, and it throws on any keyword outside that list.
src/core/json-schema-subset.ts.why: The kernel takes no schema library, so this subset is hand-written. Throwing on an unknown keyword means an edit to a schema cannot quietly stop being enforced.
src/core/json-schema-subset.ts.gotcha: The type check knows only number, not integer, so a schema that says type integer rejects every number. A null value also satisfies required and properties, because the required check looks only for undefined.

src/core/judge-report-build.ts.what: Computes, for each decision point, how often the shadow judge's pick was accepted by the human, with counts for changed and rejected decisions. Below five resolved judgments the report prints a count and no rate. It also lists persona-family judgments that name a family missing from the table.
src/core/judge-report-build.ts.why: A rate built on a handful of decisions would look like evidence it is not. The minimum sample keeps the judge's agreement from being read before there is enough data.
src/core/judge-report-build.ts.gotcha: The rejected count is computed as everything resolved that is neither accepted nor changed, so any unexpected decision value is counted as a rejection.

src/core/knowledge-gradient-catalog-pars.what: Parses and shape-checks the gradient catalog ledger, with its named presets and its shader-by-mesh surfaces, and parses the six-column preset matrix rows out of the knowledge file. The catalog parser returns null on any violation, so a half-valid roster is never used.
src/core/knowledge-gradient-catalog-pars.why: A partial roster would make the matrix check pass while skipping part of the matrix. Keeping the presets and the surfaces as separate arrays stops every preset having to repeat the shader choice.
src/core/knowledge-gradient-catalog-pars.gotcha: The matrix parser keeps only rows with exactly six cells, so a matrix row that gains a column is ignored silently and is not reported as drift.

src/core/knowledge-gradient-matrix-emit..what: Emits the machine columns of the preset matrix from the gradient ledger: the provenance marker, the header, and one row per preset with its name, slug and mesh. The narrative, anti-use and fallback cells are left empty on purpose, for a person to write.
src/core/knowledge-gradient-matrix-emit..why: The emitter must not invent the accessibility claim or the anti-use text, because those are the fields whose job is to refuse a wrong use. An empty cell fails the linter until someone writes it.
src/core/knowledge-gradient-matrix-emit..gotcha: The matrix shows name, slug and mesh only. The light and grain values from the ledger are not written into the matrix, so those two settings never appear in the table.

src/core/knowledge-index-emit.ts.what: Builds the routing index over the knowledge core, one entry per knowledge file, from the front-matter of each file, plus entries for the JSON data files in the personas and patterns folders. It also parses the front-matter with a small hand-written reader, not a YAML library.
src/core/knowledge-index-emit.ts.why: An agent routing a task should read a short index, not every knowledge file. A hand-written reader keeps the kernel free of runtime dependencies and rejects anything it does not understand.
src/core/knowledge-index-emit.ts.gotcha: The front-matter ends at the first line that starts with three dashes, so a body line such as a horizontal rule of four dashes would close the block early and be read as the end of the front-matter.

src/core/knowledge-promotion-render.ts.what: Renders the candidates file that a promotion run writes for a librarian to review. It groups candidates by category and gives each one its reason, scope, principle, detail and sources, with a header that states the gate.
src/core/knowledge-promotion-render.ts.why: A librarian reviews the file, not the ledger. Stating the gate and the counts in the header lets the reviewer see how each candidate got there.
src/core/knowledge-promotion-render.ts.gotcha: The header says the output is scrubbed of names, hostnames and paths, but this renderer does no scrubbing. It trusts that its input was cleaned upstream, and nothing here would catch a name that was not.

src/core/knowledge-routing-check.ts.what: Checks the anchored Route table in the need-routing guide against the workflow verbs. A route verb that is not a workflow verb is an error, and a workflow verb with no route row is an error, so a shipped capability cannot go untaught.
src/core/knowledge-routing-check.ts.why: The routing guide is what generated agents read to decide which capability to use. A verb with no row is a feature that no agent will ever pick.
src/core/knowledge-routing-check.ts.gotcha: Only the last cell of each row counts as the route. A row whose last cell is a note, such as see below, is read as having no route, so its verb is reported as uncovered even though the row names it.

src/core/knowledge-source-ledger-parse.t.what: Parses the tracked third-party source ledger, meaning its manifest, its skill decision file and its tree records, and rejects any shape that does not match the fixed key sets. It pins the source id and the upstream repository to exact values.
src/core/knowledge-source-ledger-parse.t.why: The ledger records what was adopted from an outside source and under which licence evidence. A strict shape check means a changed or hand-edited ledger fails before it can be trusted.
src/core/knowledge-source-ledger-parse.t.gotcha: The upstream repository is pinned to one exact URL, so a ledger captured from a mirror or a fork is rejected as invalid, even when its content is correct.

src/core/ksync-census.ts.what: Counts how much of the route manifest is built, placeholder, orphan or parked, and how much of the built part is pinned to a Figma frame. Each manifest entry takes its label from a parked marker, then its own status, then a labels file, and otherwise counts as unlabelled or as the status the caller assumes.
src/core/ksync-census.ts.why: The kernel cannot read the code, so it cannot tell a built screen from a placeholder. The census therefore reads the labels it is given and says so when it had to assume one.
src/core/ksync-census.ts.gotcha: A labels row whose status is not one of the four allowed values is dropped without a message, so a typo in the labels file leaves that entry unlabelled and nothing reports it.

src/core/ksync-drift.ts.what: Compares each pin with the frame snapshot the host captured and gives each pin one of four states: OK, DRIFT, MISSING or UNCHECKABLE. The overall verdict is STALE-INGEST when the snapshot is too old, EMPTY when there are no pins, CLEAN when every pin is OK, and DRIFT otherwise.
src/core/ksync-drift.ts.why: A CLEAN result is only meaningful when every pin was checked against a fresh snapshot. The verdict order makes an old or missing snapshot read as stale before any pin is judged.
src/core/ksync-drift.ts.gotcha: A pin that cannot be checked is UNCHECKABLE, but the verdict treats it as not clean and reports DRIFT, even though nothing has changed. The verdict says drift when the real condition is that the check could not run.

src/core/model-adapter-registry.ts.what: Holds the table of host-model invocations for each runtime and builds the small shell wrapper that normalises each host to the harvest contract: the prompt comes in on stdin and the model's text goes out on stdout. The arg-mode wrapper reads the prompt into a shell variable and passes it as one quoted argument, never through eval.
src/core/model-adapter-registry.ts.why: The learning loop needs one fixed way to call the user's own model, whatever host they run. Each invocation was probed live, so the table is kept exact and changed only after a new probe.
src/core/model-adapter-registry.ts.gotcha: The wrapper text hardcodes the host commands, so editing the argv in the table does not change the wrapper that is written. The two can drift apart without a test failing.

src/core/redirect-stub.ts.what: Detects a document that is only a meta refresh to another URL, with almost no visible text. Such a document is an intentional redirect, not a page, so the title and language checks are skipped for it.
src/core/redirect-stub.ts.why: The same detection is shared by two linters so that a redirect page is treated the same way everywhere. Gating a redirect for a title it does not need is noise.
src/core/redirect-stub.ts.gotcha: The 40-character test counts text after removing tags only, so the text inside an inline script or style block counts toward it. A redirect page with a long inline script is therefore not treated as a stub.

src/core/seam-allowlist.ts.what: Parses the allowlist of approved runtime prose reads and checks the reads found in the source against it. A read not on the list is an error, and an allowance that no longer matches any read is also an error.
src/core/seam-allowlist.ts.why: Reads of prose at runtime are a seam where behaviour can drift without a test noticing. Requiring each one to be listed and explained keeps every such read a conscious decision.
src/core/seam-allowlist.ts.gotcha: The line number is not part of the match, so an allowance still matches after its read moves within the same file, provided the call and the path list are unchanged. Only the duplicate check uses the line.

src/core/specimen-check.ts.what: Checks that a component's declared states cover the states its kind of control needs. A form control that models hover, pressed or loading must also declare disabled, and a data container must declare an empty state. A gap on a component marked stable is an error, and any other gap is a warning.
src/core/specimen-check.ts.why: The component design guidance lists the states that get forgotten most often. This turns that list into a check, and it avoids asking for focus, which is usually a runtime state rather than a design variant.
src/core/specimen-check.ts.gotcha: States are read only from the state, status and interaction dimensions and from the states list. A state written under any other dimension name, such as Mode=Disabled, is not counted, so the component is reported as missing it.

src/core/svg-artifact.ts.what: The checks that every owned inline SVG artifact shares, whether diagram or chart. They cover the root role, the labelledby pair of title and description, placeholders, scripts, external references, and colour attributes that bypass the design system's tokens.
src/core/svg-artifact.ts.why: The same promises apply to every SVG the tool produces, so the rule is written once. A fix made here reaches both the diagram and the chart linter.
src/core/svg-artifact.ts.gotcha: The owned SVG is found with a non-greedy match that stops at the first closing svg tag. A nested svg inside the artwork ends the block early, so the rest of the drawing is skipped by the colour and reference checks.

src/core/taste-dhash.ts.what: Computes a 64-bit difference hash of a PNG screenshot, a coarse fingerprint used to flag near-duplicate screenshots. It also measures the bit distance between two hashes. Anything that is not a readable PNG gives no hash rather than an error.
src/core/taste-dhash.ts.why: A hash lets ingest catalogue screenshots and spot likely duplicates within a genre without a model. Undecodable files still get a sha256, so they are not lost.
src/core/taste-dhash.ts.gotcha: The distance is counted over the shorter of the two strings, so comparing a hash with a truncated or empty one reports a small distance instead of an error.

src/core/tell-rules-surface.ts.what: The surface and card tells: a one-sided accent border on a rounded surface, a thin border meeting a large radius, a card inside another card, one spacing value used everywhere, cramped padding on a surface, cards with no horizontal gutter, and the same copy repeated across containers. Several of them need structure facts before they will fire.
src/core/tell-rules-surface.ts.why: These are the most recognisable generated-interface habits. Requiring structure before judging nesting stops a page with two unrelated radii from being called a nested card.
src/core/tell-rules-surface.ts.gotcha: The gutter test looks for any horizontal margin or left padding anywhere on the page. One unrelated padding-left on a button therefore clears the edge-flush-cards rule for every card.

src/core/tenant-lint.ts.what: Runs the Tenant-contract checks over an HTML document. It scans inline scripts and styles, and linked local scripts and stylesheets when a base directory is given, then walks the tags once for sticky-killing ancestors. Every finding is an error.
src/core/tenant-lint.ts.why: An embeddable motion section is a guest on someone else's page, so it must not change global scroll or layout state. This linter is the deterministic floor for that rule.
src/core/tenant-lint.ts.gotcha: A linked script that is missing or cannot be read is skipped without a finding, so its contents go unchecked and nothing says so. Only the stylesheet path reports load errors.

src/core/token-pairs.ts.what: Infers the foreground and surface token pairs from token paths alone, following the shadcn convention of a role token and its foreground sibling. It also accepts the counted synonyms text, fg, content and ink, and falls back to a same-group background, bg, surface or base sibling when the base is only a category.
src/core/token-pairs.ts.why: Contrast checks need to know which text sits on which surface. Pairing declared tokens replaces the guess of pairing every text with every surface, which had produced false contrast failures.
src/core/token-pairs.ts.gotcha: The function sees only paths, not token types, so a non-colour token that ends in -text, such as a typography style, pairs with a sibling -bg token if one exists.

src/adapters/skill-refs.ts.what: A static map from each workflow verb to the skills that the verb's template invokes. The Claude and Antigravity adapter generators both read it, so the two runtimes reference the same skills for a verb.
src/adapters/skill-refs.ts.why: Keeping the map in one place means the two adapters cannot disagree about which skills a verb needs.
src/adapters/skill-refs.ts.gotcha: Nothing in this file checks the map against the templates, so a skill renamed or removed in a template stays listed here under its old name until someone edits the map by hand.

src/commands/export.ts.what: The ui export command. It writes a cleaned, self-contained copy of one HTML file, with a title that is either given, taken from the existing title, or taken from the file name. --minify collapses whitespace and comments, and --zip is refused with NOT_IMPLEMENTED.
src/commands/export.ts.why: A single file that opens on its own is what gets shared or handed to a client. Cleaning it in one step removes preamble text and adds the missing doctype, viewport and charset.
src/commands/export.ts.gotcha: BUG (read, not reproduced): Without --out, the default name is the input's name with a .html extension, so exporting index.html writes to index.html, which is the input file. The write replaces the source without any warning. Found by reading the code; not reproduced.

src/commands/gflow.ts.what: The ui gflow i2v command. It runs one video-generation leg through the external gflow tool, never the chained form, checks that exactly one new MP4 was downloaded, and extracts that clip's last frame with ffmpeg as the seed for the next leg. Each run uses its own isolated download folder, and files are published by hard link so no existing file is ever replaced.
src/commands/gflow.ts.why: A paid generation must not be followed by a failure that loses its output. The preflight, the isolated folders and the no-overwrite publishing keep each run's files attributable to that run.
src/commands/gflow.ts.gotcha: BUG (read, not reproduced): ffmpeg is checked before gflow runs, but the seed extraction runs after the video is published. If extraction fails, the command returns FFMPEG_FAILED while the MP4 is already in the output folder.

src/commands/method.ts.what: The ui method command. It routes the lint subcommand to the method-run linter, and any other input gets a BAD_ARG error with the help pointer.
src/commands/method.ts.why: The six-step method run is checked by one linter, and this file only exposes it through the command line.
src/commands/method.ts.gotcha: Its help text describes the error codes, but the dispatcher itself returns only BAD_ARG, so the other documented codes come from the linter and not from here.

src/commands/pattern.ts.what: The ui pattern command. It routes the lint subcommand to the pattern-card linter and returns BAD_ARG for any other subcommand.
src/commands/pattern.ts.why: Pattern cards are checked by one linter, and this file only exposes it through the command line.
src/commands/pattern.ts.gotcha: The help text lists the checks the linter performs, such as shares over n, the floor and the no-image rule, but those rules are defined in the linter module and not here, so the help can go stale without a test catching it.

src/commands/scan.ts.what: The ui scan command. It reads a project directory, prints the framework, styling, component directories, design-system state and a verdict line, and exits 0 for any readable directory. Only an unreadable root or a stray argument gives an error.
src/commands/scan.ts.why: A new user needs to know whether to learn an existing UI or generate a new one. The verdict is data, so an existing project is never reported as a failure.
src/commands/scan.ts.gotcha: The verdict lines name slash commands such as /ui:learn as fixed text, so renaming a command means editing this file as well as the command itself.

src/commands/schema.ts.what: The ui schema command. It emits the full invocation contract for every subcommand as JSON, or a compact per-command listing as text. Positionals, flags, enum values and error codes all come from the signature table.
src/commands/schema.ts.why: A host model should read the contract rather than parse help prose. Emitting it from the same table as the parser keeps the contract and the commands in step.
src/commands/schema.ts.gotcha: The global error codes are a constant in this file, not part of the signature table. The contract is therefore built from two places, and a new global code added to the table would not appear in the output.

src/commands/scrub-scaffold.ts.what: The ui scrub-scaffold command. It writes the bundled build-assets.sh script into a target folder, marks it executable, and refuses to overwrite an existing file unless --force is given. The script encodes a clip chain to the scrub floor, and the binary never runs ffmpeg itself.
src/commands/scrub-scaffold.ts.why: The floor for scroll-scrubbed video was a set of values a person retyped for each project. A runnable script removes the retyping, and ui scrub-lint checks the result.
src/commands/scrub-scaffold.ts.gotcha: The files are written one at a time, so if the second write fails the first one is already on disk. The error is reported, but the partial output is left in place.

src/commands/seam.ts.what: The ui seam command. It routes the lint subcommand to the seam ratchet, which fails on any new runtime prose read in the kernel source and on any allowance that no longer matches a read.
src/commands/seam.ts.why: Prose read at runtime is a place where behaviour can change without a test noticing, so each one has to be a listed decision.
src/commands/seam.ts.gotcha: Any subcommand other than lint, and a missing subcommand, both return BAD_ARG with a fixed message that names only lint, so the two cases cannot be told apart from the code.

src/commands/templates.ts.what: The ui templates command. It routes the catalogue subcommand, which writes the template description index, and the lint subcommand, which checks it, and returns BAD_ARG for anything else.
src/commands/templates.ts.why: The catalogue is the only place template frontmatter is read, so the runtime reads one JSON file and never parses templates itself.
src/commands/templates.ts.gotcha: The help text names the --check flag under catalogue, but this dispatcher never looks at flags. The flag is read in the catalogue command, so the help is right only as long as that command keeps its own flag handling.

src/commands/tenant-scaffold.ts.what: The ui tenant-scaffold command. It copies the three bundled Tenant files verbatim into a target folder: the engine script, its stylesheet and a Playwright test. It reads all three sources before writing and refuses to overwrite unless --force is given.
src/commands/tenant-scaffold.ts.why: A consumer gets a working, self-testing drop-in without a browser dependency in the kernel. Copying verbatim means the emitted files are exactly the tested ones.
src/commands/tenant-scaffold.ts.gotcha: The files are written one at a time, and no execute bit is set. A failed write leaves the earlier files on disk, and test-tenant.mjs has to be run with node explicitly.

src/core/audit-detect.ts.what: Finds design-system violations in an exported node tree: raw colours that should use a token, detached instances, raw icons that should be Icon components, off-grid radii and spacing, and instances of deprecated components. Violations are keyed by node name, and each off-grid one comes with a snap-to-grid remap.
src/core/audit-detect.ts.why: Conformance to a design system is a mechanical question once the spec is known, so the judgement is made by this function and not by a model. Names are the key because node ids change on every sync.
src/core/audit-detect.ts.gotcha: A node is flagged as a detached lookalike whenever its name exactly matches a registered component name and it is not an instance, so an unrelated frame that happens to share a component's name is flagged. Only generic default names are exempt.

src/core/brief-copy-language.ts.what: Derives the recommended UI copy language from the script of the raw request: en when no word carries a distinctly Vietnamese letter, vi when at least a quarter of the words do, and mixed otherwise.
src/core/brief-copy-language.ts.why: The copy language decides how the interface text is written, so it is inferred from the request rather than left to a guess. Only letters that are distinctly Vietnamese count, so French or Spanish accents do not trigger it.
src/core/brief-copy-language.ts.gotcha: A single Vietnamese-lettered word in an otherwise English request gives mixed, not en, because the rule checks for any such word before it looks at the share.

src/core/brief-questions-format.ts.what: Turns the questions file into the two runtime formats: an AskUserQuestion payload for Claude, capped at four questions with the recommended option first, and a Markdown gap sheet for a team. It also checks that a questions file has the shape the renderers need.
src/core/brief-questions-format.ts.why: The kernel emits the questions once and each runtime maps them, so the question logic is written once. The option caps are the limits the host tool enforces.
src/core/brief-questions-format.ts.gotcha: The validator does not check that a question's recommended label matches one of its options. Such a question passes, and the Claude payload then has no option tagged Recommended, with no error raised.

src/core/delivery-model.ts.what: A re-export barrel for the delivery model. It exposes the delivery error class, the marketing viewport list, the required gates, the delivery finding and result types, and the validator, all from the delivery modules.
src/core/delivery-model.ts.why: Callers import from one stable path, so the delivery modules can be split or renamed without touching every caller.
src/core/delivery-model.ts.gotcha: The barrel re-exports only the names listed here. A type added to the delivery types module but left out of this list cannot be reached through this path, and nothing reports that.

src/core/designmd-audit-discipline.ts.what: The shipping-discipline audit family. It fails the run when plan references such as Phase 2, OD-3 or finding A appear in any file except the audit files, and it warns when TODO, FIXME, XXX, HACK or template tokens are left in.
src/core/designmd-audit-discipline.ts.why: A design document that cites internal plan phases or left a placeholder is not ready to ship. The check catches both before a client sees them.
src/core/designmd-audit-discipline.ts.gotcha: The leakage pattern matches any Phase followed by a number, so a legitimate product phrase such as Phase 2 launch in a design document fails the audit.

src/core/ds-diff-format.ts.what: Formats a design-system diff for people. It produces a full Markdown report and a shorter pull-request comment, both with the same counts line, a token table, a component list and any dangling references.
src/core/ds-diff-format.ts.why: A reviewer should see what changed in the design system and whether the change is breaking, in the form the team reads, with the version it implies.
src/core/ds-diff-format.ts.gotcha: The token table is built separately in each of the two formatters, so a change to a column in one has to be made in the other too, and nothing checks that they still match.

src/core/extractors/html/css-custom-prop.what: Resolves var() references against the cascade, walking up the element's ancestors and then the root. A cycle, a missing value with no fallback, or a chain deeper than sixteen levels is reported as unresolved instead of guessed.
src/core/extractors/html/css-custom-prop.why: A colour invented from a missing variable describes a page that does not exist. Reporting the unresolved names keeps the extracted design honest.
src/core/extractors/html/css-custom-prop.gotcha: BUG (read, not reproduced): An empty fallback, as in var(--x,), is treated as no fallback at all, so the reference is reported as unresolved. CSS itself treats an empty fallback as a valid empty value.

src/core/figma-comment-anchor.ts.what: Works out what a Figma comment points at. It walks down from the frame to the innermost meaningful node under the pin and returns the ancestor chain with a confidence label: element, region, frame, orphaned or unanchored. Text nodes are named by their on-screen characters.
src/core/figma-comment-anchor.ts.why: Figma gives only a frame and a point, and a confidently wrong element name would send the work to the wrong place. The chain plus a confidence label tells the reader how much to trust it.
src/core/figma-comment-anchor.ts.gotcha: An orphaned frame is reported only when the nodes payload holds at least one node. An empty payload makes every missing frame read as frame instead, so an absent payload can hide a deleted frame.

src/core/figma-comment-thread.ts.what: Folds a raw Figma comments payload into threads.
