A thread is resolved when its root is resolved, replies are attached to their root in time order, and anything that cannot be read or attached is counted rather than dropped. The output is ordered by Figma's own numbering when present.
src/core/figma-comment-thread.ts.why: A reviewer's thread is the unit of work, and resolution belongs to the whole conversation. Counting each unreadable or orphaned item keeps the totals honest, since the count is the contract.
src/core/figma-comment-thread.ts.gotcha: A frame anchor with no node_offset is counted as unreadable, while a reply whose root is absent from the payload is counted as an orphan. A reply with no author is shown as unknown and is not flagged at all.

src/core/figma-conventions-emit.ts.what: Builds CONVENTIONS.md from the usage rollup of real screens: layout, colour binding, spacing and radius scales, typography, component vocabulary, a per-section summary and provenance. With a design-system scale it separates on-scale values from real deviations, and without one it reports the observed house style and says so. It also derives the memory insights from the same numbers.
src/core/figma-conventions-emit.ts.why: The product's actual grammar, with counts, is more useful to a generator than a rulebook nobody measured. Saying when nothing was validated keeps an unchecked house style from passing as a rule.
src/core/figma-conventions-emit.ts.gotcha: The deprecated-component pattern matches the word old anywhere in a component name, so a component called Old price is listed under deprecated components still in use.

src/core/insight-recurrence.ts.what: Groups memory insights by their normalised text and counts how often each one has been recorded, with the up and down votes that go with it. An insight restated in the same words strengthens the existing one.
src/core/insight-recurrence.ts.why: A lesson that keeps coming back is more worth remembering than one seen once. Exact normalised matching means the kernel never decides that two different wordings are the same lesson.
src/core/insight-recurrence.ts.gotcha: A vote missing for an insight counts as an up vote, so a votes array shorter than the insights list quietly adds upvotes to the entries past its end.

src/core/knowledge-effect-catalog-parse..what: Parses and shape-checks the effect catalog ledger, which lists each effect's slug, name and family, and parses the six-column matrix rows out of the knowledge file. The catalog parser returns null on any violation, so a partly valid ledger is never used.
src/core/knowledge-effect-catalog-parse..why: A partial catalog would make the matrix check pass against half the effects. Failing the whole parse keeps the check honest.
src/core/knowledge-effect-catalog-parse..gotcha: The overlayFallback flag is checked to be a boolean but is then left out of the parsed result, so the value is validated and never used. The matrix parser also accepts a slug cell without backticks, which the gradient parser requires, so an ordinary six-cell table row can be read as a matrix row.

src/core/knowledge-index-check.ts.what: Keeps the file table in the knowledge README in step with the knowledge folder. It reports a table row whose file does not exist, and a knowledge file that no row mentions. The table can use globs, placeholders and brace lists.
src/core/knowledge-index-check.ts.why: The README is the only map an agent has of the knowledge core. A file that is missing from the map is never routed to, and a row that points at nothing sends the agent to a dead end.
src/core/knowledge-index-check.ts.gotcha: Any backtick span containing a star counts as a glob, and a broad pattern such as a star with a .md extension in any cell covers every file. Such a cell therefore hides every missing row.

src/core/knowledge-link-check.ts.what: Three link checks over the knowledge markdown: relative links between knowledge files must resolve, provenance markers must name a tracked repo file, and a marker must not point into the machine-local symlink folders, which a clean clone cannot resolve.
src/core/knowledge-link-check.ts.why: A knowledge file that cites a source must cite one that other people can open. The machine-local rule is checked by path prefix, so the check fails on every machine and not only on machines without the symlink.
src/core/knowledge-link-check.ts.gotcha: The link pattern stops at the first closing parenthesis, so a link whose target contains one is skipped silently and is never checked.

src/core/knowledge-persona-check.ts.what: Cross-checks the persona library across its three forms: the lookup table in the persona index, the per-family markdown blocks and the compiled JSON. A persona missing from one form, or filed under different families in different forms, is an error. It also checks the persona count the index states against the table.
src/core/knowledge-persona-check.ts.why: The persona library is read from three places, and when they disagree the generator can pick a persona that a reader of the index never sees. Drift checks catch that before a design uses the wrong one.
src/core/knowledge-persona-check.ts.gotcha: The count check reads only the wordings it has patterns for. An index that states its persona count in some other way is never compared with the table, so the stated number can go stale without a finding.

src/core/ksync-ingest.ts.what: Reads the frame snapshot the host captured from Figma, in either the native frames shape or the per-app ledger shape that a project already keeps. It keeps each frame's modified time and spec hash, and takes the newest app refresh time as the snapshot's age.
src/core/ksync-ingest.ts.why: The kernel never calls Figma, so the snapshot is the only evidence it has. Accepting the ledger shape directly means a real project can be checked without a conversion step.
src/core/ksync-ingest.ts.gotcha: Ledger entries carry no modified time, so with the ledger shape a pin that has no spec hash cannot be checked at all and is reported as uncheckable.

src/core/memory-graph-cache.ts.what: A type guard for the cached memory graph. It accepts a cache only when every consumed field has the shape the rest of the code reads, and any other cache is rebuilt from the events.
src/core/memory-graph-cache.ts.why: A disposable cache with a malformed field would feed bad values into the rankings. Rebuilding on any mismatch keeps the cache from being trusted by accident.
src/core/memory-graph-cache.ts.gotcha: The guard checks the shape of the cache, not its contents. It never compares the source hash with the events, so a cache of the right shape from an older run is accepted as long as its hash field is a string.

src/core/prompt-plan-model.ts.what: A re-export barrel for the prompt-plan validator, its error class, and its finding and result types.
src/core/prompt-plan-model.ts.why: Callers import the plan model from one path, so the validator's modules can be reorganised without touching them.
src/core/prompt-plan-model.ts.gotcha: The file contains only re-exports. Any change to what the validator returns reaches callers through the type exports here, and nothing in this file would show that the two have drifted.

src/core/rendered/runtime-capture.ts.what: The versioned public contract for a rendered-page capture: what the engine saw, for each element, with the browser and viewport it was rendered in. It also defines the check that a capture is one this build can read, and the message that names the version when it is not.
src/core/rendered/runtime-capture.ts.why: A capture from one run can be judged by a later run only if both sides agree on the shape. Stamping the engine into every capture turns a browser difference into a stated condition rather than a silent flake.
src/core/rendered/runtime-capture.ts.gotcha: The support check accepts any value whose type is object for the engine field, and typeof null is also object, so a capture with a null engine passes the check.

src/core/rulings-render.ts.what: Renders a rulings file as Markdown, grouped by category and then by id, in plain code-unit order so the output does not depend on locale. Missing fields are shown as unknown, not hidden. A separate blocker check names the one kind of damage that stops rendering entirely.
src/core/rulings-render.ts.why: A reader should see every ruling, including ones with gaps, so the gaps are visible. The lint step is the gate for bad fields, and the renderer does not second-guess it.
src/core/rulings-render.ts.gotcha: The renderer assumes the document already passed the linter. A null entry in approved_by is not caught by the blocker check and throws a TypeError during rendering instead of being shown as a gap.

src/core/scroll-story-kernel.ts.what: The grid, difference and verdict arithmetic for a scroll-capture: each frame is shrunk to a small grey grid, adjacent frames are compared, and the report gives the longest run of near-identical frames and how much the layout shifts across the sequence. The verdict is FLAT when frames mostly repeat, ACTIVE when the layout moves, and FLAT otherwise.
src/core/scroll-story-kernel.ts.why: A scroll story that never moves is a broken scroll or a paused animation. Using fixed thresholds rather than tuning per dataset keeps the verdict the same from one capture to the next.
src/core/scroll-story-kernel.ts.gotcha: A single frame is always FLAT, because with no pairs there is no change to measure and its layout variance is zero. A one-frame capture reads as a broken scroll even when it was taken correctly.

src/core/tell-rules-labels.ts.what: Rules for repeated label and ornament devices: a rounded icon tile repeated above headings, all-caps kickers repeated, a pill chip above the hero headline, and zero-padded section numbers. Each fires only on repetition, except the chip, which is a single instance.
src/core/tell-rules-labels.ts.why: One kicker is an editorial choice and a kicker above every section is a template, so a habit is flagged and a single use is left alone.
src/core/tell-rules-labels.ts.gotcha: The numbered-label pattern matches only 00 to 09, so sections numbered 10 and above are never flagged. The chip rule accepts any pill-shaped radius anywhere on the page, not only one on the chip, so an unrelated pill button can satisfy it.

src/core/tell-rules-motion.ts.what: Rules for motion and decoration that simulates something: a pulsing dot that loops forever, a fast loop that reads as a blinking caret with no input on the page, a marquee the reader cannot pause, a transform transition over several images, an illustration assembled from textless shapes, and a radial glow behind the headline.
src/core/tell-rules-motion.ts.why: These habits make an interface look alive or deep without anything happening. The marquee rule checks for readable content first, so a decorative sweep over an empty overlay is not flagged.
src/core/tell-rules-motion.ts.gotcha: The image-hover rule counts any transform transition anywhere on the page as an image hover, as long as there are at least three images, so a card lift elsewhere can trigger it.

src/core/tell-rules-type.ts.what: Rules on type: an overused face, a flat size scale with no step above 1.25 times, an oversized h1 with nothing between it and the next size, headings that do not fall in size with their level, tight leading on body copy, wide or extreme negative tracking, over-long body runs, justified text, and tiny interface text.
src/core/tell-rules-type.ts.why: Type carries most of the hierarchy in an interface. These checks catch the common ways a scale stops ranking, and each one states the threshold it judged against.
src/core/tell-rules-type.ts.gotcha: The long-line message always says over 400 characters, but the check reads its limit from the threshold table. If that limit is changed, the message still states the old number.

src/core/tenant-lint-checks.ts.what: The two rule groups behind the Tenant linter. scanJS and scanCSS apply the section-body rules to script and style text: no page-level scroll writes, no fixed positioning, no root-level scrub variables. scanHostAncestors walks the tags for a host ancestor that would kill the sticky pin.
src/core/tenant-lint-checks.ts.why: An embedded motion section must read and write only inside its own box, and these are the writes that break the host page. Each rule is written for the exact pattern it forbids, so a legal local scroll is not flagged.
src/core/tenant-lint-checks.ts.gotcha: BUG (read, not reproduced): The comment stripper removes everything after a double slash that is not preceded by a colon, including a double slash inside a string literal. A violation later on that same line is therefore never scanned.

src/core/vr-support.ts.what: Helpers for the visual-regression command: parsing the mask rectangles and the 0-to-1 threshold flags, turning each gate result into its status line, and deciding which results count as a regression.
src/core/vr-support.ts.why: Keeping these as pure functions lets the gate behaviour be tested without reading any image files.
src/core/vr-support.ts.gotcha: A mask with a zero width or height is accepted, because only negative and non-numeric values are rejected, so it hides nothing and reports no error.

src/commands/guide.ts.what: The ui guide command. It prints the plain-language map of what a designer can ask for, each goal with the /ui:* command to type and a short explanation, plus setup, quality and under-the-hood notes. The same content is emitted as JSON.
src/commands/guide.ts.why: A designer should be able to find the right command without reading the plumbing commands. Keeping the map in one place means the text and the JSON cannot disagree.
src/commands/guide.ts.gotcha: The map makes claims about each platform's assurance level and about what the generator returns, such as three quality-checked variants. Those claims are written by hand here, and no check compares them with the capability catalogue they describe.

src/core/adapter-writer.ts.what: Writes the adapter files for a runtime, either whole files or a sentinel-marked block inside an existing host file. It checks for conflicts before writing, writes in a fixed order, and on any failure restores every file it changed in that call.
src/core/adapter-writer.ts.why: An init that fails halfway should leave the project as it was. Snapshotting every target first makes the rollback exact rather than a best guess.
src/core/adapter-writer.ts.gotcha: BUG (read, not reproduced): The file being written when the error happens is not on the rollback list, because it is added only after a successful write. A partly written file is therefore left with its partial content.

src/core/change-log-rotation.ts.what: Reads the rotation marker that the figma-agent writes when it rotates the change-log. The marker records how many lines existed in the old file at the moment it rotated, so the reconcile step can tell that a saved cursor no longer matches the fresh live file. This module only reads the marker and never writes one.
src/core/change-log-rotation.ts.why: After a rotation the live file starts again at line zero. Without the marker, a saved cursor would either wait forever for lines the new file never reaches, or silently read the new file from the wrong place.
src/core/change-log-rotation.ts.gotcha: A marker that fails validation is treated the same as no marker at all. A corrupt marker written after a real rotation therefore leaves the old cursor in use, and nothing reports that the rotation went unrecognised.

src/core/changelog.ts.what: Folds the design-system changelog and the recorded decisions into one history, grouped as Added, Changed and Decisions, newest first, with each line tagged with its date and its provenance. The Markdown rendering follows the Keep a Changelog layout.
src/core/changelog.ts.why: A reviewer needs one place to see what changed in a design system and who decided it. Folding both sources keeps the token history and the reasons for it side by side.
src/core/changelog.ts.gotcha: BUG (read, not reproduced): A timestamp that is not in the plain date form is kept whole, so it sorts against the plain dates by string comparison and can land in an arbitrary position in the list.

src/core/command-signatures.ts.what: The typed table of every command's positional arguments, flags, enum values and error codes. The schema command and the central flag guard both read it. The file has no logic beyond a lookup that finds the signature for a command and, when there is one, its subcommand.
src/core/command-signatures.ts.why: A host model can form a correct invocation from one table instead of reading help text, and a flag that is not in the table can be rejected in one place for every command.
src/core/command-signatures.ts.gotcha: A dispatcher run with no subcommand, or with an unknown one, gets no signature, so the flag guard does not check its flags. A misspelled flag on such a call is reported only by the subcommand's own parser, if at all.

src/core/component-kit/accordion.ts.what: The accordion component of the owner kit: a stack of disclosure sections built from real buttons with aria-expanded and aria-controls, with one section open and the others collapsed. Hover, focus and disabled headers are drawn statically so every state can be seen at once.
src/core/component-kit/accordion.ts.why: The header buttons and labelled regions give assistive technology the disclosure pattern without extra scripting. The static states make the specimen grid show every interaction without a browser.
src/core/component-kit/accordion.ts.gotcha: The caret rotates through a transform transition with no reduced-motion query. The file header says none is needed, but nothing checks that reasoning, so a later change to a longer rotation would ship without a guard.

src/core/component-kit/alert.ts.what: The inline alert component of the owner kit, in four tones: info, success, warning and danger. Each tone tints its own surface with a colour mix of its status colour into the background, and carries a solid left rail. Polite tones use role status and urgent tones use role alert.
src/core/component-kit/alert.ts.why: Body text stays on the foreground colour so it passes contrast on the light tint, and the role split means urgent messages interrupt while routine ones wait.
src/core/component-kit/alert.ts.gotcha: All four banners are in the static markup with their roles, so a page that embeds the kit as shown has an urgent alert and a polite status region present from the first render.

src/core/component-kit/avatar.ts.what: The avatar component of the owner kit: three sizes of a round user glyph, with the initials shown on the accent tint and an optional photo that falls back to them. The placeholder photo is an inline SVG data URI.
src/core/component-kit/avatar.ts.why: Initials are the fallback that always works, so the avatar never shows an empty circle when a photo is missing or blocked.
src/core/component-kit/avatar.ts.gotcha: The placeholder photo's fills are the named colours steelblue and aliceblue, written inside the data URI. The file's comment calls the fragment token-clean, but the token checks read CSS and attributes and never see colours inside a data URI.

src/core/component-kit/badge.ts.what: The status badge component of the owner kit: a small pill in neutral, success, info, warning or danger. Each tone's text colour comes from a paired foreground token, so every pill is meant to pass contrast by construction.
src/core/component-kit/badge.ts.why: Pairing each status fill with its own foreground token keeps the contrast decision in the design system instead of in each component.
src/core/component-kit/badge.ts.gotcha: The text colours depend on eight foreground tokens with no fallback. A project that does not define one of them gets an unset text colour and no error from the kit or the linters.

src/core/component-kit/breadcrumb.ts.what: The breadcrumb component of the owner kit: a labelled nav with an ordered list of crumbs, a real link for each ancestor, and the current page as a span marked aria-current. Separators are hidden from assistive technology.
src/core/component-kit/breadcrumb.ts.why: Using a real list and a real current-page marker lets screen readers announce the location, while the hidden separators keep the slashes from being read aloud.
src/core/component-kit/breadcrumb.ts.gotcha: Each separator is its own list item, so the list holds about twice as many items as there are crumbs. A tool that counts list items to report the depth of a trail will report the wrong number.

src/core/component-kit/button.ts.what: The action button component of the owner kit, across three tones, three sizes and five states. Each tone and state is drawn statically, and the spinner used for the loading state stops for users who ask for reduced motion.
src/core/component-kit/button.ts.why: Drawing every tone and state in one specimen lets a reviewer see the whole matrix at once, and the reduced-motion guard keeps the loading spinner from moving for people who ask it not to.
src/core/component-kit/button.ts.gotcha: The loading button also carries the disabled attribute, so it leaves the tab order while it saves. aria-busy is the only signal that the action is still running.

src/core/component-kit/card.ts.what: The content card component of the owner kit: a header, a body and footer actions on the card surface tokens, shown flat with a hairline border and raised with the card elevation shadow.
src/core/component-kit/card.ts.why: One surface component with two elevations covers most content blocks without a separate component for each.
src/core/component-kit/card.ts.gotcha: The grid uses columns that are at least 260 pixels wide. On a viewport narrower than that, the single column still keeps its minimum width, so the card runs past the edge of the screen and the page scrolls sideways.

src/core/component-kit/checkbox.ts.what: The checkbox component of the owner kit: a native checkbox tinted to the brand colour, inside a label so the label text is its accessible name. Default, hover, focus, checked and disabled rows are drawn statically.
src/core/component-kit/checkbox.ts.why: A native input keeps keyboard and screen-reader behaviour for free, and the implicit label means the text is the name without a separate id.
src/core/component-kit/checkbox.ts.gotcha: The disabled row lowers the opacity of the whole label, text included, so its text drops below the contrast the other rows keep. The specimen is meant to show a disabled state, and it also makes the disabled text harder to read.

src/core/component-kit/combobox.ts.what: The combobox component of the owner kit: a labelled role combobox input paired with a listbox of options, one of them selected, plus a no-matches state and a disabled field. Three fields are shown side by side in a grid.
src/core/component-kit/combobox.ts.why: The combobox pattern tells assistive technology which option is active and how many are shown, and the specimen shows its states together so a reviewer can compare them.
src/core/component-kit/combobox.ts.gotcha: The empty state puts a paragraph inside a role listbox. A listbox is meant to contain options, so the no-matches text is not exposed as an option or as a status message. The grid also uses columns at least 240 pixels wide and runs past a narrow screen.

src/core/component-kit/dialog.ts.what: The modal dialog component of the owner kit, shown open over a dimmed scrim. It has a title, a body, a close button named with aria-label, and cancel and confirm actions, and it is marked role dialog with aria-modal true.
src/core/component-kit/dialog.ts.why: The labelled, described dialog gives screen readers the title and the consequence, and the scrim and overlay elevation make the modal read as blocking.
src/core/component-kit/dialog.ts.gotcha: The specimen is static, so nothing traps focus or closes on Escape, yet the markup says aria-modal true. A page that embeds it as shown tells assistive technology it is modal while the keyboard can still leave it.

src/core/component-kit/dropdown-menu.ts.what: The dropdown menu component of the owner kit: a button that opens a role menu of menu items, with a separator before the destructive action and one item marked aria-disabled. The trigger names the menu through aria-labelledby.
src/core/component-kit/dropdown-menu.ts.why: The menu roles let a screen reader announce the menu and its item count, and the separator keeps the destructive action apart from the rest.
src/core/component-kit/dropdown-menu.ts.gotcha: Every menu item has tabindex -1, so none of them can be reached with the Tab key. The roving pattern needs one item at tabindex 0, and this markup leaves that to the script, which is not included.

src/core/component-kit/field.ts.what: The form row that wraps a label, a control and a help or error line. It shows default, invalid and disabled rows, and the invalid row ties its error text to the control with aria-describedby.
src/core/component-kit/field.ts.why: One wrapper gives every form control the same label, hint and error placement, so the form reads consistently.
src/core/component-kit/field.ts.gotcha: The required marker is the visible word Required in the label text, and the control has no required attribute. A screen reader hears the word, but the form does not treat the field as required.

src/core/component-kit/input.ts.what: The single-line text input component of the owner kit, in default, hover, focus, invalid and disabled states, each with a visible label and a help line.
src/core/component-kit/input.ts.why: Every field has a real label for, so the name is always available to assistive technology and clicking the label focuses the field.
src/core/component-kit/input.ts.gotcha: Only the invalid field ties its help text to the control with aria-describedby. The help lines under the other fields are not associated with their inputs, so a screen reader does not read them when the field is focused.

src/core/component-kit/kbd.ts.what: Keyboard key hints in the kit: single keys and multi-key combos, each on a keycap surface drawn with a hairline border and a small radius.
src/core/component-kit/kbd.ts.why: A real kbd element tells a reader that the text is a key, and keeping the keycap style in the kit makes shortcut hints look the same everywhere.
src/core/component-kit/kbd.ts.gotcha: The modifier glyphs in the combos are the macOS symbols, so the specimen shows the Mac form for every platform, and a Windows reader sees symbols that do not match their keyboard.

src/core/component-kit/pagination.ts.what: The page navigator component of the owner kit: a labelled nav with a list of numbered page links, the current page marked aria-current, an ellipsis for the gap, and Previous and Next links. The first page's Previous link is shown disabled.
src/core/component-kit/pagination.ts.why: A labelled nav with aria-current lets a screen reader say where the reader is in the set, and the ellipsis keeps a long set compact.
src/core/component-kit/pagination.ts.gotcha: The disabled Previous is an anchor with an href and aria-disabled. aria-disabled does not stop an anchor from being followed, so the link still navigates and only its appearance says it is off.

src/core/component-kit/popover.ts.what: A non-modal popover in the owner kit: a trigger button that opens a role dialog panel with a title, a short body and two actions, drawn with a small arrow and card elevation. The panel has no scrim and does not trap focus.
src/core/component-kit/popover.ts.why: A popover fits a quick action or a share prompt without blocking the page, which is why it is kept separate from the modal dialog.
src/core/component-kit/popover.ts.gotcha: The panel has no close control inside it, so in this markup the trigger is the only way to dismiss it. A keyboard user has no close action in the panel itself.

src/core/component-kit/progress.ts.what: The progress bar component of the owner kit, shown as three rows: two with a known value and one indeterminate. Each track is a progressbar role. The indeterminate sweep moves only by transform and becomes a static full bar for users who ask for reduced motion.
src/core/component-kit/progress.ts.why: Omitting aria-valuenow on the indeterminate bar is the correct signal that the amount is unknown, and the reduced-motion fallback keeps the sweep from moving for people who ask it not to.
src/core/component-kit/progress.ts.gotcha: Each determinate fill has a fixed width class, 30 percent or 72 percent, so changing aria-valuenow would not move the bar. The markup and the visible bar can disagree once the value changes.

src/core/component-kit/radio.ts.what: The radio group component of the owner kit: native radios sharing one name inside a fieldset with a legend, showing default, hover, focus, checked and disabled rows.
src/core/component-kit/radio.ts.why: A fieldset with a legend gives the group its name, and native radios with one shared name give the arrow-key behaviour a screen reader user expects.
src/core/component-kit/radio.ts.gotcha: The hover and focus demo rows are real radios in the same group, so clicking one in the specimen changes which option is checked for the whole group.

src/core/component-kit/select.ts.what: The select component of the owner kit: a native select restyled with the kit's tokens and a CSS chevron, shown in default, hover, focus, empty and disabled states. The empty state is a placeholder option that reads as muted.
src/core/component-kit/select.ts.why: A native select keeps the platform's picker and keyboard handling while the token styling keeps it in the design system.
src/core/component-kit/select.ts.gotcha: The empty state uses a disabled placeholder option, so once a user picks a plan they cannot return the field to that state. The empty state is a starting point only.

src/core/component-kit/separator.ts.what: Hairline separators in the kit, horizontal and vertical. Each rule carries role separator and an explicit aria-orientation, so assistive technology reads it as a boundary.
src/core/component-kit/separator.ts.why: A separator marks where one group ends and the next begins, and naming its orientation tells a screen reader which way the boundary runs.
src/core/component-kit/separator.ts.gotcha: The vertical rules sit between spans in a flex row, so their width is inside the row's gap. Changing the gap also moves the space on each side of the rule.

src/core/component-kit/skeleton.ts.what: The loading placeholder of the kit: line, circle and block shapes on the muted surface that pulse by opacity only, with a reduced-motion guard that stops the pulse. The whole placeholder is hidden from assistive technology.
src/core/component-kit/skeleton.ts.why: A skeleton shows the shape of content before it arrives, and an opacity-only pulse avoids layout movement while it runs.
src/core/component-kit/skeleton.ts.gotcha: The skeleton is aria-hidden and has no text or live region, so a screen reader user gets no announcement that content is loading. The loading state exists only for sighted users.

src/core/component-kit/switch.ts.what: The toggle switch component of the owner kit: a visually hidden checkbox with an aria-hidden track and thumb, and the label text as its accessible name. Default, hover, focus, checked and disabled rows are drawn statically.
src/core/component-kit/switch.ts.why: A real checkbox keeps the on and off state for assistive technology and for forms, while the track and thumb carry only the visual.
src/core/component-kit/switch.ts.gotcha: The focus ring is drawn only on the is-focus demo class. No rule draws one from the hidden checkbox when it receives keyboard focus, so a keyboard user sees no focus indicator on a real switch.

src/core/component-kit/table.ts.what: The data table component of the owner kit: a semantic table with a caption, a header, zebra rows and a hovered row. Below 40rem each row reflows into a bordered card with its header text shown from a data-th attribute. A second table shows the static empty state.
src/core/component-kit/table.ts.why: Stacking the rows on a phone avoids a sideways scroll or cut-off columns, and the hidden header keeps the column names for screen readers.
src/core/component-kit/table.ts.gotcha: On a narrow screen a cell without a data-th attribute shows no label. Every data cell has to repeat its column name by hand, and the markup does not check that it does.

src/core/component-kit/tabs.ts.what: The tabs component of the owner kit: a tablist of role tab buttons with aria-selected on the active tab, a roving tabindex, one disabled tab, and a linked tab panel, shown with default, hover, focus and disabled tabs.
src/core/component-kit/tabs.ts.why: The tablist and selected-tab roles tell a screen reader which view is active, and the roving tabindex lets the arrow keys move between tabs.
src/core/component-kit/tabs.ts.gotcha: All five tabs point aria-controls at the same panel, and that panel is labelled by the Overview tab. A screen reader user on the Reports tab hears a panel named Overview.

src/core/component-kit/textarea.ts.what: The multi-line text field of the kit, in default, hover, focus, invalid and disabled states, each with a visible label and a help line. The invalid field ties its error text to the control with aria-describedby.
src/core/component-kit/textarea.ts.why: A labelled textarea with a described error gives the same accessible name and error association as the single-line input, so the two fields behave alike.
src/core/component-kit/textarea.ts.gotcha: The minimum height uses the spacing token space.16, so a change to the spacing scale also changes the height of every text area in the kit.

src/core/component-kit/toast.ts.what: The toast notification component of the owner kit: a stack of neutral, success and danger toasts on the popover surface with overlay elevation, each with a title, a message and a dismiss button. Neutral and success use role status and danger uses role alert.
src/core/component-kit/toast.ts.why: The polite and urgent role split matches the tone, so a failed upload interrupts while a saved draft does not.
src/core/component-kit/toast.ts.gotcha: All three dismiss buttons have the same accessible name, Dismiss notification, so a screen reader user moving through the stack hears three identical controls and cannot tell which notification each one closes.

src/core/component-kit/tooltip.ts.what: The tooltip component of the owner kit: a text button whose description comes from a role tooltip bubble with card elevation and a small arrow. The bubble is drawn open in the specimen.
src/core/component-kit/tooltip.ts.why: aria-describedby gives the hint to a screen reader on focus, and the bubble gives a sighted user the same hint on hover.
src/core/component-kit/tooltip.ts.gotcha: The bubble is always rendered in this markup, so the hint shows on the page permanently, not only on hover or focus. The bubble also uses nowrap, so on a narrow screen it runs past the edge.

src/core/coverage-check.ts.what: Checks how many of a brief's acceptance criteria a produced design covers. Each criterion is covered when a screen names it, and it counts as evidenced only when it cites a source. The result gives the coverage percentage, the uncovered and unsourced criteria, and any screen that names a criterion the brief does not have.
src/core/coverage-check.ts.why: A brief can list requirements that nobody sourced, and a design can claim to meet them. Separating covered from evidenced keeps an assumption from passing as a real requirement.
src/core/coverage-check.ts.gotcha: A spec with no acceptance criteria reports 100 percent coverage, so an empty spec passes any coverage floor.

src/core/designmd-html-snapshot.ts.what: Turns a fetched page into a single self-contained preview file. It inlines the page's stylesheets, strips scripts and preload hints, removes the inline opacity and transform values that scroll-reveal libraries leave on hidden content, and makes root-relative links absolute against the source origin.
src/core/designmd-html-snapshot.ts.why: A preview has to open offline, and without its scripts a scroll-reveal page would stay invisible. Removing only the hiding values lets the rest of the page render as it was.
src/core/designmd-html-snapshot.ts.gotcha: Any inline transform that mentions translate, scale or perspective is removed, including a layout transform the page depends on. The rule does not check whether the value is a reveal offset.

src/core/ds-preview-chrome.ts.what: The stylesheet for the specimen page itself: the page layout, the swatch grid, the type ramp, the radius, elevation and motion chips, and the component frames. A reduced-motion block stops every animation and transition on the page.
src/core/ds-preview-chrome.ts.why: The specimen page is built from the design system's own tokens, so it shows the system working on a real page.
src/core/ds-preview-chrome.ts.gotcha: The header says every value resolves through a token, but the code samples use a literal monospace font stack instead of a token. Those samples are the one part of the page that is not built from the system.

src/core/extractors/html/css-shorthands..what: Expands the box shorthands that the tells depend on, padding, margin, border width and gap, into their one-sided parts, so the spacing rules see a value for each side. Background, font and transition are left alone, because their grammar is too loose to expand safely.
src/core/extractors/html/css-shorthands..why: Most real stylesheets write padding as a shorthand, so without this step the spacing rules would see nothing and report a clean page.
src/core/extractors/html/css-shorthands..gotcha: expandBox takes a parts argument that every caller passes as an empty array, so the function always splits the string itself and the argument does nothing.

src/core/extractors/web/tailwind-resolve.what: Maps a Tailwind class to the design value it sets, such as a padding amount, a radius, a font size, a weight or a colour. Anything it does not know is left unresolved, so no value is invented.
src/core/extractors/web/tailwind-resolve.why: Utility classes are plain data, so the design can be read without running the project's build. Unknown classes are counted, not guessed.
src/core/extractors/web/tailwind-resolve.gotcha: State and breakpoint prefixes such as md: and hover: are stripped before matching, so md:p-8 is read as p-8 at every width. The breakpoint and state conditions are lost.

src/core/html-img-fallback-script.ts.what: The inline script added to a page by the image autofix rule. When an image fails to load, it first asks picsum.photos for a placeholder seeded from the image's alt text or nearby heading, and if that fails it shows a grey SVG.
src/core/html-img-fallback-script.ts.why: A broken image leaves a gap in a delivered page. A placeholder keeps the layout intact, and the fallback chain always ends in a local SVG.
src/core/html-img-fallback-script.ts.gotcha: The first fallback step sends a request to picsum.photos with a seed taken from the alt text or nearby heading. Page copy therefore leaves the page to an outside host, even though the file's header describes the script as dependency-free.

src/core/inline-ignores.ts.what: Finds the in-file waivers written as design-os-disable comments. A waiver can cover the whole file, one line, or the next line, and must name a reason. A waiver with no reason is reported as malformed rather than honoured.
src/core/inline-ignores.ts.why: A waiver that travels with the source is visible to the next reader, and a required reason stops suppression from becoming a habit. The count of waived findings is kept so the total stays visible.
src/core/inline-ignores.ts.gotcha: A whole-file waiver is found in the same scan as the line waivers and covers every finding of its rule. One disable comment at the bottom of a file silences that rule for the whole file, wherever the finding sits.

src/core/knowledge-effect-matrix-emit.ts.what: Emits the machine columns of the effect matrix from the effect ledger: the provenance marker, the header, and one row per effect with its name, slug and family. The narrative, anti-use and fallback cells are left empty for a person to write.
src/core/knowledge-effect-matrix-emit.ts.why: The emitter must not invent the anti-use text or the fallback claim, because those fields are where a wrong use is refused. An empty cell fails the linter until someone writes it.
src/core/knowledge-effect-matrix-emit.ts.gotcha: The parser checks that overlayFallback is a boolean, but the matrix does not carry it, so the fallback flag never reaches the table that a writer fills in.

src/core/knowledge-scrub.ts.what: Removes identifying details from text before it leaves a project: emails, URLs, Figma file keys, absolute paths, IP addresses and hostnames, plus any project or person names the caller supplies, which are replaced with placeholders. Each replacement is counted by kind.
src/core/knowledge-scrub.ts.why: Promotion candidates are written for a shared library, and the library must not expose a client's name, an internal host or a file path.
src/core/knowledge-scrub.ts.gotcha: Supplied names shorter than two characters are dropped without a message, so a project named with one letter is never scrubbed from the text.

src/core/knowledge-web-technique-parse.t.what: Parses the catalogue of web techniques and checks that each technique card has the nine required headings with non-empty content. It also lists the technique ids that a document defines.
src/core/knowledge-web-technique-parse.t.why: Each technique is a card that a builder reads before using it, so every card must state its purpose, its fallback and how it fails. The headings are checked so a card cannot skip them.
src/core/knowledge-web-technique-parse.t.gotcha: Each technique must have exactly the listed keys. A catalogue with one technique that carries an extra field is rejected as a whole, so one bad entry blocks every other technique from loading.

src/core/outcome-registry.ts.what: The list of commands that record an outcome in the memory ledger as a side effect of running, each with its file, its event type and a prose note on when it records. A test checks that each listed file calls the recording helper and that no other command file does.
src/core/outcome-registry.ts.why: Recording has to be deliberate. A single list stops a command from quietly writing to the ledger, and the test keeps the list and the call sites in step.
src/core/outcome-registry.ts.gotcha: The condition column is prose, and nothing executes or compares it. It can drift from the guard at the call site, and only a reviewer reading both would notice.

src/core/persona-lint-thin-family.ts.what: Flags persona families that are thin: fewer screens per app than the floor, or fewer than three apps. A thin family passes only when one of its own history notes says it is thin or provisional, so the gap is recorded as a decision.
src/core/persona-lint-thin-family.ts.why: A family built from few apps looks as settled as one built from many. Requiring a recorded note makes the thin family an explicit choice rather than a silent one.
src/core/persona-lint-thin-family.ts.gotcha: The excuse is any note that contains the word thin or provisional, so a note that says a family is not thin still counts as an excuse, and the wording of a note can excuse a gap by accident.

src/core/rulings-labels.ts.what: The fixed table of headings and field labels for rendered rulings, in English and Vietnamese. Only these strings are translated; ruling text, ids and sources pass through in their original language.
src/core/rulings-labels.ts.why: Keeping the translated strings in one table means a reader sees the same structure in both languages, and the source text is never altered.
src/core/rulings-labels.ts.gotcha: The table is typed so that each language must supply every label. A partial translation fails the type check instead of falling back to English, so a new language cannot ship half-labelled.

src/core/scrub-encode-floor.ts.what: The single set of numbers for the scroll-video encode floor: the constant rate factor, the group-of-pictures length for desktop and phone clips, the sharpening, the phone width, the poster width and quality. The build script and the linter both read their values from here.
src/core/scrub-encode-floor.ts.why: The floor was once copied into two places and drifted apart. Keeping one definition means changing a number changes what the encoder makes and what the linter accepts.
src/core/scrub-encode-floor.ts.gotcha: The linter reads only the maximum group-of-pictures length. Changing the emitted target alone does not change what the linter accepts, and the two numbers are tied together only by a comment and by the emitter's test.

src/core/scrub-lint.ts.what: Checks an encoded video against the scroll floor by walking the file's box tree, with no decoding. It reports a file whose moov box comes after mdat, an audio track, a missing video track, and too many frames between keyframes.
src/core/scrub-lint.ts.why: These are container facts, so they can be checked from the bytes alone. A clip that fails them seeks badly on a phone, and the linter catches that before the clip is published.
src/core/scrub-lint.ts.gotcha: A file the box walk cannot read, such as a file that is not ISO-BMFF or is truncated before moov, returns no findings at all. The lint passes it silently, and only the command layer reports the read problem.

src/core/stream-parse.ts.what: Two helpers for model output: one removes the code-fence wrappers and any prose around a full HTML document, and the other pulls complete JSON objects out of a concatenated stream.
src/core/stream-parse.ts.why: Model output often arrives wrapped in fences or with a sentence on either side, and a stream may hold several objects in a row. Both helpers recover the content without guessing at fragments.
src/core/stream-parse.ts.gotcha: BUG (read, not reproduced): The JSON scanner counts every brace, including braces inside string values, so a string that contains a closing brace ends the object early. The span then fails to parse, and the scanner skips to the next brace, which can lose the object entirely.

src/core/stylesheet-host-scope.ts.what: Decides whether a stylesheet the linter could not read is a known webfont sheet or an unknown one. A font sheet can only hide font names, so the caveat for it is narrower, and any other sheet keeps the strict caveat. The decision is made from the host name.
src/core/stylesheet-host-scope.ts.why: The strict caveat fired on most pages and was ignored, so it was narrowed to the sheets that can really hide layout, colour or shadow.
src/core/stylesheet-host-scope.ts.gotcha: Font hosts are trusted by name alone, so a font sheet that also carries layout rules is treated as harmless. The file names this as a known blind spot and does not inspect the contents of the sheet.

src/core/template-catalogue-parse.ts.what: Reads the one-line description from a template's frontmatter. It is the only parser of template frontmatter; the runtime reads the catalogue JSON that it helps build.
src/core/template-catalogue-parse.ts.why: The parser is kept narrow, so the same template always yields the same description and the catalogue stays byte-stable.
src/core/template-catalogue-parse.ts.gotcha: Only a single-line description is read. A description written as a folded or literal block, with a greater-than or pipe sign, comes back as that sign alone, or as null, so the catalogue entry is wrong.

src/core/trace-summarize.ts.what: Summarises an agent's read trace: how much context was loaded before the first write, which orientation files were opened, whether the design-checking skill was loaded and whether its checklist actually ran, and how many gate runs happened. The loaded and the ran facts are kept as separate fields on purpose.
src/core/trace-summarize.ts.why: Loading a checklist is not the same as running it, and the summary keeps the two apart so a reviewer can tell which one happened.
src/core/trace-summarize.ts.gotcha: When a session filter is given, every record without a session field is dropped. A trace written by a host that does not record sessions therefore summarises to nothing under the filter.
